texto: I was so excited to see this on opening night. I am the target audience for "Ralph Fiennes in the Vatican." I hated it. The movie looked good, but who gets credit for that? I should think sets and costumes take care of themselves, and your job is merely not to mess it up (which they don’t). Beyond that, there was nothing. The plot generated no suspense whatsoever, and by the end I could not have cared less who became the pope. They could have elected an elephant and I’d barely have looked up from my watch. The movie's version of Catholic politics was a facile caricature. Conflating it with the left-right divide in America is obvious and stupid as well as inaccurate. Having said that, you at least have to hand it to them that they gave the devil his due. Sergio Castellitto as the conservative cardinal Tedesco was the only performance that actually leapt off the screen and made me feel anything. Everyone else was practically comatose. For twisty, silly, sexy, Malkovichy Vatican shenanigans, The Young Pope and The New Pope still take the palm.

I was enjoying it at first, then noticed that some of the views being discussed in the film were leaning more left and what some Catholics would originally stand for. texto: После смерти Папы Римского кардиналы собираются для выбора нового главы католической церкви. Процесс превращается в настоящую борьбу, ведь у каждого кандидата оказывается свой скелет в шкафу. Зрителя погружают в атмосферу мрачных коридоров Ватикана. Звукорежиссёр позволяет услышать шаги, шёпот и даже дыхание героев, что одновременно создаёт напряжение и интимную обстановку для обсуждения вопросов веры. Сохранение традиции или реформа религиозных институтов? Глава церкви - менеджер или пастырь? Может ли он сомневаться? Какие человеческие слабости нельзя в нём принять? Все эти вопросы практически не поднимаются в "Конклаве". Триллер здесь тоже сложно найти. Главный герой узнает тайну одного из кандидатов, делает её публичной, баланс сил на голосовании меняется - и так несколько раз. Тогда зачем это всё нужно? Ответ разочаровывающе банален: фильм является реакцией на выборы в странах Запада. Да, это очередное обсуждение "правых популистов", "левых либералов" и прочих словосочетаний, не вызывающих уже ничего, кроме скуки. Хорошо, фильм хочет говорить про политику, а не про религию. Будет ли здесь показан интересный конфликт идей? Нет. В самом начале зрителю чётко говорят: "Вот правые, они очень плохие. Вот левые, они хорошие, но им чего-то не хватает для победы". Ни аргументов, ни дискуссии здесь не будет. То есть, чтобы сопереживать местной драме, нужно заранее находиться в определённой части политического спектра. Финал фильма, когда зритель узнает, кто и в какой обстановке победил Главного Буржуина, может вызвать только нервный смешок.

texto: Conclave feels like a story about the difference between faith and certainty. It takes place inside one of the most powerful religious institutions in the world, but the film is less interested in religion itself than in what happens when human beings convince themselves they understand something greater than them. What makes the film resonate is how every cardinal carries his own idea of truth. They speak about God, tradition, and morality, but underneath those beliefs are ambition, fear, ego, and insecurity. The conclave becomes a reminder that even the most sacred institutions are still operated by imperfect people. Lawrence is what gives the story its emotional weight. His crisis of faith isn't portrayed as weakness. If anything, his doubt makes him one of the few people capable of genuine reflection. The film quietly suggests that certainty can be more dangerous than disbelief because certainty leaves no room for humility. What lingers is the idea that faith might require doubt. To believe while acknowledging you could be wrong is completely different from using belief as proof of your own righteousness. The characters most convinced of their moral purity often seem the least capable of questioning themselves. The final revelation reinforces everything the film has been asking. Humanity constantly tries to create categories, rules, and structures to make existence easier to understand. But life has never been obligated to fit neatly inside them. Conclave stays with me because it suggests that maybe the opposite of faith isn't doubt. Maybe it's certainty. The moment you believe you have all the answers is often the moment you stop searching for truth.

texto: Oh, I’m honestly in shock. This film is absolutely fascinating, and I’d recommend it regardless of what you believe. The acting is simply phenomenal, and the score works in such perfect synergy with the visuals. It knows exactly when to emphasize a moment, create tension, or leave you with a sense of mystery. The story itself feels like a small detective mystery intertwined with political intrigue, tangled destinies, and genuine character development. I was particularly impressed by how the characters evolve throughout the film, how their perspectives and perceptions change, and how we’re gradually presented with new details that reshape our understanding of the people we thought we knew. I also loved getting a glimpse into the inner workings of a Vatican conclave: how a pope is elected, the traditions, and all the behind-the-scenes politics. It’s fascinating in its own right. Throughout the film, I found myself repeatedly admiring what I was watching. At one point, I genuinely thought, This is a 9/10. And then... the final twist happened. I won’t spoil it, but my jaw was on the floor. I was completely blindsided. I genuinely have no words. I don’t even know how to feel about this film anymore. It doesn’t erase everything the movie accomplished before that, but the ending clashes deeply with my personal beliefs. My personal take: if you cut the last 15 minutes, this would have been perfect.

texto: Every big Hollywood film dealing with problems of the marginalized is almost always about the success of a small business owner. The starting of Dallas Buyers Club is about a man getting treated as if he's a homosexual while he wastes away, and all the problems that come with it. This regressive hick dealing with the new reality that he has been forced into. Very nice. The middle third is about him being a small business owner and his run ins with the government. And ofc making fat stacks off of sick gays. That's his calling in life. That's where he finds real success. Matthew Maccounaghey is The Wolf of AIDS street. The end tries to reel it in and ground him as a person who has experienced real growth, how the experience has changed him, has made him a more compassionate man despite the hardships he's facing. But it's too little, too late. By the point it tries to reel it in, the film is no longer about the illness or the social atmosphere or even the protagonist's struggle with the illness. An aside, Known pedophile Jared Leto as a transvestite/transgender was an interesting choice.

texto: for a film which mathew mccoughney seemed to have fully locked in, DBC offers very less for a biopic of an actual man. it’s the raging homophobia - that’s slowly turned into sympathy since the community is suddenly profitable - to the enlightenment that only comes post a sacrifice of a close one (on whom the onus laid unsaid yet heavily to somehow transform a pretty aggressive character’s arc) i am not sure if this trajectory is something that woodrof deserved. or for that matter, even mccoughney who very clearly gave it his all deserved either. i also could understand why would misgendering of a transwoman probably exist in the 80s, but for a film that was made in 2013, rayon could have been played by anyone but a cis-het and rather offensive jared leto. in totality of it, i kept wanting to see the queer characters also trying to live their lives, instead of them just being miserable folks who just gather some money in order to score some drugs so they can live another day while a proudly straight protagonist makes an empire out of it. in fact, i kept waiting to see homosexuality roaring unashamed unafraid in the face of woodrof, like sure, think whatever you hold against us that’s totally your personal problem, gurl. but no, that power was never given into the hands of the characters opressed. all you get to feel towards them is sadness. as if the film never cared much for them, it’s as if they remained largely invisible, and suddenly AIDS is huge because a straight guy got it. and that’s just, sad .

texto: I watched this movie without big expectations, but I was surprised by its unexpected plot. I initially thought it would be a Western-themed queer movie, but the main character wasn’t queer. Instead, after contracting AIDS from drug use, he reflects on his life and works to help others in similar situations while building a new path for himself. Since I prefer movies with dramatic elements and strong emotional delivery, this movie wasn’t quite to my taste. The way it sustained tension for a long time to show inner changes, along with its realistic and documentary-like style, felt slow and dull to me. Nevertheless, the fact that it is based on a true story made its direct delivery of messages impressive. It’s a film that captures the life of a resilient person who truly lived such a remarkable life.

texto: I'm about to be pretentious/the friend that is too woke, so apologies in advance. I was hoping for more nuanced characters. While the AIDS crisis affected straight people too, the choice to make the protagonist a homphobic macho man while most lgbt characters are treated as set dressing is odd. The only attempt at an actual openly lgbt character (as in, one who is given a personality) is Rayon, the trans woman played by Jared Leto and I believe the movie shows some implicit judgement towards her. McConaughey's character gets clean almost immediatly and becomes very proactive in trying to maintain his health. Rayon keeps engaging in harmful habits which make her appear more at fault for her own tragic death. Practically from the moment you see her she seems doomed, you know her choices and lifestyle are leading to her demise. And given this is a film about AIDS with a straight protagonist, that juxtaposition feels weirdly like victim blaming. "They had it coming but here's a film about the disease affecting normal everyday heterosexual people you can actually empathisize with and who try to do something about it instead of laying around being tragic" I know this has some basis on real people and I don't mean to say we can't focus on atypical protagonists for these types of stories, but the very sparse (or straight up absent) portrayal of the queer community's coordinated actions to handle the crisis and the focus instead on a straight man's individual efforts felt off and distracted me throughout the movie.

texto: It seems when most people review this film they really only focus on McConaughey’s performance, and rightfully so, because that’s really the only part worth watching for. From a film standpoint this is just about as formulaic and boring as it gets. Literally no emotion throughout the entire film, with bland direction that offers no flair or anything new visually. Should have known this wouldn’t be good since its directed by the same guy as Demolition. Matthew McConaughey is legendary like usual, but I could name at least 5 roles where he performed better, and Interstellar isn’t even one of them. Jared Leto is awful as usual, with a questionably controversial performance and completely unlikeable character. I said ew out loud like 20 times. Overall its just lifeless Oscar bait and I’m afraid many of you have fell for it.

tema: Representação e retrato da comunidade LGBTQ+
exemplo: Há críticas à falta de representação da comunidade LGBTQ+, especialmente à falta de um ator trans no papel de Rayon, e à forma como a personagem trans é retratada de maneira reducionista e que reforça estereótipos negativos.
texto: I'm about to be pretentious/the friend that is too woke, so apologies in advance. I was hoping for more nuanced characters. While the AIDS crisis affected straight people too, the choice to make the protagonist a homphobic macho man while most lgbt characters are treated as set dressing is odd. The only attempt at an actual openly lgbt character (as in, one who is given a personality) is Rayon, the trans woman played by Jared Leto and I believe the movie shows some implicit judgement towards her. McConaughey's character gets clean almost immediatly and becomes very proactive in trying to maintain his health. Rayon keeps engaging in harmful habits which make her appear more at fault for her own tragic death. Practically from the moment you see her she seems doomed, you know her choices and lifestyle are leading to her demise. And given this is a film about AIDS with a straight protagonist, that juxtaposition feels weirdly like victim blaming. "They had it coming but here's a film about the disease affecting normal everyday heterosexual people you can actually empathisize with and who try to do something about it instead of laying around being tragic" I know this has some basis on real people and I don't mean to say we can't focus on atypical protagonists for these types of stories, but the very sparse (or straight up absent) portrayal of the queer community's coordinated actions to handle the crisis and the focus instead on a straight man's individual efforts felt off and distracted me throughout the movie.

tema: Falso retrato da realidade e falta de veracidade
exemplo: Reviews apontam que a história é distorcida, com personagens que não existem na realidade e uma abordagem que simplifica a complexidade da crise do AIDS, gerando retratos falsos e prejudiciais.
texto: "[Woodroof] and other characters denounce [AZT] as 'toxic,' and Woodroof recommends that customers of the buyers club dispose of what AZT they have and never take it again.... One could be forgiven for coming away [from the movie] with the sense that the medical community was poisoning HIV/AIDS patients with the drug, and keeping them from other, safer, therapies. The trouble is that AZT is actually a very effective therapy against HIV/AIDS. 'People who were consistently using AZT prolonged life for one year,' says Jonathan Engel, a medical historian at Baruch College and author of 'The Epidemic: A History of AIDS.' That may not sound like a lot, but at a time when the disease had a mortality rate of 100 percent, anything that delayed death was valuable.'" 'The stuff he was importing from Mexico was almost all useless,' Engel says. A case in point is the experimental drug Peptide T. '[Woodruff] did become a proponent of Peptide T, and he used it himself, and believed it himself,' [cofounder of the Treatment Action Group Peter] Staley says. 'It never panned out. It's a useless therapy, and it never got approved, and nobody uses it today, but the film implies that it helped him.'" Another drug that Woodroof sold, "Compound Q," was actively dangerous: "Compound Q...backfired, with at least two deaths linked to it over the course of two trials (one FDA-approved, one run "guerrilla-style" by the activist Martin Delaney). 'When it became apparent that it could kill people, the FDA tried to get buyers clubs to pull it, and everyone did pull it, except Ron Woodroof,' Staley recalls." - The Washington Post, 2013 Great movie, great acting, a terrible historical biopic that spreads dangerous lies about the AIDS crisis.

texto: The Dallas Buyers Club that is not about the Dallas Buyers Club at all. This isn't an entirely bad movie, but to me it wasn't all that great either. I'm very conflicted when it comes to this film. It does have some high notes: the acting performances and the chemistry displayed from Matthew McConaughey and Jared Leto was great, it is a heartbreaking narrative, and contained solid cinematography. However, there are some very low points for me about this film I experienced both throughout and after the film. For example, while a true story, the script seems so artificial to me. It had no real flow, and just felt like a compilation of randomness piled onto each other for two hours. I know what the movie is about, yet I was asking myself multiple times while watching: what is this movie really even about? 2 hours felt like 4 for this movie. I'd wish we spend more time on Ron Woodroff's character before the diagnosis as well, instead of straight....BOOM....AIDS. The exposition seemed so rushed for the film. After finishing the film as well, I did research and realized that Jared Leto's character didn't even exist in real life, so it makes me question the meaning of the character in the first place... To push a narrative? To exaggerate what the lesson of the movie is supposed to be? It doesn't make sense to me. Also, according to Ron Woodroof’s primary care physician, Dr. Steven Pounders, Woodroof's ex-wife Brenda stated that he was bisexual. This is a massive contradiction than what we saw on the screen. Overall, this movie didn't do it for me. 4/10

texto: Easily one of the best performances of the 21st century from McConaughey, and the people who say Jared Leto can’t act must not have seen this. Dallas Buyers Club is an incredibly heartbreaking story, but also a deeply inspiring one. I do find the movie a tad too long, with a great deal of scenes that feel unnecessary, but at least we get to see more McConaughey in the role of Ron Woodroof. The whole business and finance side of the story was a bit underexplained too, with only the basics being covered. This movie isn’t entirely true to life either, as the real Ron wasn’t homophobic, nor was he a cowboy, and a couple of other characters were entirely fictional to give the movie more depth, which isn’t necessarily a bad thing, and it for sure makes the movie better overall. McConaughey’s acting is all of the juice. Must-watch, no question.

texto: o substituto é um filme que me interessa muito mais pela ferida que existe por trás de sua própria forma do que pela maneira como ele tenta falar sobre educação. porque tony kaye faz um filme sobre um professor substituto que entra numa escola pública em crise, mas filma esse ambiente como se estivesse entrando num lugar onde todas as pessoas já chegaram emocionalmente depois do fim do mundo. não existe propriamente a promessa de transformação pedagógica. existe exaustão. adrian brody é perfeito pra isso porque o personagem praticamente já chega interpretado pela própria postura corporal. henry não entra naquela escola com a energia do professor idealista que vai descobrir sua vocação. ele entra como alguém que aprendeu a não criar raízes. o título, é menos uma característica profissional do que uma estratégia de sobrevivência. ele observa alunos, colegas, familiares e desconhecidos, mas tenta não se deixar possuir por nenhum deles. a ironia é que o próprio ato de observar acaba produzindo vínculos que ele gostaria de evitar. e kaye filma essa distância de maneira muito particular. o filme parece estar constantemente oscilando entre documentário, drama televisivo, videoclipe, ensaio visual e diário subjetivo. tem câmera na mão, animação, desenhos sobre a imagem, fotografias, textos, imagens em baixa definição, cortes abruptos, planos que parecem ter sido arrancados de um arquivo pessoal. às vezes isso é poderoso porque dá a sensação de que estamos dentro de uma consciência fragmentada. outras vezes é excessivo, porque kaye parece tão ansioso pra comunicar o estado emocional do personagem que a própria forma começa a gritar aquilo que a atuação já estava dizendo. esse é, pra mim, o grande problema e também a grande virtude do filme. tony kaye é um diretor que não parece confiar na neutralidade da câmera. ele quer que cada sequência carregue uma posição emocional. em a outra história americana , isso aparecia através da manipulação formal e do contraste entre preto e branco e cor. aqui ele leva essa tendência pra um território ainda mais subjetivo. a escola não é simplesmente uma instituição filmada. ela é quase uma paisagem mental da alienação contemporânea. o problema é que o roteiro às vezes reduz essa complexidade a uma série de afirmações bastante explícitas. o filme quer falar sobre professores desvalorizados, adolescentes abandonados, famílias ausentes, burocracia educacional, sexualização precoce, depressão, pobreza e a transformação da escola em uma instituição que precisa administrar problemas sociais muito maiores do que ela consegue resolver. tudo isso é legítimo. mas frequentemente o filme parece ter medo de que o espectador não tenha entendido, então coloca outra camada de sofrimento por cima. isso fica especialmente evidente na maneira como alguns estudantes são construídos. há momentos em que eles parecem menos personagens do que manifestações de determinados problemas sociais. a garota prostituída, a adolescente que procura afeto, o aluno agressivo, a professora esgotada. o filme possui uma indignação genuína, mas às vezes sua indignação transforma pessoas em símbolos. é uma diferença importante: quando o filme observa uma pessoa sofrendo, ele pode ser devastador; quando precisa explicar o significado daquele sofrimento, torna-se muito mais convencional. e tem algo bastante curioso na relação entre henry e os alunos justamente porque ele tenta não ser o “salvador”. isso diferencia de boa parte do subgênero do professor inspirador. não existe uma grande sequência em que o professor encontra a técnica pedagógica perfeita e muda uma turma inteira. henry sabe que uma pessoa sozinha não consegue consertar uma estrutura social quebrada. ele pode escutar alguém, oferecer algum cuidado, impedir uma pequena tragédia, mas não pode transformar a escola em outra coisa. isso dá ao filme uma dimensão política interessante, mesmo quando ele se torna sentimental demais. a escola aparece como o lugar onde todas as falhas da sociedade chegam ao mesmo tempo. professores precisam lidar com alunos cuja vida doméstica está destruída, adolescentes procuram nos outros aquilo que não recebem em casa, administradores respondem a estatísticas e avaliações, famílias transferem responsabilidades. a escola não criou necessariamente essas condições. ela simplesmente é o lugar onde elas se tornam impossíveis de ignorar. por isso eu gosto particularmente das cenas em que o filme deixa de discursar e simplesmente acompanha henry trabalhando. existe uma tensão entre cuidar dos outros e não conseguir cuidar de si mesmo que brody sustenta muito bem. a voz baixa, o olhar cansado, a maneira como ele ocupa os espaços. ele não interpreta um homem vazio. interpreta alguém que construiu o vazio deliberadamente pra não precisar encarar aquilo que existe por baixo. e aí mercedes, a jovem prostituída torna essa contradição ainda mais dolorosa. a relação entre os dois funciona porque henry não consegue simplesmente permanecer um observador. ele reconhece nela uma vulnerabilidade que desperta algo que sua filosofia de distanciamento não consegue controlar. ao mesmo tempo, o filme precisa tomar cuidado pra não transformar essa relação em uma fantasia de redenção masculina, e felizmente tem momentos em que ele consegue preservar a assimetria e o desconforto da situação. o avô de henry também é essencial pra compreender o personagem. o passado não aparece apenas como informação biográfica, mas como aquilo que torna impossível pra ele permanecer completamente desprendido. o filme vai revelando que o “ substituto ” não nasceu de uma filosofia sofisticada. nasceu de trauma, culpa e perda. e isso é muito mais interessante do que a superfície de “professor desencantado”. por outro lado, existe uma espécie de romantização da depressão e do sofrimento que considero problemática. às vezes parece acreditar que quanto mais devastada estiver uma pessoa, mais profundamente humana ela é. a fotografia, a trilha, a montagem e as performances trabalham constantemente pra elevar a dor ao estatuto de experiência quase poética. em seus melhores momentos isso produz uma melancolia genuína. nos piores, parece que o filme está transformando sofrimento em estética. essa ambivalência é muito tony kaye. ele é um cineasta profundamente emocional, mas sua emoção frequentemente vem acompanhada de uma necessidade quase compulsiva de tornar visível a emoção. ele não quer apenas que você perceba que alguém está triste. quer que a textura da imagem fique triste, que a montagem fique triste, que o desenho fique triste, que a música fique triste. às vezes é lindo. às vezes é como alguém sublinhando três vezes uma frase que já estava sublinhada. no fim, acho que o título acaba sendo mais importante do que toda a retórica sobre educação. henry passa o filme tentando se manter separado do mundo, como se observar fosse uma maneira de não sofrer. mas a própria experiência de ensinar demonstra o contrário: olhar verdadeiramente pra outra pessoa já é uma forma de envolvimento. você pode se recusar a salvar o mundo, e provavelmente deve, porque ninguém consegue, mas não consegue observar uma pessoa em sofrimento indefinidamente sem que alguma coisa dentro de você responda. e talvez o filme seja mais forte justamente nessa contradição. henry quer ser espectador de uma sociedade em colapso, mas descobre que não existe posição neutra diante da dor. tony kaye pode exagerar, sentimentalizar e transformar sua indignação em espetáculo, mas é difícil dizer que ele não acredita profundamente naquilo que está filmando.

texto: Being a teacher isn’t for the weak. This movie was depressing on so many levels.. ad nauseam to the point of utter nihilism. It catalogues the sufferings of so many different experiences, and the “detatchment” is the numbness the protagonist uses to no avail. It’s difficult for me to watch something like this because I know in reality the solution to all the anguish and turmoil of humanity is found in Christ alone. On the one hand it’s disheartening subject matter but on the other, pretty amazing that I can watch something as brutal and not sink into self-pity and existential dread, because I know there is goodness and hope despite it.

texto: ho pensieri contrastanti su questo film. Alla fine è indubbiamente molto carino, brody come sempre è il gotto ma purtroppo è il film stesso ad avere dei palesi problemi. Questo film cerca di trasmettere messaggi giusti come la critica alle istituzioni, alla società odierna, alla scuola, ai rapporti umani e chi più ne ha più ne metta. Tutti questi messaggi (anche se giusti per carità) hanno creato un minestrone confusionario di scene a tratti toccanti, a tratti quasi banali e non necessarie. Molti dei problemi trattati in questo film si sono praticamente ridotti a semplici clichè che non riescono effettivamente a far breccia completamente in chi guarda, infatti penso che per apprezzare questo film tu debba già aver condotto riflessioni e conclusioni in merito a questi argomenti per conto tuo, altrimenti purtroppo non riuscirà a passarti molto. In se comunque è un film carino, ma come detto prima, si è voluto fare troppo. Sebbene questo, almeno dalle descrizioni, fosse un film incentrato sulla scuola e le sue criticitá odierne, la parte più forte e toccante del film è stato il rapporto tra il protagonista ed erica, che sebbene l’inizio mi abbia dato l’impressione di una sindrome da crocerossina, si è evoluto bene e avrei gradito molto più un focus su quest’ultimo. In sostanza vengono passati molti messaggi condivisibili, ma non vengono approfonditi a dovere, un peccato, sembra quasi un film a metà.

texto: Felt a bit too stream-of-consciousness-y and disjointed in parts, but the writing is touching and the message powerful. A tour de force for Brody who's almost on every moment of the film but Sami Gayle (Erica, the young prostitute), Christina Hendricks and James Caan (in a very funny part) also stayed with me for their performances. Being a teacher is such a responsibility and it's so hard and not thanked enough, but it's also true that so many are failing the younger generations. However, the film just emphasizes the brokenness and almost painful loneliness without ever giving any hope or an attempt at what could be changed so the message felt, to me, a bit too bleak and too oppressive in the end.

arrancados de um arquivo pessoal. às vezes isso é poderoso porque dá a sensação de que estamos dentro de uma consciência fragmentada. outras vezes é excessivo, porque kaye parece tão ansioso pra comunicar o estado emocional do personagem que a própria forma começa a gritar aquilo que a atuação já estava dizendo. esse é, pra mim, o grande problema e também a grande virtude do filme. tony kaye é um diretor que não parece confiar na neutralidade da câmera. ele quer que cada sequência carregue uma posição emocional. em a outra história americana , isso aparecia através da manipulação formal e do contraste entre preto e branco e cor. aqui ele leva essa tendência pra um território ainda mais subjetivo. a escola não é simplesmente uma instituição filmada. ela é quase uma paisagem mental da alienação contemporânea. o problema é que o roteiro às vezes reduz essa complexidade a uma série de afirmações bastante explícitas. o filme quer falar sobre professores desvalorizados, adolescentes abandonados, famílias ausentes, burocracia educacional, sexualização precoce, depressão, pobreza e a transformação da escola em uma instituição que precisa administrar problemas sociais muito maiores do que ela consegue resolver. tudo isso é legítimo. mas frequentemente o filme parece ter medo de que o espectador não tenha entendido, então coloca outra camada de sofrimento por cima. isso fica especialmente evidente na maneira como alguns estudantes são construídos. há momentos em que eles parecem menos personagens do que manifestações de determinados problemas sociais. a garota prostituída, a adolescente que procura afeto, o aluno agressivo, a professora esgotada. o filme possui uma indignação genuína, mas às vezes sua indignação transforma pessoas em símbolos. é uma diferença importante: quando o filme observa uma pessoa sofrendo, ele pode ser devastador; quando precisa explicar o significado daquele sofrimento, torna-se muito mais convencional. e tem algo bastante curioso na relação entre henry e os alunos justamente porque ele tenta não ser o “salvador”. isso diferencia de boa parte do subgênero do professor inspirador. não existe uma grande sequência em que o professor encontra a técnica pedagógica perfeita e muda uma turma inteira. henry sabe que uma pessoa sozinha não consegue consertar uma estrutura social quebrada. ele pode escutar alguém, oferecer algum cuidado, impedir uma pequena tragédia, mas não pode transformar a escola em outra coisa. isso dá ao filme uma dimensão política interessante, mesmo quando ele se torna sentimental demais. a escola aparece como o lugar onde todas as falhas da sociedade chegam ao mesmo tempo. professores precisam lidar com alunos cuja vida doméstica está destruída, adolescentes procuram nos outros aquilo que não recebem em casa, administradores respondem a estatísticas e avaliações, famílias transferem responsabilidades. a escola não criou necessariamente essas condições. ela simplesmente é o lugar onde elas se tornam impossíveis de ignorar. por isso eu gosto particularmente das cenas em que o filme deixa de discursar e simplesmente acompanha henry trabalhando. existe uma tensão entre cuidar dos outros e não conseguir cuidar de si mesmo que brody sustenta muito bem. a voz baixa, o olhar cansado, a maneira como ele ocupa os espaços. ele não interpreta um homem vazio. interpreta alguém que construiu o vazio deliberadamente pra não precisar encarar aquilo que existe por baixo. e aí mercedes, a jovem prostituída torna essa contradição ainda mais dolorosa. a relação entre os dois funciona porque henry não consegue simplesmente permanecer um observador. ele reconhece nela uma vulnerabilidade que desperta algo que sua filosofia de distanciamento não consegue controlar. ao mesmo tempo, o filme precisa tomar cuidado pra não transformar essa relação em uma fantasia de redenção masculina, e felizmente tem momentos em que ele consegue preservar a assimetria e o desconforto da situação. o avô de henry também é essencial pra compreender o personagem. o passado não aparece apenas como informação biográfica, mas como aquilo que torna impossível pra ele permanecer completamente desprendido. o filme vai revelando que o “ substituto ” não nasceu de uma filosofia sofisticada. nasceu de trauma, culpa e perda. e isso é muito mais interessante do que a superfície de “professor desencantado”. por outro lado, existe uma espécie de romantização da depressão e do sofrimento que considero problemática. às vezes parece acreditar que quanto mais devastada estiver uma pessoa, mais profundamente humana ela é. a fotografia, a trilha, a montagem e as performances trabalham constantemente pra elevar a dor ao estatuto de experiência quase poética. em seus melhores momentos isso produz uma melancolia genuína. nos piores, parece que o filme está transformando sofrimento em estética. essa ambivalência é muito tony kaye. ele é um cineasta profundamente emocional, mas sua emoção frequentemente vem acompanhada de uma necessidade quase compulsiva de tornar visível a emoção. ele não quer apenas que você perceba que alguém está triste. quer que a textura da imagem fique triste, que a montagem fique triste, que o desenho fique triste, que a música fique triste. às vezes é lindo. às vezes é como alguém sublinhando três vezes uma frase que já estava sublinhada. no fim, acho que o título acaba sendo mais importante do que toda a retórica sobre educação. henry passa o filme tentando se manter separado do mundo, como se observar fosse uma maneira de não sofrer. mas a própria experiência de ensinar demonstra o contrário: olhar verdadeiramente pra outra pessoa já é uma forma de envolvimento. você pode se recusar a salvar o mundo, e provavelmente deve, porque ninguém consegue, mas não consegue observar uma pessoa em sofrimento indefinidamente sem que alguma coisa dentro de você responda. e talvez o filme seja mais forte justamente nessa contradição. henry quer ser espectador de uma sociedade em colapso, mas descobre que não existe posição neutra diante da dor. tony kaye pode exagerar, sentimentalizar e transformar sua indignação em espetáculo, mas é difícil dizer que ele não acredita profundamente naquilo que está filmando.

texto: Detachment hooked me with its premise, but unfortunately, it didn’t quite hold up with its own narrative. While it tackled important themes like trauma, isolation, and the struggles within the education system, it ended up feeling like a string of tragic subplots being ticked off a checklist rather than one cohesive story. There was so much going on that I kept asking myself, “What’s happening? What’s this even about?” As the film kept introducing new tragedies without giving any of them enough time to fully resonate, I found myself becoming less and less invested. It became so dependent on piling on misery to make its point that, for me, it completely lost the emotional impact it was aiming for.

A movie that was made to be clipped and shown in health classrooms and for teachers whose entire personality is their self-inflicted Sisyphean career choices.

texto: I saw tiktok edits of this movie and decided I’ll give it a watch because I loved Adrien Brody’s character in Peaky Blinders and I think he’s a good actor. I do try my very best to watch movies with an open mind, and can appreciate when filmmakers take a more bold approach towards their craft. But this whole movie just felt like a misery porn that misses the mark, finding itself outside of what I assumed they were trying to go for. I’ve given this movie 2 tries and was just waiting for the movie to end both times. While I do understand why Tony Kaye chose to shoot the film in a handheld documentary-esque way, I just don't feel like it fits the way some people have said. Maybe my palette for cinema just isnt developed, But it makes me a bit sad to give this a low rating considering how much I really like Lucy Liu, Bryan Cranston, and Adrien Brody. I will eventually come around to watching this a third time because I do think this movie deserves an extra chance. Unfortunately at the current moment, Detachment will sit at a 2-star rating.

texto: "How many of you have felt the weight of pressure on your shoulders?" Não tem uma fotografia incrível, ângulos marcantes ou imagens deslumbrantes. O filme se destaca por expor, de forma nua e crua, a dor da realidade em que estamos inseridos: a solidão, negligência, violência, pobreza, cobrança e abandono. Em um mesmo cenário: a escola. E isso é apresentado por meio de diferentes perspectivas, dos alunos, dos professores, da diretora, da conselheira... e como o acúmulo de tantas experiências negativas afeta o nosso interior e, consequentemente, a forma como vivemos e nos relacionamos. Uma palavra para descrever? Complexidade. Algo que resuma? Baita crise existencial.

texto: I expected this to be primarily about the school system and while it of course is, on a broader scale it feels like it tackles generational divide more than anything. The youth are expected to learn and be guided by those who came before, but what of the problems plaguing that generation? How can you teach and guide when you feel aimless and lost yourself? Being older does not inherently mean being wiser, and so often these people are thrust into a position of responsibility when they were never given the guidance they’re now expected to pass on. These issues chain all the way back through the generations that came before and they will continue to all those that will follow. At one point do you change from the person who is guided to the one who guides, and what do you do if you’re wholly unprepared for that? Until we can solve that question, the kids really don’t stand a chance.

texto: Adrian Brody with an insanely impressive performance. Single handily roped me into this movie despite some of the acting from a few of the kids here. I think the premise was great to try and harp on the teachers rather than the system but the actions were a bit drawn out of proportion for the students especially how quickly they were to “realize” or “change.” Brody’s teaching style is so subtle and effective I genuinely loved watching him talk in every scene. The rest of the cast had a few surprises as I just scrolled on Prime and finally chose this but some adults here like Caan were great too. Loved his 1 on 1 scene with the kid that he verbally destroyed. Detachment felt similar to Half Nelson where as it both revolved around teachers and students showing that clearly both parties have deeper problems outside the classroom. Very sad but overall a super solid movie.

texto: Bien, sans être un très grand film. Henry Barthes est professeur remplaçant. Il est assigné trois semaines dans un lycée difficile de la banlieue new-yorkaise, et il s'efforce de toujours garder ses distances. Adrien Brody est excellent, et le personnage est bien plus complexe qu'il n'y paraît. Il n'est pas un saint : il a choisi le détachement pour se protéger des émotions négatives, sauf que ça le coupe aussi des positives. C'est ce qui rend le film juste il ne peut pas être là pour les deux filles qui auraient besoin de lui. Ce que Tony Kaye réussit, c'est le portrait du corps enseignant. Les espoirs, le doute, le ras-le-bol, la fatigue, parfois la haine du métier et des élèves. Chaque prof incarne une façon différente de tenir, et tous sont touchants. Kaye appelle ça un paysage d'émotions. Le film évite aussi le récit attendu. On croit qu'il va conquérir les gamins et leur redonner une voix, et Kaye refuse complètement ce jeu. Ma réserve : c'est parfois hyperbolique et didactique. Kaye assène ses points à coups de masse, et certaines scènes sont là uniquement pour choquer. On sent la volonté de nous mettre le nez dedans plus que la confiance dans le récit. Beau, dur, et un peu trop démonstratif pour moi.

texto: "I'm not here,you may see me but I'm hollow" حين يصبح الابتعاد وسيلة للبقاء هناك أفلام تحاول أن تشرح لنا العالم، وهناك أفلام تجعلنا نشعر بثقله دون أن تمنحنا فرصة للهروب منه. وفيلم Detachment ينتمي إلى النوع الثاني؛ فهو ليس مجرد فيلم عن التعليم أو عن معاناة المعلمين والطلاب، بل تأمل مؤلم في الإنسان حين يصبح محاصرًا بين ما يشعر به وما يستطيع التعبير عنه، وبين حاجته إلى الآخرين وخوفه من الاقتراب منهم. منذ عنوانه، يضع الفيلم أمامنا فكرة أساسية: الانفصال العاطفي. ذلك الابتعاد الذي قد يبدو في البداية نوعًا من القوة أو السيطرة على الذات، لكنه قد يكون في الحقيقة وسيلة دفاع يلجأ إليها الإنسان بعدما يصبح الألم أكبر من قدرته على احتماله. فأحيانًا لا يبتعد الإنسان لأنه لا يحتاج إلى أحد، بل لأنه يحتاج إلى الآخرين أكثر مما يستطيع الاعتراف به. وأحيانًا لا يكون الصمت دليلًا على البرود، بل محاولة أخيرة لحماية ما تبقى من روح أنهكتها التجارب. ### الفكرة — عالم مليء بالناس، لكنه عاجز عن التواصل يتناول الفيلم عالم التعليم من زاوية تتجاوز المناهج والدرجات والنجاح الأكاديمي. فالمدرسة هنا ليست مجرد مكان لنقل المعرفة، بل مساحة تتقاطع فيها معاناة الطلاب، وعجز المعلمين، وضغوط المجتمع، وتلك المسافة المتزايدة بين الإنسان والإنسان. هنري بارثس، الذي يؤدي دوره أدريان برودي، معلم بديل ينتقل بين المدارس دون أن يسمح لنفسه بالانتماء الكامل إلى أي مكان. يبدو هادئًا ومتماسكًا، لكنه يحمل داخله ماضيًا مؤلمًا يجعله مترددًا في بناء علاقات عميقة مع الآخرين. إنه يعرف كيف يستمع، وكيف يفهم ألم الناس، لكنه يجد صعوبة في السماح لأحد بأن يقترب من ألمه الخاص. وهنا تكمن المفارقة التي يمنحها الفيلم عمقًا إنسانيًا كبيرًا: قد يكون الإنسان قادرًا على فهم الآخرين، لكنه عاجز عن إنقاذ نفسه. وقد يمنح الآخرين الكلمات التي يحتاجون إليها للاستمرار، بينما لا يجد الكلمات المناسبة ليواجه بها حياته. الفيلم لا يصور هنري باعتباره بطلًا مثاليًا أو شخصًا يمتلك إجابات عن كل شيء؛ بل يقدمه إنسانًا يحاول أن يؤدي دوره في عالم لا يعرف كيف يتعامل مع جراحه. وهذا ما يجعل شخصيته مؤثرة؛ لأنها لا تنتمي إلى عالم الأبطال الخارقين، بل إلى عالم الأشخاص الذين يواصلون حياتهم رغم أنهم لا يعرفون تمامًا كيف يفعلون ذلك. ### الإبداع في الطرح — الألم الذي لا يحتاج إلى صراخ من أكثر الجوانب إبداعًا في Detachment طريقته في تصوير المعاناة النفسية. فهو لا يعتمد دائمًا على الأحداث الكبيرة أو المواجهات المباشرة، بل يمنح التفاصيل الصغيرة مساحة واسعة كي تكشف ما تعجز الشخصيات عن قوله. تتداخل الصور والذكريات والحوارات والمونولوجات لتخلق إحساسًا بأننا لا نشاهد العالم من الخارج فقط، بل نقترب من الطريقة التي يراه بها إنسان مثقل بتجاربه. والمدرسة، بما تحمله من فوضى وضغوط وعلاقات متوترة، تصبح صورة مصغرة لمجتمع يعاني من أزمة أعمق: أزمة في القدرة على الإصغاء، وفي فهم احتياجات الآخرين، وفي الاعتراف بأن وراء كل سلوك إنسانًا له قصة لا نعرفها. إن الإبداع هنا ليس في تقديم فكرة جديدة تمامًا، بل في الطريقة التي تتشابك بها الأفكار الإنسانية مع الأسلوب السينمائي. فالفيلم يستخدم صورًا وتكوينات بصرية غير تقليدية ليجعلنا نشعر بالاضطراب الداخلي للشخصيات، وكأن الشكل نفسه أصبح امتدادًا لحالتها النفسية. ### التمثيل — أداء يحمل ما لا تقوله الكلمات يقدم أدريان برودي أداءً هادئًا ومشحونًا بالمشاعر المكبوتة. فهو لا يعتمد على الانفعالات الصاخبة بقدر ما يعتمد على النظرات، والتردد، ونبرة الصوت، والمسافة التي يتركها بين شخصيته وبين العالم المحيط بها. إن هنري شخصية يصعب فهمها بالكامل، وهذا جزء من قوتها. فكلما حاولنا الاقتراب منها، اكتشفنا أن هناك شيئًا لا تستطيع قوله، أو ربما لا تعرف كيف تقوله. وتقدم بيتي كاي، في دور إيريكا، حضورًا إنسانيًا مؤلمًا يضيف إلى الفيلم بعدًا آخر من أبعاد الإهمال والوحدة والحاجة إلى الحنان. ومن خلال الشخصيات المحيطة بهما، لا تبدو المعاناة حكرًا على فرد واحد، بل حالة تتخذ أشكالًا مختلفة، وتترك آثارًا متفاوتة في كل إنسان. قوة التمثيل في الفيلم تكمن في أنه لا يجعل الشخصيات مجرد أدوات لإيصال رسالة اجتماعية؛ بل يمنحها تناقضاتها وضعفها واحتياجاتها، حتى نشعر أن لكل منها حياة كاملة تتجاوز حدود الشاشة. ### الأثر النفسي — حين نكتشف أن الصمت ليس دائمًا سلامًا ربما أكثر ما يجعل الفيلم مؤثرًا هو أنه يضعنا أمام أشكال مختلفة من الوحدة. هناك من يختار الابتعاد عن الآخرين، وهناك من يُترك وحيدًا رغم محاولاته المستمرة للتواصل، وهناك من يعيش وسط الناس لكنه يشعر بأنه غير مرئي. والفيلم يجعلنا نتساءل: كم مرة مررنا بجانب إنسان ولم ننتبه إلى ما يحمله داخله؟ وكم مرة فسرنا صمت شخص بأنه عدم اهتمام، بينما كان في الحقيقة عاجزًا عن التعبير؟ وكم مرة أخفينا نحن أنفسنا خلف الهدوء، لأننا لم نعرف كيف نطلب المساعدة؟ إنه لا يطلب منا أن نبرر كل تصرف مؤلم، ولا أن نعتبر كل شخص ضحية بلا مسؤولية؛ بل يدعونا إلى أن نكون أكثر انتباهًا إلى التعقيد الإنساني الذي لا يظهر دائمًا على السطح. ومع ذلك، لا يقدم الفيلم الانفصال العاطفي باعتباره حلًا ناجحًا. فهو يكشف ثمنه أيضًا: أن تحمي نفسك من الألم قد يعني أحيانًا أن تحرمها من القرب والدفء والانتماء. وأن تتجنب التعلق بالآخرين قد يجنبك بعض الخسارات، لكنه قد يجعلك تخسر أشياء لا يمكن تعويضها. ### الخاتمة — أن تبقى إنسانًا رغم كل شيء Detachment ليس فيلمًا يمنحك شعورًا مريحًا بأن كل شيء سينتهي على ما يرام. إنه فيلم يتركك أمام أسئلة ثقيلة عن التعليم، والمجتمع، والطفولة، والوحدة، وعن قدرة الإنسان على الاستمرار حين لا يجد من يفهمه. لكنه، وسط كل هذا الألم، لا يخلو من لحظات إنسانية تذكّرنا بأن التواصل، مهما بدا صعبًا، يظل ممكنًا. وأن مجرد رؤية شخص آخر، والإصغاء إليه، والاعتراف بمعاناته، قد يكون أمرًا أكثر أهمية مما نتخيل. إن Detachment هو حكاية الإنسان الذي يبتعد عن العالم كي لا ينكسر، ثم يكتشف أن الابتعاد نفسه قد يكون شكلًا آخر من أشكال الانكسار. إنه فيلم عن أولئك الذين يواصلون أداء أدوارهم في الحياة، بينما يحملون في داخلهم أشياء لم يستطيعوا مواجهتها بعد. وعن أولئك الذين يمنحون الآخرين ما كانوا يتمنون أن يحصلوا عليه هم أنفسهم. وربما أكثر ما يبقى منه بعد المشاهدة هو هذا السؤال: هل نبتعد عن الآخرين لأننا لم نعد نحتاج إليهم، أم لأننا نخشى أن نحتاج إليهم ثم نفقدهم؟ قد لا يقدم الفيلم إجابة نهائية، لكنه يجعلنا ندرك أن الإنسان، مهما حاول أن يبدو مكتفيًا بنفسه، يظل بحاجة إلى أن يُرى، وأن يُفهم، وأن يشعر بأنه ليس وحده في هذا العالم.

exemplo: O filme é visto como um retrato poderoso da solidão e da necessidade de se afastar emocionalmente como forma de sobreviver, com espectadores identificando-se com essa dualidade.
texto: "I'm not here,you may see me but I'm hollow" حين يصبح الابتعاد وسيلة للبقاء هناك أفلام تحاول أن تشرح لنا العالم، وهناك أفلام تجعلنا نشعر بثقله دون أن تمنحنا فرصة للهروب منه. وفيلم Detachment ينتمي إلى النوع الثاني؛ فهو ليس مجرد فيلم عن التعليم أو عن معاناة المعلمين والطلاب، بل تأمل مؤلم في الإنسان حين يصبح محاصرًا بين ما يشعر به وما يستطيع التعبير عنه، وبين حاجته إلى الآخرين وخوفه من الاقتراب منهم. منذ عنوانه، يضع الفيلم أمامنا فكرة أساسية: الانفصال العاطفي. ذلك الابتعاد الذي قد يبدو في البداية نوعًا من القوة أو السيطرة على الذات، لكنه قد يكون في الحقيقة وسيلة دفاع يلجأ إليها الإنسان بعدما يصبح الألم أكبر من قدرته على احتماله. فأحيانًا لا يبتعد الإنسان لأنه لا يحتاج إلى أحد، بل لأنه يحتاج إلى الآخرين أكثر مما يستطيع الاعتراف به. وأحيانًا لا يكون الصمت دليلًا على البرود، بل محاولة أخيرة لحماية ما تبقى من روح أنهكتها التجارب. ### الفكرة — عالم مليء بالناس، لكنه عاجز عن التواصل يتناول الفيلم عالم التعليم من زاوية تتجاوز المناهج والدرجات والنجاح الأكاديمي. فالمدرسة هنا ليست مجرد مكان لنقل المعرفة، بل مساحة تتقاطع فيها معاناة الطلاب، وعجز المعلمين، وضغوط المجتمع، وتلك المسافة المتزايدة بين الإنسان والإنسان. هنري بارثس، الذي يؤدي دوره أدريان برودي، معلم بديل ينتقل بين المدارس دون أن يسمح لنفسه بالانتماء الكامل إلى أي مكان. يبدو هادئًا ومتماسكًا، لكنه يحمل داخله ماضيًا مؤلمًا يجعله مترددًا في بناء علاقات عميقة مع الآخرين. إنه يعرف كيف يستمع، وكيف يفهم ألم الناس، لكنه يجد صعوبة في السماح لأحد بأن يقترب من ألمه الخاص. وهنا تكمن المفارقة التي يمنحها الفيلم عمقًا إنسانيًا كبيرًا: قد يكون الإنسان قادرًا على فهم الآخرين، لكنه عاجز عن إنقاذ نفسه. وقد يمنح الآخرين الكلمات التي يحتاجون إليها للاستمرار، بينما لا يجد الكلمات المناسبة ليواجه بها حياته. الفيلم لا يصور هنري باعتباره بطلًا مثاليًا أو شخصًا يمتلك إجابات عن كل شيء؛ بل يقدمه إنسانًا يحاول أن يؤدي دوره في عالم لا يعرف كيف يتعامل مع جراحه. وهذا ما يجعل شخصيته مؤثرة؛ لأنها لا تنتمي إلى عالم الأبطال الخارقين، بل إلى عالم الأشخاص الذين يواصلون حياتهم رغم أنهم لا يعرفون تمامًا كيف يفعلون ذلك. ### الإبداع في الطرح — الألم الذي لا يحتاج إلى صراخ من أكثر الجوانب إبداعًا في Detachment طريقته في تصوير المعاناة النفسية. فهو لا يعتمد دائمًا على الأحداث الكبيرة أو المواجهات المباشرة، بل يمنح التفاصيل الصغيرة مساحة واسعة كي تكشف ما تعجز الشخصيات عن قوله. تتداخل الصور والذكريات والحوارات والمونولوجات لتخلق إحساسًا بأننا لا نشاهد العالم من الخارج فقط، بل نقترب من الطريقة التي يراه بها إنسان مثقل بتجاربه. والمدرسة، بما تحمله من فوضى وضغوط وعلاقات متوترة، تصبح صورة مصغرة لمجتمع يعاني من أزمة أعمق: أزمة في القدرة على الإصغاء، وفي فهم احتياجات الآخرين، وفي الاعتراف بأن وراء كل سلوك إنسانًا له قصة لا نعرفها. إن الإبداع هنا ليس في تقديم فكرة جديدة تمامًا، بل في الطريقة التي تتشابك بها الأفكار الإنسانية مع الأسلوب السينمائي. فالفيلم يستخدم صورًا وتكوينات بصرية غير تقليدية ليجعلنا نشعر بالاضطراب الداخلي للشخصيات، وكأن الشكل نفسه أصبح امتدادًا لحالتها النفسية. ### التمثيل — أداء يحمل ما لا تقوله الكلمات يقدم أدريان برودي أداءً هادئًا ومشحونًا بالمشاعر المكبوتة. فهو لا يعتمد على الانفعالات الصاخبة بقدر ما يعتمد على النظرات، والتردد، ونبرة الصوت، والمسافة التي يتركها بين شخصيته وبين العالم المحيط بها. إن هنري شخصية يصعب فهمها بالكامل، وهذا جزء من قوتها. فكلما حاولنا الاقتراب منها، اكتشفنا أن هناك شيئًا لا تستطيع قوله، أو ربما لا تعرف كيف تقوله. وتقدم بيتي كاي، في دور إيريكا، حضورًا إنسانيًا مؤلمًا يضيف إلى الفيلم بعدًا آخر من أبعاد الإهمال والوحدة والحاجة إلى الحنان. ومن خلال الشخصيات المحيطة بهما، لا تبدو المعاناة حكرًا على فرد واحد، بل حالة تتخذ أشكالًا مختلفة، وتترك آثارًا متفاوتة في كل إنسان. قوة التمثيل في الفيلم تكمن في أنه لا يجعل الشخصيات مجرد أدوات لإيصال رسالة اجتماعية؛ بل يمنحها تناقضاتها وضعفها واحتياجاتها، حتى نشعر أن لكل منها حياة كاملة تتجاوز حدود الشاشة. ### الأثر النفسي — حين نكتشف أن الصمت ليس دائمًا سلامًا ربما أكثر ما يجعل الفيلم مؤثرًا هو أنه يضعنا أمام أشكال مختلفة من الوحدة. هناك من يختار الابتعاد عن الآخرين، وهناك من يُترك وحيدًا رغم محاولاته المستمرة للتواصل، وهناك من يعيش وسط الناس لكنه يشعر بأنه غير مرئي. والفيلم يجعلنا نتساءل: كم مرة مررنا بجانب إنسان ولم ننتبه إلى ما يحمله داخله؟ وكم مرة فسرنا صمت شخص بأنه عدم اهتمام، بينما كان في الحقيقة عاجزًا عن التعبير؟ وكم مرة أخفينا نحن أنفسنا خلف الهدوء، لأننا لم نعرف كيف نطلب المساعدة؟ إنه لا يطلب منا أن نبرر كل تصرف مؤلم، ولا أن نعتبر كل شخص ضحية بلا مسؤولية؛ بل يدعونا إلى أن نكون أكثر انتباهًا إلى التعقيد الإنساني الذي لا يظهر دائمًا على السطح. ومع ذلك، لا يقدم الفيلم الانفصال العاطفي باعتباره حلًا ناجحًا. فهو يكشف ثمنه أيضًا: أن تحمي نفسك من الألم قد يعني أحيانًا أن تحرمها من القرب والدفء والانتماء. وأن تتجنب التعلق بالآخرين قد يجنبك بعض الخسارات، لكنه قد يجعلك تخسر أشياء لا يمكن تعويضها. ### الخاتمة — أن تبقى إنسانًا رغم كل شيء Detachment ليس فيلمًا يمنحك شعورًا مريحًا بأن كل شيء سينتهي على ما يرام. إنه فيلم يتركك أمام أسئلة ثقيلة عن التعليم، والمجتمع، والطفولة، والوحدة، وعن قدرة الإنسان على الاستمرار حين لا يجد من يفهمه. لكنه، وسط كل هذا الألم، لا يخلو من لحظات إنسانية تذكّرنا بأن التواصل، مهما بدا صعبًا، يظل ممكنًا. وأن مجرد رؤية شخص آخر، والإصغاء إليه، والاعتراف بمعاناته، قد يكون أمرًا أكثر أهمية مما نتخيل. إن Detachment هو حكاية الإنسان الذي يبتعد عن العالم كي لا ينكسر، ثم يكتشف أن الابتعاد نفسه قد يكون شكلًا آخر من أشكال الانكسار. إنه فيلم عن أولئك الذين يواصلون أداء أدوارهم في الحياة، بينما يحملون في داخلهم أشياء لم يستطيعوا مواجهتها بعد. وعن أولئك الذين يمنحون الآخرين ما كانوا يتمنون أن يحصلوا عليه هم أنفسهم. وربما أكثر ما يبقى منه بعد المشاهدة هو هذا السؤال: هل نبتعد عن الآخرين لأننا لم نعد نحتاج إليهم، أم لأننا نخشى أن نحتاج إليهم ثم نفقدهم؟ قد لا يقدم الفيلم إجابة نهائية، لكنه يجعلنا ندرك أن الإنسان، مهما حاول أن يبدو مكتفيًا بنفسه، يظل بحاجة إلى أن يُرى، وأن يُفهم، وأن يشعر بأنه ليس وحده في هذا العالم.

texto: "How many of you have felt the weight of pressure on your shoulders?" Não tem uma fotografia incrível, ângulos marcantes ou imagens deslumbrantes. O filme se destaca por expor, de forma nua e crua, a dor da realidade em que estamos inseridos: a solidão, negligência, violência, pobreza, cobrança e abandono. Em um mesmo cenário: a escola. E isso é apresentado por meio de diferentes perspectivas, dos alunos, dos professores, da diretora, da conselheira... e como o acúmulo de tantas experiências negativas afeta o nosso interior e, consequentemente, a forma como vivemos e nos relacionamos. Uma palavra para descrever? Complexidade. Algo que resuma? Baita crise existencial.

Si l'ennui les menace, ou si l'absurdité de leur vie jaillit au détour d'un miroir cruel, qu'ils se souviennent de toi, et la douleur d'exister leur semble préférable à l'inquiétude de ne plus être. Ce que tu ne vois plus, ils le regardent. Ce que tu n'entends plus, ils l'écoutent. Et ce que tu ne chantes plus, ils l'entonnent. La joie des choses simples leur apparaît à la lumière de ton triste souvenir. Tu es cette lumière noire mais intense qui, depuis ta nuit, éclaire à nouveau le jour qu'ils ne voyaient plus.

texto: The dark melancholy of older indie is an inescapable taste that rustles over and under my teeth, that it feels quite unbearable to just listlessly ponder over. I find that one long sit through is too much, I have to pause and walk around the house, digest and imagine the world within the film. Only then does the bitter taste in my mouth turn sweet and savory. And this film grey and depressive as it may appear, left me with a taste so rich I know I'll remember it long after the day this day is done.

texto: Why was this highkey a Christmas movie I didn’t dislike this movie at all actually contrary to my rating. I really loved that this touched on the topic of is it as bad to just think about cheating as it is to actually do it and I loved how the cult represented that as well. I actually really liked Tom Cruise’s performance in this too being it’s actually my first movie of his (I know shocker) and I loved how a lot of the scenes with Bill and Alice were long talking scenes. I was never bored during this movie. Now with saying all that my biggest problem is that I just wanted more from every aspect of this movie. Yes the cult was creepy with the masks and oh my gosh was the music creepy during those scenes along with the scene of Bill being followed but from both of those scenes I just wanted more. I heard from people that this movie was one of the most creepy movies people have ever scene and while the cult scene was unsettling the only thing I found creepy was the music. Then it only lasted for like 20 ish minutes and yes it weaved into the rest of the story after that but I wish there was more to it in the beginning half of the movie vs just the back half of the movie cause while I understand why that scene was there I kinda felt like it was smacked in there as to like oh now this is happening we see the password on the napkin and we gotta find out what it is but it’s not a build up to it. Now the scene of Bill being followed was good but I wanted so much more from it. I wanted him to be followed longer and lowkey I wish he was chased too (I know you aren’t supposed to rate movies based off of what you would do). I just wanted so much more from that whole scene. Lastly, I did feel like the 2 hours and 30 ish minutes went by really fast. I didn’t find myself wanting it to end or feeling the runtime the whole time it was just that I wanted so much more. Also the random plot of him being a doctor I was just like okay I know that’s not what the movies about at all but that’s just there to be there again with everything feeling like it needed to be more. I really wish I loved this more because I’ve seen so many great reviews and it’s even a couple of peoples favorite movies. Maybe this is one I’ll try to watch again in the future.

texto: We rarely suffer any physical harm from “betrayal.” Betrayal is something that is born in the heart, something that wounds the heart. And it’s incredibly difficult to grasp what betrayal actually is. Perhaps betrayal only comes into existence when either you or the other person feels that something is “betrayal.” That’s how I think it works. Betrayal can exist even without any action behind it, and in essence, it is just as much a betrayal as one that involves an actual act. If both are guilty, then perhaps neither is. Surely, everyone lives with countless betrayals inside themselves that they never actually act upon. And perhaps that is why, when we ourselves are betrayed, we suffer from the fact that we have no choice but to forgive the other person as someone who is guilty of the very same thing we are. And because it hurts, we close our eyes to it. Both of us. The movie does feel somewhat drawn-out overall, but I found it interesting how it makes you feel that everything that happens between people ultimately happens inside their hearts. Perhaps I felt that even more strongly because the two leads, who are both beautiful yet somehow strangely devoid of sex appeal, seemed almost like empty “vessels.”

texto: “I’m not gonna tell you their names… no, I’m not going to tell you their names… but if I did, I don’t think you’d sleep so well at night.” If I could describe this film in one word it would be TOPICAL. If it came out today I feel like it would either be the only thing people talked about or it would be so heavily censored that it wouldn’t even be released. The fact that Kubrick suddenly died from a heart attack just 4 days after a private screening is heartbreaking and also a bit strange? All respect to him, he’s a legend, but it definitely makes you wonder. I really enjoyed this film and was completely invested throughout. My only complaints are the pacing and how graphic it was. At times it genuinely felt like a miniseries the way it was paced. The amount of naked people was also just so uncomfortable 😭. I get that some of it is vital to the story and the nature of the secret society but it just felt sooo excessive at times. The score was so simple yet so haunting and the piano was so unsettling even just by alternating between two notes. This was definitely one of the most suspenseful films I’ve seen and it does a great job of putting you in every mysterious moment. The scene where he’s walking through the streets after he leaves Domino’s is absolutely brilliant, I was on the edge of my seat. Overall this was a great film and I can see why many would say that it’s Kubrick’s best. I loved the premise and think it’s such an interesting concept but there were just some minor things I didn’t like. If Letterboxd had a 3.75 stars option then I’d pick that.

texto: Nessuno sa catturare l'anima e l'abisso umano attraverso gli occhi come Stanley Kubrick. È un viaggio tesissimo dentro le crepe di una coppia apparentemente indistruttibile, scossa dal dubbio e dalla tentazione di essere altro, per poi comprendere che essere "normali" non è una condanna ma una salvezza. Le scene della villa in maschera sono tra le più disturbanti e magnetiche mai girate; la nudità è abbondante ma di un'eleganza assoluta, priva di qualsiasi volgarità. L'ultimo atto costruisce una tensione paranoica soffocante, alimentata dalla lucida consapevolezza dell'impotenza individuale di fronte a poteri invisibili e inaccessibili. Prova maiuscola di Nicole Kidman e Tom Cruise — al netto di un doppiaggio italiano imbarazzante —, impreziosita da una recitazione complessa che risente positivamente delle reali tensioni dei due protagonisti. Da guardare, non da vedere.

The scene where he’s walking through the streets after he leaves Domino’s is absolutely brilliant, I was on the edge of my seat. Overall this was a great film and I can see why many would say that it’s Kubrick’s best. I loved the premise and think it’s such an interesting concept but there were just some minor things I didn’t like. If Letterboxd had a 3.75 stars option then I’d pick that.

texto: Normally I would say some light-hearted things about the movie I just watched. And I’ll say same at the end, but for now I am going to keep things serious. Because this was a serious movie. The wheels in my head are still turning about the meaning behind what I’ve watched, below the surface of what we are told. It’s a dangerous movie, that is for sure. I can only imagine what was within the 40 cut minutes of this film, which were destroyed after Kubrick’s death. It almost feels like a warning to how the uppermost people of the world exist. It’s scary because it could be true. Key word “could”. Some films are scary because we know they are real somewhere, but this one is purely unknown. Alas, how unknown is it really, how far-fetched do the events in this film actually seem? This is what Kubrick seemed to want to show us with his final film. To tell us to keep our Eyes Wide Open in a corrupt world that thrives on us keeping them Shut. However, this what I feel could be an underlying theme. Obviously this film is based on an older novella as I discovered, which shares a different message. Just as interesting though. Tom Cruise did wonders in this film, can’t wait to see him in Digger. The ambiance was unbelievably tense, that piano was dreadful, in a good way. The dialogue and scenes were so encapsulating. Truly a work of art. Finally as promised, a lighter paragraph. If Die Hard and Gremlins are Christmas movies (for the record I think they both are), is Eyes Wide Shut as well? Food for thought.

Outwardly the budget is improved, Lee Van Cleef is here to chew up the scenery, Volonté is back for another villainous turn and Morricone's score is as sharp as ever and the motifs are now front and center with the addition of the haunting diegetic watch theme. But a series of fun and dark set pieces isn't enough to bring the whole picture together in a cohesive unit. Ultimately the characters are a little more one-dimensional, particularly Eastwood's unnamed man who is more morally grey but just has less to do and is less interesting. It is fun to see Van Cleef's Mortimer get the upper hand a few times but never goes much deeper than fun.

The instant deaths from gunshots down play the legitimate suffering that happens when you shoot someone. The lesson being told isn’t applicable to the real world, it may work here and there but in the long run it will eat you alive. The movie is very pretty having a significant budget increase from the first film in the trilogy. Enio Morricone is once again very good at his job. Sergio Leone always seems to know how to frame his characters in order to squeeze out as much emotion from his shots as he can. But as pretty as it is I can’t get behind its message.

texto: For a few dollars more had potential to be more interesting than a fistful of dollars, but something about the execution left me wanting for more. For starters, the soundtrack for the most part exceeds the original. The gimmick with the pocketwatch helped to build anticipation during the duels  and also gave the scenes a little more emotional weight to them. In contrast to the usual epic western music, the quiet tune puts us in the shoes of the characters a little. The additional layer of melancholy in the music allows us to reflect on the brutality of these duels, and to see them for what they really are: People killing each other. I also think it was a brilliant idea to introduce another lone cowboy into the mix. Lee Van Cleef is just as effortlessly cool as Clint Eastwood and I was excited to see what kind of rivalry will spawn when two capable bounty hunters set their sights on the same target. We get a little bit of that when they first meet but they pretty much get along for the rest of the film. I just feel like that limited the opportunities for creative interactions they could've had, and took away alot of the intrigue I had from the start of the film. Another thing is I'm just not sure I like the story beats here as much as I like the ones in fistful of dollars. This is just a little messy compared to the straightforward traditional hero's journey in the first one. I also think both the Colonel and Indio's backstories and motivations could've been a little better fleshed out. There are definitely ways of doing that without nessecarily stripping away the mystery of the two characters. This would've made the final duel feel a bit more impactful and given it the sauce it needs to surpass the third act of the first film. I think the thing with Leone is that he has such a brilliant style but sometimes he just gets a little too carried away with it. Enough that there's an abundance of style but not enough substance. I still like these westerns but the problem is I can't love it as much as I want to. Maybe I'll change my mind with the good, the bad and the ugly

Leone’s style was unique in what angles he chose and how the characters were framed in the shot. The editing was also fun in this one and often dictated the tone and pacing. It was the script that held this one back. The twist and connections between the characters didn’t feel organic. The banter and witty relationships between these bounty hunters and bandits just didn’t land like they did in Leone’s first film. Still a solid watch though and looking forward to moving through the rest of his filmography.

texto: Two bounty hunters walk into the desert, discover they have the same hobby, and decide the logical solution is to compete over who can kill more people. For a Few Dollars More is basically cowboy LinkedIn, except the networking events involve revolvers and the job offers come with corpses. Clint Eastwood’s Man with No Name barely speaks, barely reacts, and somehow manages to have more charisma than everyone in the film combined. Meanwhile, Lee Van Cleef’s Colonel Mortimer arrives looking like he has been personally designed by God to wear a black hat. And then there’s the pocket watch. A tiny musical pocket watch somehow becomes one of the most sinister objects in the entire movie. Every time that melody starts playing, you know somebody’s about to have a really bad afternoon. The best part is the chemistry between Eastwood and Van Cleef. They’re not exactly friends. They’re more like two extremely competent coworkers who have accidentally been assigned the same murder project. And Sergio Leone knows how to stretch a moment until you’re practically holding your breath. The close-ups, the silence, the music, the ridiculous amount of dust — everything feels bigger than life.

texto: Shots are great, especially in the stand offs and one on one scenes. The framing has that classic old school western style where the characters are positioned carefully to build anticipation. Lighting and lens are very sharp. Sets and locations are great too. The dusty towns and wide open environments really help sell the western atmosphere. The sound design also feels old school. It lacks bass, I think. Everything sounds high pitched. Dialogues are obviously dubbed or rerecorded in the studio because some lines do not sync with the movements of their lips. The musical score sounds heroic, but emotionally I did not really feel it connecting with the story. Even by the end, I never fully felt the tension or triumph that the film was aiming for.

texto: Ok 90% of that movie makes way more sense when you realize that even though it’s the SAME ACTOR playing the villain as in a fistful of dollars, he is NOT Ramon, he is in fact Indio. I now feel silly for grunting slyly at the TV “aim for the heart, Ramon”. The excessive macho dick measuring contests for a little stale by the end. It felt like every scene was a standoff or sharpshooting some obscure object without flinching. It lost its gravitas. There were also way too many schemes to coherently follow. Even insignificant side characters had an agenda to throw the train of thought off the tracks. It was a knot of plot twists that you couldn’t untangle. Also, why’d the bitch shoot herself when she could’ve just as easily shot el Indio. Seemed unwarranted and could’ve given el Indio a more powerful backstory if there was a more relatable backstory, or at least fed into the psycho side more. He’s literally crying over some girl he raped after sliming her man. Showing any emotion at all feels contradictory to his character, but perhaps this adds to the chaotic nature of his character. Also, I know this was the 60s, but the Rojos and El Indio is just mental. Red and Indian? Like Indians are the cliche villain in Westerns, but to call Mexicans Indians in their own language seems like a unnecessary shot fired. Regardless of the over saturation of the macho, the colonel was a sweet addition. Threatening the macho of our Manco was refreshing. The cinematography felt like it took more of an advantage of the landscape, and the opening and closing shots were some of my favorites (for of a person shot off a horse in the opening, colonel riding off into the sun at end). The opening credits also had an intriguing graphic that flowed along the landscape. Fun. Color on set, lighting, and costuming felt a little more bland than fistful, but the night effects were better with the blue light as opposed to just darkening the screen in fistful. The audio syncing was yet again pretty criminal, but I won’t give too much grief given the era.

texto: WHAT A BADASS DUO ! It’s was a great sequel to the first one. You can already see Leone refining his style, both in the originality of his shots and in the musical score. The script doesn’t repeat itself. It’s different while maintaining the exact same tone, and also adding more emotional depth to the whole thing. Both characters have an unmatched aura. They feel equally powerful, but in reality, they are very different from each other and complement one another perfectly. The only thing I didn’t like, and something I generally dislike in movies, is when the same actor plays different characters in different parts of a franchise, especially when one of those characters is the main villain.

texto: Je rattrape mes classiques ! Après avoir vu Pour une poignée de dollars que je n'avais pas trop adoré, lui préférant d'ailleurs largement Yojimbo de Kurosawa, je viens de finir Et pour quelques dollars de plus, le deuxième de la trilogie, avant d'aller découvrir Le Bon, la Brute et le Truand au cinéma en 4K ce soir. Contrairement au premier volet un peu plus artisanal, ce film est beaucoup plus froid, méthodique et perfectionné. L'histoire suit deux chasseurs de primes rivaux aux méthodes opposées qui se retrouvent sur la même piste : celle de l'Indien, chef de gang psychopathe évadé qui prépare le braquage de la banque d'El Paso. D'un côté, on a Monco (Clint Eastwood) qui chasse pour l'appât du gain pur et dur, et de l'autre le colonel Douglas Mortimer (Lee Van Cleef), guidé par une vengeance personnelle et intime. Le cœur du film repose sur cette cupidité. Sergio Leone oppose le matérialisme décomplexé de l'Amérique naissante avec Clint qui compte chaque cadavre en dollars au code d'honneur chevaleresque et tragique de Mortimer, pour qui l'argent ne vaut rien face au sang versé. Côté acting, c'est du lourd. Clint Eastwood affine son mythe en pure économie de mouvements, mâchoire serrée sur son cigare, regard plissé sous le chapeau : du vrai aura farming qui fait le contrepoids parfait au reste du casting. Lee Van Cleef a un profil d'aigle, un port altier et un regard d'acier teinté de mélancolie et d'aristocratie, avec une autorité naturelle qui lui permet presque de voler la vedette. Gian Maria Volontè livre une performance fiévreuse, constamment sous l'emprise de la fumette avec ses rires sardoniques et ses folies meurtrières. Mention spéciale à la surprise de voir Klaus Kinski dans le rôle du bossu Wild ! Visuellement, Leone maîtrise ses très grands angles panoramiques dans le désert d'Almería, avec des coupes brutales vers des gros plans assez extrêmes sur les yeux, les fronts moites et les mains gantées. La musique d'Ennio Morricone vit à l'intérieur de l'histoire, complètement diégétique via la boîte à musique de la montre à gousset, véritable symbole du temps, de la mémoire et du trauma : quand la mélodie s'arrête, on sait que ça sent mauvais. Le climax final est un pur opéra, la caméra tournant autour des tireurs en suivant les montées chromatiques des trompettes et des cloches. Un très bon film, j'espère que Le Bon, la Brute et le Truand sera à la hauteur de celui-là.

texto: I just finished the second movie in the Dollars series and I gotta tell ya, it's way more complex and way more engaging than the first one. It honestly buries the first one, even if the first one is more iconic and more mainstream accessible. This one is just better written and better directed. (Plus, it's not a rip off of another movie...) Everyone kills it, Morricone is at his best working with Leone, and everything about this is just so fucking good. This makes me wanna be a cowboy outlaw, and I hate cowboys. This already made it in my favorite movies. Definitely top 100. There's not much to say here other than this was a fantastic trilogy and I am even more sad that Leone passed at the age that he did. We lost a colossal talent when we lost him. And considering he wanted to make an adaption of "Don Quixote" and that we never got one is one of the biggest, most heartbreaking losses of cinema tied with Kubrick's Napoleon. Now on to rewatch "The Good, The Bad, and the Ugly."

Morricone once again delivers a tremendous score, which peaks at the climax, where the motif of the chimes that haunt both Mortimer and Indio intertwine with guitar and horns to accentuate one of the best standoffs in cinema.

texto: For a Few Dollars More de Sergio Leone est un chef d’œuvre. Ce western met en scène deux chasseurs de prime amenés à se rencontrer et à partager la même mission. Ainsi, Manco et le colonel Mortimer mettrons en place plusieurs stratagèmes pour mettre la main sur El Indio, venant de s’évader de prison, ainsi que sa bande. Cette seconde réalisation pour la trilogie du Dollars est à mon sens la meilleure. On nous donne deux acteurs d’exemptions ( Clint Eastwood et Lee Van Cleef ) amenés a travailler ensemble contre El Indio ( joué par Gian María Volonté ). L’intrigue est très bonne et met en place un scénario super bien fondé. Ici, il sera beaucoup plus question de justice mais avec quelques contraste, Manco fait justice et s’enrichit tandis que Mortimer est à la recherche d’une réel justice. La Vengeance est ici le thème principal du film et il sera amenés au fur et à mesure avec des flashbacks. La mélodie de la montre est aussi un son iconique du film ainsi qu’un élément centrale du film. Beaucoup de scènes sont iconique et représentent énormément de chose, comme la scènes des chapeau qui n’est pas une scène de duels mais plutôt de démonstration pour savoir qui est le meilleur. Le film nous montre que la vengeance peut rapidement devenir une prison, Mortimer se venge mais le passé ne change pas, il n’obtiendra donc qu’une victoire amère.

texto: five minutes into this, clint eastwood is introduced in silhouette, riding into town in the dead of night in a storm. ennio morricone is pulling out his best whistler for the job. like it’s insane. i’m googling man with no name poncho immediately. and then it cuts to a close-up shot of eastwood, head bowed, hat brim covering his eyes, lighting a cigarillo and raising his head JUST AS A PEAL OF THUNDER HITS. i’m leant all the way forward. i’m moaning. i’m yowling. i’m going insane. it’s plainly the coolest thing i’ve ever seen. the next 2 hours is just cool scenes upon cool scenes (van cleef’s massive stupid revolver! “you have until the music stops to try”! eastwood’s little wave as he lights a stick of dynamite! “very careless of you old man - try this. now we start”!) that is ALMOST as cool as this minute of film. like it’s mad. he’s probably the coolest character ever created probably. he’s a fucking cowboy with a big gun and endless little cigars and a flare for the dramatic and a CAPE and he’s FUNNY he’s a CHEEKY little bugger he’s got a DASHING little vest i am obsessed with him good lord

texto: I just finished the second movie in the Dollars series and I gotta tell ya, it's way more complex and way more engaging than the first one. It honestly buries the first one, even if the first one is more iconic and more mainstream accessible. This one is just better written and better directed. (Plus, it's not a rip off of another movie...) Everyone kills it, Morricone is at his best working with Leone, and everything about this is just so fucking good. This makes me wanna be a cowboy outlaw, and I hate cowboys. This already made it in my favorite movies. Definitely top 100. There's not much to say here other than this was a fantastic trilogy and I am even more sad that Leone passed at the age that he did. We lost a colossal talent when we lost him. And considering he wanted to make an adaption of "Don Quixote" and that we never got one is one of the biggest, most heartbreaking losses of cinema tied with Kubrick's Napoleon. Now on to rewatch "The Good, The Bad, and the Ugly."

texto: For a Few Dollars More de Sergio Leone est un chef d’œuvre. Ce western met en scène deux chasseurs de prime amenés à se rencontrer et à partager la même mission. Ainsi, Manco et le colonel Mortimer mettrons en place plusieurs stratagèmes pour mettre la main sur El Indio, venant de s’évader de prison, ainsi que sa bande. Cette seconde réalisation pour la trilogie du Dollars est à mon sens la meilleure. On nous donne deux acteurs d’exemptions ( Clint Eastwood et Lee Van Cleef ) amenés a travailler ensemble contre El Indio ( joué par Gian María Volonté ). L’intrigue est très bonne et met en place un scénario super bien fondé. Ici, il sera beaucoup plus question de justice mais avec quelques contraste, Manco fait justice et s’enrichit tandis que Mortimer est à la recherche d’une réel justice. La Vengeance est ici le thème principal du film et il sera amenés au fur et à mesure avec des flashbacks. La mélodie de la montre est aussi un son iconique du film ainsi qu’un élément centrale du film. Beaucoup de scènes sont iconique et représentent énormément de chose, comme la scènes des chapeau qui n’est pas une scène de duels mais plutôt de démonstration pour savoir qui est le meilleur. Le film nous montre que la vengeance peut rapidement devenir une prison, Mortimer se venge mais le passé ne change pas, il n’obtiendra donc qu’une victoire amère.

texto: "Where life had no value, death, sometimes, had its price. That is why the bounty killers appeared." Even though it is widely considered and quite rightly so that The Good, the Bad and the Ugly is the best of the Dollars trilogy. For me my favourite of this trio hands down is this absolute masterpiece of cinema. Lee Van Cleef, Clint Eastwood, and Gian Maria Volonté exude extreme cool from the opening scenes to the climatic end duel, all of them bringing commanding performances. So many iconic shots, sequences, and lines of dialogue have fully imprinted themselves into my mind. Sergio Leoni was truly the master adapting Japanese cinema and here it's no less obvious in it brilliance and simplicity. The old school sound effects and Ennio Morricones iconic score permeating throughout is such a joy to the ears. I will never grow tired of watching this film, to me this is the iconic Western upon which all others must stand against.
