texto: Wow. I already thought the first one was great, but this is one hell of a step up. Genuinely a complete movie and one of the best westerns I've ever seen. The main reason being: it finally gets a notable side character, a memorable villain, and more complex / variable intentions among all parties. And the 'notable side character' arguably has just as much, if not more screen presence than Clint eastwood, which I never would've expected. Van cleef is fucking incredible in this movie and I couldn't believe someone could be more imposing than clint, in what is pretty much his film. Insane addition to the movie and changes everything about it. The contrast in their personalities and different approaches to the same problem that their characters make is so nice to watch, their dynamic is at its best with the hat shootout. And then you have indio and his gang, a memorable villain with a more nuanced backstory and intentions that always keep changing. It's a much better, more refined story that is less predictable yet easier to follow, and that's exactly what the first one was missing. The intro credits as usual are innovative and so cool. The cinematography is incredible, beautiful landscapes, stunning shot framing, insanely operatic showdowns and innovative camerawork. And the night sequences are especially stunning, I really mean it. Then you have the shootouts. It takes the showdowns of fistful of dollars to another level - longer, higher stakes, less predictable, and the score behind all of it elevates it to another level. One of the best western scores ever, and it is so essential to the movie here, it's incredible. I love how every character has his own sound motif, and the cherry ontop is the music box motif used so perfectly in the finale. The final showdown was just insane. As a whole, it's a complete movie that I can't fault in any way. It's decisively better than 'For a fistful of dollars', as good as it was. And after seeing 'The good, the bad and the ugly', I can confidently say that this one is the best of the 3. It's just got the formula totally nailed down, I see it as the perfect balance between the first and third movies - introducing the all-important van cleef, having a more nuanced story & memorable villain, yet retaining a more concise runtime, and not having to split the screentime across 3 main leads (I didn't like Wallach in TGTBTU that much). It's an amazing movie.

texto: ok so first and foremost yes i watched this because a man put it on for me. that is obvious. but let’s discuss this. ALL PERSONAL OPINIONS! the 2.5 hour runtime is no fucking joke here it absolutely feels like a 2.5 hour long movie. genuinely feels incredibly grating at times and truly does feel like a LONG movie. could be bad pacing issues, but could also certainly be because i don’t find this subject to be at all interesting. this is also made for a very specific type of person which is not me whatsoever, which i can usually find lots of enjoyment in films of that nature but for this one, i feel it is hard to feel connected to the story if you are not already interested in cars/racing. for someone like me who has little to no interest in either subject, it is extremely hard to digest and comes across as very boring during all of the scenes that are not either the business plotline or ken’s family’s plotline. car go fast vrroom!! is not interesting on its own without prior knowledge for someone like me. as for the things i did like about this movie, i felt as though it was quite well made! this is a very good film on a technical aspect, with very good sound, colouring, shots etc. and i liked the soundtrack! big fan of 60s. 2.5 stars, not for me at all, but could understand why someone would really like it.

texto: ok so first and foremost yes i watched this because a man put it on for me. that is obvious. but let’s discuss this. ALL PERSONAL OPINIONS! the 2.5 hour runtime is no fucking joke here it absolutely feels like a 2.5 hour long movie. genuinely feels incredibly grating at times and truly does feel like a LONG movie. could be bad pacing issues, but could also certainly be because i don’t find this subject to be at all interesting. this is also made for a very specific type of person which is not me whatsoever, which i can usually find lots of enjoyment in films of that nature but for this one, i feel it is hard to feel connected to the story if you are not already interested in cars/racing. for someone like me who has little to no interest in either subject, it is extremely hard to digest and comes across as very boring during all of the scenes that are not either the business plotline or ken’s family’s plotline. car go fast vrroom!! is not interesting on its own without prior knowledge for someone like me. as for the things i did like about this movie, i felt as though it was quite well made! this is a very good film on a technical aspect, with very good sound, colouring, shots etc. and i liked the soundtrack! big fan of 60s. 2.5 stars, not for me at all, but could understand why someone would really like it.

texto: There are 2 main things that the movie does not explain which limits my ability to care or get invested in the outcome of the movie. 1: Why Ferrari? The movie is Ford v Ferrari but they are barely mentioned at all, and are more a vague boogyman rather than an actual competitor or villian. They get bought by Fiat, and they are basically never mentioned or seen again till the end of the film. 2: What's the deal with Le Mans over any other race? They explained why the track is different the other race tracks, but never got me to understand why its more important than the Sebring or the Daytona. Even the movie puts more stakes on the Daytona race. There's a ton of plot how a big automobile companies treat both their workers and their racers, which is well done, and that should have been the focus of the movie if they weren't going to answer my uncultured questions.

texto: “Giddy-up! Giddy-up!” Yes, he says that. I swear on my life. Go ahead—watch this 2h 30m movie to try and prove me wrong. He actually says it FIVE times WHY is Christian Bale in EVERYTHING? This is not the kind of actor I usually consider to be “in everything,” and he certainly isn’t in ME, but here he is—voice of Howl, Batman for some mf reason, The Bride—I just Googled it, WHERE is he in LITTLE WOMEN???? SHAFT?????? NEWSIES??????? He lowkey pulls a Zendaya here. Like, good job, Chrissy (I DO know him like that), but you’re still Christian Bale and you are Patrick Bateman and that’s about it. Wrap it up. I mean, he’s good, really good, but him being British here ticks me off. Okay, I came out swinging and I have to say that I WANTED TO LIKE this movie!! It took me a second, but I realized I was actually pretty entertained despite being critical of pretty much everything while I was watching it. Like, I was WATCHING CARS on a SCREEN. I was gonna give it a 3 or a 3.5. What kind of sad chick am I that I’m saying “I like this movie! THREE!”? Ignore. But anyway, I was gonna give it that rating because, y’know, there were a couple really pretty shots, but the cinematography TO ME was eh, and also…the characters are lowkey buns. I thought this even before the Great Rating Drop of 2026. The longer we went through the movie, the more I saw distinct personalities, so THAT was good. But, y’know, the ONE female character was horrid. Mollie? Bro, the most “woman written by a man” character ever. “I know you’re covered in oil, but I’m in a pretty dress—you want to crack open a beer and dance and play some music?” To quote my buddy Alex, “Get the hell out.” To quote me complaining about this movie to my buddy Cam (I’m committing so many sins by not indenting per quote, I’m sorry to all the kids whose homework I did on IXL in seventh grade), “I don’t care if my man’s covered in oil, that’s kinda hot, but I feel like that’s not the average POV.” It’s giving male fantasy, it’s giving beer ad, and I’m the woker for this and I DO NOT CARE! Mollie has a whole scene where she’s leaning against the doorway while Ken (CBale) is talking to his son before bed, and she’s looking all longingly…WHAT ARE WE DOING? Oh my God, or when CBale and Matt Damon’s characters are getting into a tussle, and she’s like “Are you boys done fighting😉?” And one of them is GENUINELY like “get me a soda? [🇬🇧]” and she’s all “okaaaaay~! <3” ?????? ?? ???? Dog what is this. ALSO she has this moment when she’s like “I don’t want you to go out there driving again!! It’s dangerous!!” Son SHUT UP I’ve SEEN this movie with buttcheeks gulag (The Courier) and it STILL PMO. GET JESSIE BUCKLEY IN HERE🗣️🗣️!! Jessie Buckley? Christian Bale? Is this Cine2Nerdle, because that’s The Bride! Wow! I’m still mad, you can’t distract me. Anyway, I was still gonna give it a three. But. Okay, it feels like I watched a Moviedle of a different movie at the end. A different movie? A different review? I still have to write, like, twelve. Whatever. Here. New quote! “My main goal is to blow up and act like I don’t know nobody.” This ending PISSED ME OFF!! It has been over a MONTH and I STILL REMEMBER!! Spoiler warning? No shit. But this is actually a pretty big twist (because it makes no sense) so if you ever want to watch it and fully get the experience, you should have stopped reading a minute ago, because your peripheral vision is probably already picking up the spoiler. I am STILL mad, you STILL cannot distract me STILL. Okay, not the twist, but if you’ve seen this movie, you know what I was alluding to a second ago. Let’s start here: Christian Bale has shown NO indication—yes, he drives for the love of the game, the money’s cool, but it’s not about the money—that he would EVER slow down. WHYYYY would he slow down? And then the loss makes you feel awful, because you just watched a 2.5 hour movie to see them lose. “Maybe that was the point.” “That’s how life is.” It’s been a LONG time since I used that quote when talking about a movie that did pretty pointless emo shit! I know it’s based on an actual race, so they’re not going to change the outcome, but you are rewriting a man’s life and you can’t make this make sense SOMEWHERE in those 2.5 hours? And the DEATH was framed like ABSOLUTE dogwater! Anthony and I kept joking “any minute now” and yukking up about characters blowing up, so it was actually crazy when it happened—in fact, I LIKED how it was shot and done! Having it in the last ten minutes makes it even more shocking…but then, y’know, past the shock, what are you going to do in the last ten minutes? If we want to do the dramatic/sad route, end on Bale getting his shit blown smoove off. Don’t make me think I’m gonna get Damon/Mollie on some Vance/Erika shite or…try to fit in some sort of message? It felt weird. That’s all. I sound remarkably mad about a movie I gave two stars, but I was peeved. Was I entertained? Regrettably, absolutely. You win this round.

texto: Ford v Ferrari is essentially a $100 million superhero movie where the capes are made of grease and Italian leather. The roar of the GT40 and the kinetic chemistry between Damon and Bale is cliche.  I wanted some depth, but I found myself idling. Between the cartoonishly evil corporate villains and a family subplot that feels like it was written by an algorithm, the film frequently veers into by-the-numbers territory. It’s a stalled ride.

I know it’s based on an actual race, so they’re not going to change the outcome, but you are rewriting a man’s life and you can’t make this make sense SOMEWHERE in those 2.5 hours? And the DEATH was framed like ABSOLUTE dogwater! Anthony and I kept joking “any minute now” and yukking up about characters blowing up, so it was actually crazy when it happened—in fact, I LIKED how it was shot and done! Having it in the last ten minutes makes it even more shocking…but then, y’know, past the shock, what are you going to do in the last ten minutes? If we want to do the dramatic/sad route, end on Bale getting his shit blown smoove off. Don’t make me think I’m gonna get Damon/Mollie on some Vance/Erika shite or…try to fit in some sort of message? It felt weird. That’s all. I sound remarkably mad about a movie I gave two stars, but I was peeved. Was I entertained? Regrettably, absolutely. You win this round.

texto: EN If you loved Cars as a child, this is the perfect adult alternative to experience that exact same vibe. The title is actually misleading: the battle with Ferrari is mostly about Ford's ego after a failed partnership attempt. The real, secondary conflict in the film is the one fought by individual talents against the bureaucratic Ford corporation, where image matters more than passion. Just like the iconic GT40, the film runs exceptionally smooth when it comes to pacing. It offers an accessible style of storytelling combined with a very strong cinematographic vision. Even though I know nothing about cars and have zero interest in them, the story kept me engaged from start to finish thanks to the human relationships. The chemistry between Damon and Bale is fantastic, their friendship feels so authentic that they almost seem like brothers at times. You can tell it's a very American story, in which Ferrari and the Italians are portrayed as fairly headstrong and arrogant to create a sharp contrast, to get that typical American underdog feeling. Furthermore, the racing sequence at the end drags on quite a bit and you occasionally see a lot of repetitive footage, but thanks to the rock-solid editing, the tension remains palpable throughout. NL Als je vroeger als kind van Cars hield, is dit het perfecte alternatief voor volwassenen om diezelfde vibe te ervaren. De titel is eigenlijk misleidend: de strijd met Ferrari draait vooral om een ego van Ford nadat een poging tot partnerschap mislukte. De échte, tweede strijd in de film is die van de individuele talenten tegen het bureaucratische Ford-concern, waar imago belangrijker is dan passie. Net zoals de iconische GT40 loopt de film qua pacing ontzettend soepel. Het is een toegankelijke manier van storytelling, gecombineerd met een hele sterke cinematografische visie. Hoewel ik zelf niets van auto's ken en het me niet interesseert, bleef het verhaal me van begin tot eind boeien door de menselijke relaties. De chemie tussen Damon en Bale is fantastisch, hun vriendschap voelt oprecht dat het soms net broers lijken. Je merkt wel dat het een heel Amerikaans verhaal is waarin Ferrari en de Italianen vrij eigenzinnig en arrogant worden neergezet om een dik contrast te creëren, zo ontstaat er ook een typische Amerikaanse underdog gevoel. Daarnaast duurt het racegedeelte op het einde vrij lang en zie je soms veel van dezelfde beelden, maar door de ijzersterke montage blijft de spanning er toch steeds inzitten.

tema: Comparação com outros filmes de guerra
exemplo: Este grupo compara o filme com outras produções de guerra, como Apocalypse Now e Full Metal Jacket, considerando-o inferior ou menos complexo, apesar de reconhecer sua importância histórica.
texto: Even if I feel I'm interested in Vietnam's conflict, I feel like Vietnam's movies are not my type of movie. Needless to say, I can acknowledge that Full Metal Jacket is a great work due to features such as the following ones: - The first part of the film really hits, with the "Sir, yes, Sir" the whole time, the strict routine, and an overwhelming ambience that just catches you in the terror of America. Because the first part is not about Vietnam, but rather about the wickedness of the US (something that also appears in the second half of the film). The stupidity of the conflict is already there, and the last scene, the one where private Pyle spits the now classic "full. metal. jacket.", is great proof of the fact that Americans themselves, in their style of life, cultivated their own defeat – a defeat that, however, has still not arrived neither for them nor us, although its appearance is starting to accelerate. Moving, true, critical, but nothing new – and that's sort of my delusion with all Vietnam's films, including Coppola's. - Still, I think that Kurick's message, although typical and too much spoon-fed, gets straight to the point, and his analysis is spot on. The moment where the soldiers start wondering the reasons for the civilizating mission in Vietnam, they say something like, "We are here to give them freedom, but they do not seem to want it" alongside the "we're killing them in order for them to be free. I don't know. I would prefer to be free rather than dead" it's fantastic. However, Kubrick's point about stupidity and irreflexivity (also, carrying the "born to kill" alongside the sign of peace) goes further, and points at the American contradiction of creating monsters (first part, in the island) while expecting them to only obliterate the enemy – when the only real enemy was themselves. - Even if Kubrick and Coppola's films are critical of the American gaze on the Vietnam War, they are so American-centered. Both films are about American soldiers, without even considering the Vietnamese point of view of the conflict – but rather the American point of view of the Vietnamese point of view. Needless to say, I'm not claiming that Kubrick and Coppola should have done a Vietnamese-centered movie: they are American. Still, the complaint is more about the winners of the narrative: while America arguably lost Vietnam, they even appropriated their own narrative on how badly they lost it. It's not by chance that when one thinks of Vietnam films, everyone thinks of the two mentioned before, and none of the Vietnamese films are counted in that list. Americans are even capable to capitalize their defeats, and to create a narrative of them being the losers which makes them effectively the winners of the narrative. As I stated before, it might be due to the "critical, obvious and american" nature of the critique that I'm not really into Vietnam movies. However, I enjoyed the film, and being able to see it in a cinema room was a great chance that no one should waste.

texto: أكثر ما أُعجبني في هذا الفيلم هو عدم إظهار الجنود الأمريكيين كملائكة أو جالبين للحرية وداحضين للشيوعية، بل أظهرهم كما فعلوا تاريخياً: قتل للمدنيين بلا أي استثناء وعدم اهتمام. بالإضافة إلى النصف الأول من الفيلم (أول خمسين دقيقة) في معسكر التدريب، كان نصفاً مثيراً نفسياً بحق، وصادماً بنهايته، وذا أداء تمثيلي مميز من إيرمي على وجه الخصوص، وأيضاً لم أتوقع هكذا بداية في فيلم لكوبريك، فعادةً ما تكون بداية أفلامه بطيئة، لكن هنا لم أأشعر بالوقت. وأما بالنصف الثاني فهنا الفيلم يتحول لعمل قاسٍ غير مكترث بالمشاعر وهذا متوقع نسبياً نظراً لكونه فيلم حرب. وأما بقية الأحداث فليست بالأمر الجلل، أحداث فيلم حرب تقليدية. وأغرب ما في الفيلم هي الموسيقى، لا تدري ما موقعها في فيلم كهذا، تشعر وكأنها موسيقى فيلم كوميدي وليست موسيقى فيلم حرب. آخر قولي عنه: عمل جيد، يستحق المشاهدة لمرة واحدة ككل ولأكثر من مرة لنصفه الأول، محايد في محتواه، أداء تمثيلي ممتاز ككل، ليس مضيعة للوقت.

texto: I saw it as a teen and thought, like everyone I knew, that the first part was incredible and the second part dropped off considerably. I was determined this go round to enjoy both parts equally. It didn't go well. The first 40 minutes is about as good as cinema can get. Pretty much every emotion one is capable of feeling comes out at some point. Laughter, anger, sadness. They are all provided in large quantities. But once they go off to war, it has to restart and rebuild momentum and, even with the addition of the always perfectly cast Adam Baldwin, it just never does.

texto: Stanley Kubrick makes this film feel lopsided and disappointing. The opening act at the training camp, following Joker and Pyle's story, is actually quite well done  but it drags on far too long, eating up nearly half the film's runtime. What's most disappointing is the lack of a truly tense atmosphere once the story moves to the Vietnam War itself. Instead of capturing the atmosphere so distinct to Vietnam dense jungle and Viet Cong style traps  Kubrick opts for an urban setting instead, pitting the soldiers against skilled Viet Cong snipers. It ends up feeling more like watching a war against Nazi Germany in Europe than a guerrilla war in Vietnam..

texto: This is my 3rd out of 5 Kubrick movies I've seen that I did not enjoy. I'm sure almost everyone has the same thought that the first half of the movie was more enjoyable. That entire scene with Pyle, that is is something I will NEVER forget. Absolutely insane. It's not that the second half was bad, however, I think it's just the timing of seeing this film. If I had been alive to see it when it was released, I am almost positive that I would have been blown away, rating it 5 stars. But so many war movies have come out since then and there's just nothing insanely special. I guess I'm glad I watched it. Maybe I'll come to like it a little better over time after thinking about it, the characters and dialogue were really good as well.

texto: Full Metal Jacket is one of those classics that I really wanted to love... and I can see why people do, but it just didn't fully land for me. The first half, the boot camp section, is undeniably strong technically, but it dragged for me in a way I wasn't expecting. At around 25 minutes in, I realised I hadn't heard a single line of dialogue that wasn't screamed at someone. It's effective at building that atmosphere of dehumanisation, sure, but after a while, the constant intensity started to flatten out for me rather than build. The second half is almost entirely a different film, and it's good, but it feels strangely detached. I get that this is probably intentional, mirroring the characters' own numbness and disconnection, but knowing that intellectually didn't make it hit any harder emotionally. It's the kind of film I respect more than I connected with.

texto: Сюжет: фільм умовно поділений на дві частини - навчання солдат із іконічними сценами(командир, який чмирить усіх, на всіх оре і т.д.) та їх участь у війні. До першої частини питань немає, іноді було нуднувато. Друга частина це піздєц. Я постійно кімарив, що відбувається - незрозуміло. Ця частина показує, що війна це не те, що уявляють про неї солдати. Війна це постійний абсурд та смерті і в цьому немає сенсу(в контексті війни у в'єтнамі це можливо, я особисто в цій історичній темі не шарю). Але це не робить фільм крутим, це нецікаво абсолютно. Битви нецікаві(хоч і, можливо, реалістичні), смертей небагато, як для війни. Кінцівка якийсь крінж, задумка хуйня імхо. Персонажі: прикольний командир, Лоуренс запам'ятався, але не в хорошому сенсі. Дуже багато схожих зовнішньо персонажів + в них військова форма однакова, додає незрозумілості, що відбувається Візуал: для військового фільму непогано, але, на мою думку, не вистачає жестяка. Вердикт: такий собі фільм, задум хуйня якась, скучний. Це уже третій фільм Кубрика, який я дивлюсь і мені знову не подобається його сенс. Але окрім хуйового сенсу, це ще й нудно. Перша частина дійсно непогана, були великі очікування після неї, але все обісралось

texto: Full Metal Jacket فیلمنامهٔ Full Metal Jacket برای من از همان ابتدا با یک مشکل اساسی روبه‌روست: فیلم به دو بخش کاملاً جدا تقسیم می‌شود؛ بخش آموزش تفنگداران و بخش ویتنام و جنگ. این دو بخش برای من ارتباط ارگانیکی با یکدیگر پیدا نمی‌کنند و فیلم نمی‌تواند این دو قسمت را به یک اثر منسجم تبدیل کند. بخش اول قابل‌تحمل‌تر است و حتی تنش میان شخصیت پایل و فرمانده، یعنی هارتمن، تا حدی جذابیت دارد، اما بخش دوم برای من تقریباً کاملاً شکست‌خورده است. در بخش اول، با وجود اینکه موقعیت آموزش نظامی قابلیت ایجاد تنش دارد، شخصیت‌ها بیشتر تیپ هستند تا انسان‌های واقعی. سربازها، فرمانده‌ها و حتی شخصیت جوکر بیشتر برای انتقال ایده‌های فیلم ساخته شده‌اند. دیالوگ‌ها هم اغلب کلیشه‌ای، تکراری و شعاری‌اند. جوکر قرار است با دیالوگ‌های فلسفی و نگاه متفاوتش شخصیت عمیق‌تری پیدا کند، اما برای من این عمق بیشتر در دیالوگ‌ها بیان می‌شود تا اینکه در رفتار و شخصیت او دیده شود. در نتیجه شخصیت‌ها بیشتر ابزار ایدهٔ فیلم هستند تا آدم‌هایی که بتوانیم واقعاً با آن‌ها ارتباط برقرار کنیم. با این حال، بخش اول حداقل یک تنش قابل‌قبول دارد؛ مخصوصاً رابطهٔ پایل و هارتمن. این بخش نسبت به نیمهٔ دوم بسیار بهتر عمل می‌کند و حداقل یک مسیر تنش مشخص دارد، هرچند شخصیت‌پردازی همچنان کلیشه‌ای است و این نقطهٔ قوت هم نمی‌تواند مشکلات فیلمنامه را کاملاً جبران کند. اما با ورود فیلم به ویتنام، برای من تقریباً همه‌چیز فرو می‌ریزد. بخش دوم نه جنگ را باورپذیر نشان می‌دهد، نه از نظر شخصیت‌پردازی جذاب است و نه از نظر روایت ارتباطی با بخش اول پیدا می‌کند. صحنه‌های جنگی برای من نه واقع‌گرایانه‌اند، نه درد و خشونت واقعی جنگ را منتقل می‌کنند و نه تنش قابل‌توجهی دارند. احساس کردم کوبریک در این بخش اصلاً نمی‌تواند جنگ را به‌عنوان یک تجربهٔ انسانی به تصویر بکشد. تصویری که فیلم از ویتنامی‌ها ارائه می‌دهد هم برای من یکی از مشکلات جدی فیلم است. زنان ویتنامی عمدتاً یا در قالب شخصیت‌های جنسی و فاحشه‌گونه ظاهر می‌شوند یا تحقیر می‌شوند و این نگاه، جهان فیلم را بسیار سطحی می‌کند. در نتیجه فیلم نه‌تنها تجربهٔ ویتنامی‌ها را جدی نمی‌گیرد، بلکه تصویری کلیشه‌ای و تحقیرآمیز از آن‌ها ارائه می‌دهد. در مقابل، آمریکایی‌ها هم به شکلی اغراق‌شده و غیرانسانی تصویر می‌شوند؛ انسان‌هایی که به ماشین‌های کشتار تبدیل شده‌اند و دیگر راهی برای بازگشت ندارند. بنابراین برای من هیچ‌کدام از دو طرف به شخصیت‌هایی واقعی و انسانی تبدیل نمی‌شوند. به همین دلیل حتی اگر بخواهیم فیلم را دربارهٔ «تبدیل انسان به ماشین جنگی» بدانیم، احساس می‌کنم خود فیلم در اجرای این ایده موفق نیست. این فرایند بیشتر با دیالوگ و رفتارهای کلیشه‌ای به ما گفته می‌شود تا اینکه به شکل عمیق و انسانی تجربه‌اش کنیم. فیلم به جای اینکه این تغییر را در روان شخصیت‌ها به ما نشان دهد، بیشتر آن را به‌عنوان یک ایده مطرح می‌کند. کارگردانی کوبریک هم برای من برخلاف انتظار، نتوانسته این مشکلات را جبران کند. دوربین در بخش جنگی برای من نه حس واقع‌گرایی ایجاد می‌کند و نه درد و وحشت جنگ را منتقل می‌کند. به نظرم جنگ در فیلم بیش از حد شبیه یک نمایش ساخته‌شده است و همین باعث شده نتوانم آن را جدی بگیرم. برای من جنگ در این فیلم بیشتر شبیه یک شوخی بصری است تا یک تجربهٔ هولناک انسانی. حتی میزانسن و فضاسازی ویتنام هم نتوانسته این حس را ایجاد کند؛ محیط ویتنام برای من به اندازهٔ کافی زنده، واقعی و باورپذیر نیست. در بخش آموزشی، میزانسن و کارگردانی قابل‌تحمل‌تر هستند، چون فضای بسته و منظم آموزش نظامی با ساختار فیلم هماهنگ‌تر است. اما در نیمهٔ دوم، همان ویژگی‌ها دیگر جواب نمی‌دهند و فیلم از نظر بصری برای من جذابیت چندانی ندارد. موسیقی هم برای من نقطهٔ قوتی نیست. استفاده از موسیقی پاپ، برخلاف موسیقی‌ای که بتواند به فضای جنگ یا شخصیت‌ها عمق احساسی بدهد، تأثیر احساسی خاصی برای من ایجاد نکرد. موسیقی بیشتر بخشی از فضای فیلم است تا عنصری که واقعاً به احساس یا تنش آن کمک کند. تدوین هم یکی از مشکلات ساختاری فیلم است. مهم‌ترین مسئله این است که نیمهٔ دوم نه‌تنها ادامهٔ طبیعی نیمهٔ اول نیست، بلکه انگار فیلم دیگری را شروع می‌کند. این گسست باعث می‌شود ساختار دو بخشی فیلم برای من بیشتر یک ضعف باشد تا یک انتخاب روایی موفق. در مجموع، Full Metal Jacket برای من نه یک اثر ضدجنگ موفق است و نه اثری موفق دربارهٔ تبدیل انسان به ماشین جنگی. بخش اول، مخصوصاً تنش میان سرباز چاق و هارتمن، قابل‌تحمل‌تر و جذاب‌تر است، اما شخصیت‌ها همچنان تیپیک و کلیشه‌ای هستند. بخش دوم اما برای من تقریباً در تمام زمینه‌ها Completely void of emotion or depth as has been the case with all the Kubrick movies I've seen. Half the performances are bad, again, as has been the case with all of them. texto: Full Metal Jacket is one of those classics that I really wanted to love... and I can see why people do, but it just didn't fully land for me. The first half, the boot camp section, is undeniably strong technically, but it dragged for me in a way I wasn't expecting. At around 25 minutes in, I realised I hadn't heard a single line of dialogue that wasn't screamed at someone. It's effective at building that atmosphere of dehumanisation, sure, but after a while, the constant intensity started to flatten out for me rather than build. The second half is almost entirely a different film, and it's good, but it feels strangely detached. I get that this is probably intentional, mirroring the characters' own numbness and disconnection, but knowing that intellectually didn't make it hit any harder emotionally. It's the kind of film I respect more than I connected with.

باورپذیر نیست. در بخش آموزشی، میزانسن و کارگردانی قابل‌تحمل‌تر هستند، چون فضای بسته و منظم آموزش نظامی با ساختار فیلم هماهنگ‌تر است. اما در نیمهٔ دوم، همان ویژگی‌ها دیگر جواب نمی‌دهند و فیلم از نظر بصری برای من جذابیت چندانی ندارد. موسیقی هم برای من نقطهٔ قوتی نیست. استفاده از موسیقی پاپ، برخلاف موسیقی‌ای که بتواند به فضای جنگ یا شخصیت‌ها عمق احساسی بدهد، تأثیر احساسی خاصی برای من ایجاد نکرد. موسیقی بیشتر بخشی از فضای فیلم است تا عنصری که واقعاً به احساس یا تنش آن کمک کند. تدوین هم یکی از مشکلات ساختاری فیلم است. مهم‌ترین مسئله این است که نیمهٔ دوم نه‌تنها ادامهٔ طبیعی نیمهٔ اول نیست، بلکه انگار فیلم دیگری را شروع می‌کند. این گسست باعث می‌شود ساختار دو بخشی فیلم برای من بیشتر یک ضعف باشد تا یک انتخاب روایی موفق. در مجموع، Full Metal Jacket برای من نه یک اثر ضدجنگ موفق است و نه اثری موفق من ارتباط ارگانیکی با یکدیگر پیدا نمی‌کنند و فیلم نمی‌تواند این دو قسمت را به یک اثر منسجم تبدیل کند. بخش اول قابل‌تحمل‌تر است و حتی تنش میان شخصیت پایل و فرمانده، یعنی هارتمن، تا حدی جذابیت دارد، اما بخش دوم برای من تقریباً کاملاً شکست‌خورده است. در بخش اول، با وجود اینکه موقعیت آموزش نظامی قابلیت ایجاد تنش دارد، شخصیت‌ها بیشتر تیپ هستند تا انسان‌های واقعی. سربازها، فرمانده‌ها و حتی شخصیت جوکر بیشتر برای انتقال ایده‌های فیلم ساخته شده‌اند. دیالوگ‌ها هم اغلب کلیشه‌ای، تکراری و شعاری‌اند. جوکر قرار است با دیالوگ‌های فلسفی و نگاه متفاوتش شخصیت عمیق‌تری پیدا کند، اما برای من این عمق بیشتر در دیالوگ‌ها بیان می‌شود تا اینکه در رفتار و شخصیت او دیده شود. در نتیجه شخصیت‌ها بیشتر ابزار ایدهٔ فیلم هستند تا آدم‌هایی که بتوانیم واقعاً با آن‌ها ارتباط برقرار کنیم. با این حال، بخش اول حداقل یک تنش قابل‌قبول دارد؛ مخصوصاً رابطهٔ پایل و هارتمن. این بخش نسبت به نیمهٔ دوم بسیار بهتر عمل می‌کند و حداقل یک مسیر تنش مشخص دارد، هرچند شخصیت‌پردازی همچنان کلیشه‌ای است و این نقطهٔ قوت هم نمی‌تواند مشکلات فیلمنامه را کاملاً جبران کند. اما با ورود فیلم به ویتنام، برای من تقریباً همه‌چیز فرو می‌ریزد. بخش دوم نه جنگ را باورپذیر نشان می‌دهد، نه از نظر شخصیت‌پردازی جذاب است و نه از نظر روایت ارتباطی با بخش اول پیدا می‌کند. صحنه‌های جنگی برای من نه واقع‌گرایانه‌اند، نه درد و خشونت واقعی جنگ را منتقل می‌کنند و نه تنش قابل‌توجهی دارند. احساس کردم کوبریک در این بخش اصلاً نمی‌تواند جنگ را به‌عنوان یک تجربهٔ انسانی به تصویر بکشد. تصویری که فیلم از ویتنامی‌ها ارائه می‌دهد هم برای من یکی از مشکلات جدی فیلم است. زنان ویتنامی عمدتاً یا در قالب شخصیت‌های جنسی و فاحشه‌گونه ظاهر می‌شوند یا تحقیر می‌شوند و این نگاه، جهان فیلم را بسیار سطحی می‌کند. در نتیجه فیلم نه‌تنها تجربهٔ ویتنامی‌ها را جدی نمی‌گیرد، بلکه تصویری کلیشه‌ای و تحقیرآمیز از آن‌ها ارائه می‌دهد. در مقابل، آمریکایی‌ها هم به شکلی اغراق‌شده و غیرانسانی تصویر می‌شوند؛ انسان‌هایی که به ماشین‌های کشتار تبدیل شده‌اند و دیگر راهی برای بازگشت ندارند. بنابراین برای من هیچ‌کدام از دو طرف به شخصیت‌هایی واقعی و انسانی تبدیل نمی‌شوند. به همین دلیل texto: Amazing look at the futility of war using a famously futile one. Acts of horrendous magnitude are constantly justified, and the hypocrisy of the American invasion is constantly staring you in the face through Joker’s helmet/pin combo. War turns basic morality into treason, and if you do not bend to its whims, you will break, your humanity and individuality be damned. I need to look into how this entire movie was filmed, as it is nothing short of magnificent on a technical level.

texto: Amazing look at the futility of war using a famously futile one. Acts of horrendous magnitude are constantly justified, and the hypocrisy of the American invasion is constantly staring you in the face through Joker’s helmet/pin combo. War turns basic morality into treason, and if you do not bend to its whims, you will break, your humanity and individuality be damned. I need to look into how this entire movie was filmed, as it is nothing short of magnificent on a technical level.

texto: Full Metal Jacket is another Kubrick movie where I think the reputation is completely justified. It’s brutal, darkly funny, emotionally cold, and remarkably controlled. If A Clockwork Orange asks whether the state can take away someone’s free will in the name of creating a better person, Full Metal Jacket asks a related question: What happens when an institution deliberately destroys your humanity because it believes that will make you better at killing? Kubrick’s answer is basically: you may become very good at killing but something inside you has already died.

texto: sean porter’s crisp, polished cinematography paints a rich, nostalgic portrait of 1960s america, wrapping the journey in warm tones and elegant period framing that instantly signals prestige filmmaking. every frame is calculated for maximum audience accessibility, capturing the shifting American landscape from sleek urban nightscapes to vintage southern estates with smooth camera movements and flawless lighting. you can see exactly why this swept the academy awards, as the glossy visual finish combines effortlessly with a crowd-pleasing, classic narrative structure that hits every emotional beat with reliable precision. the plot functions as a classic study in defensive compartmentalisation and boundary breakdown between two completely contrasting personalities. don shirley guards his emotional vulnerability behind rigid posture, refined speech, and intellectual superiority to cope with the extreme isolation of being accepted by neither white elite circles nor his own community. conversely, tony lip relies on hyper-masculine bravado and unrefined pragmatism to mask his narrow worldview. as their physical journey south progresses, the forced proximity chips away at their respective psychological armour, forcing tony to confront his latent prejudices while don is pushed to strip away his loneliness and allow genuine human connection to break through his isolated facade.

Green Book is constantly trying to stir it's audience with it's glib angle that "the black guy is a virtuosic and cultured intellect and the white guy is a blue collar schlub who is in a sense closer to black culture than he is" but that can only work if you maintain the very same narrow and old-fashioned view of blackness it purports to wag it's finger at while simultaneously playing to and culturing in it's audience. texto: Um filme que fala de um pianista negro bom pra caralho nos anos 60. O filme, de fato, é sobre ele? Não, é sobre o motorista branco racista, que aparentemente deixou de ser racista quando passa o filme inteiro. Adivinha? Sendo racista e passando pano pra racista. O filme tenta até  avançar um pouco a “crítica”, mas recua, e fica um grande poço que não é nada profundo. Apesar de ser uma história real, o filme usa a história do Dr. Shirley apenas como base, para enaltecer o Tony, o grande salvador. Não é à toa que a produção foi também feita pelo filho do próprio. A única coisa boa nesse filme é a atuação do Mahershala Ali, que ganhou o Oscar como ator coadjuvante pelo filme. Sim, o filme não é sobre o personagem dele, o que é bem escroto. Esse filme ter ganhado o Oscar de Melhor Filme é loucura.

texto: This movie is genuinely so bad. Like insane to think that the thesis to a period piece about racism is a steven universe-esque "Everyone Can Be Kind, You Just Have To Look For It". REALLY victim-blamey overall ??? Generally the whole premise is "What if a white person was an uncivilized savage and a black person was..... smart ??? and clean ???" The director clearly thinks this is subversive, implying that he assumes the opposite to be the default. Obviously this adds a new undertone that what actually makes someone gross and violent is being poor. A couple notable scenes in the movie : - Don is forced by Tony to eat fried chicken. He says "no" at first, repulsed by the idea of adhering to a stereotype, but ends up caving in and enjoying it. This scene is meant to be comedic and heartwarming, mostly at Don's expense, for even daring to refuse fried chicken. - Don and Tony get stopped by a white police officer while getting home, making the former very anxious, due to his past misadventures with racist cops. However, this one is just plain nice, as Not All Cops Are Bastards, wishes them a Merry Christmas and lets them go. In summary, this movie is insanely racist, and makes blatantly false assumptions about racism in the 60s. It treats racism as an individual rather than systemic problem : you are expected to accept racism as an unchangeable truth of the world in order to engage with this piece. I'd give zero stars if I could.

texto: The idea that “we should love one another because it’s Christmas” isn’t a message. It really could have been a truly important, truly meaningful film, but in the end, they didn’t want to make it that way. I really regret that. It’s a clichéd, boring story—despite its theme and surface, it’s a colorful, lively comedy that seems to be downright afraid to delve deeper into a social problem that is indeed important and still very much present today, and for that very reason, it’s an experience you can safely skip. If you’re interested in the topic of racism, I can wholeheartedly recommend the film *The Hate U Give*, which, - although it doesn't delve nearly as deeply into the subject as it should - conveys a much richer and more thought-provoking message.

tema: Falta de profundidade e de respeito à história real
exemplo: Este grupo destaca que o filme não honra a história real do pianista Don Shirley, reduzindo sua trajetória e o que ele representou para um papel secundário, e que a produção ignorou ou distorceu fatos importantes da vida do personagem.
texto: On the one hand, yes, the acting is great, you’ve got Viggo Mortensen, who very rarely turns in a bad performance and is very selective when it comes to picking the right script to work on and knowing if he can make something good come out of it which he does here, and Mahershala Ali, what more do I even need to say about him that he hasn’t done already, he’s a fantastic actor and in the years since he gained a bigger spotlight he’s got Curious Case Of Benjamin Button, Predators, Hunger Games: Mockingjay, Moonlight, Hidden Figures, True Detecitve season 3, Spider-Man: Into The Spiderverse, even his channeled Wesley Snipes performance in Alita: Battle Angel was great, this guy is a fantastic actor and rightfully deserved to win Best Supporting Actor this year. If anything these two guys are the reason why the film is salvageable. But other than that, everything else about this movie is just bland and forgettable. For one thing, it’s a bad sign in the family of the person you’re making the movie off of had no idea they were even making the film without them knowing. Yeah, no joke, Shirley’s relatives condemned the film, stating that they were not contacted by studio representatives until after development, and that it misrepresented Shirley’s relationship with his family. Don’s brother Maurice Shirley said, “My brother never considered Tony to be his ‘friend’; he was an employee, his chauffeur (who resented wearing a uniform and cap). This is why context and nuance are so important. The fact that a successful, well-to-do black artist would employ domestics that did NOT look like him, should not be lost in translation.” Mahershala Ali responded with an apology to Shirley’s nephew Edwin Shirley III, saying that “I did the best I could with the material I had” and that he was not aware that there were “close relatives with whom I could have consulted to add some nuance to the character”. Writer-director Peter Farrelly said that he was under the impression that there “weren’t a lot of family members” still alive, that they did not take major liberties with the story, and that relatives of whom he was aware had been invited to a private screening for friends and family. Nick Vallelonga, Vallelonga’s son, acknowledged that members of the Shirley family were hurt that he did not speak to them, and that he was sorry that they were offended. He told Variety that “Don Shirley himself told me not to speak to anyone” and that Shirley “approved what I put in and didn’t put in.” That’s already a bad sign right out of the gate. Another problem the movie has is that follows the white savior stereotype/cliché. Peter Farrelly told Entertainment Weekly that he was aware of the white savior trope before filming and sought to avoid it. He said he had long discussions with the actors and producers on the point, and believes that it was not advanced by the film, saying it is “about two guys who were complete opposites and found a common ground, and it’s not one guy saving the other. It’s both saving each other and pulling each other into some place where they could bond and form a lifetime friendship.” New York Times writer Wesley Morris characterized Green Book as being a “racial reconciliation fantasy”. Morris argues that the film represents a specific style of racial storytelling “in which the wheels of interracial friendship are greased by employment, in which prolonged exposure to the black half of the duo enhances the humanity of his white, frequently racist counterpart”. Writing in The Hollywood Reporter, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar noted that “filmmakers are history’s interpreters, not its chroniclers.” Because when I think of somebody trying to avoid falling into clichés, it’s Peter Farrelly, whose last big directing contribution to the world was the shitpile that was Movie 43….oops. But let’s get down to the real reason why this movie does not work at all, it’s fucking Driving Miss Daisy all over again, just reverse the races, make Jessica Lange Mahershala Ali and make Morgan Freeman Viggo Mortensen and bang, it’s pretty much the same movie, there is nothing clever or unique about this movie. It’s just an Oscar bait film, the same typical Oscar bait film that we’ve been trying to get rid of for years now, and the worst part about all of this is that there was a far superior Oscar bait film that got completely snubbed this year and that was A Star Is Born, that was an example of an Oscar bait movie done 100% right avoiding a lot of the tropes and clichés and creating new twists and turns with it to create not only a great movie but one of the best movies of last year….and it got completely snubbed at the Oscars only winning 1 of its’ 8 nominations while Green Book got 3. While Green Book doesn’t level my complete anger at winning Best Picture for a lackluster movie like The King’s Speech did in 2010, the fact that Green Book won the Best Picture proves that no matter how much the Oscars thinks it’s changing its’ course and getting its’ shit together, they’re still stuck in the past by letting generic shit like this winning the top prize and trying to make people think that this was the definitive movie of the year. Green Book is just an bore of a film, I really tried to give it a fair shot but I’m sorry, this is one of the dullest and blandest Best Picture winners ever, other than Mortensen and Ali, the rest of the movie is just a forgettable lump, it’s just a bore, a bore of a film that doesn’t work at all.

texto: I didn’t like it bc mostly of the content was kinda cringe, didn’t seem realistic at all, and the whole racial ideology was a bit off, those outdated white saviour tropes and it just seemed like the underlining point of the movie was to show that not all white people are racist. It’s an absolute shocker the amount that this film got awarded at the Oscar’s, the fact that they won screenplay for a well below average screenplay, and best picture is insane. Viggo and Mahershala were both nominated as well, and I felt significantly underwhelmed and unmoved by both their performances. I really thought this was a bad film, but I can see some entertainment value if your an old person wanting to watch a somewhat heartwarming story. Honestly there are some positives, some of it is shot really well and with the screenplays countless attempts to be funny, I genuinely laughed a couple times, although I think they did try way too hard. There are some smart people I know that told me this was good, and I am disappointed in them.

texto: This movie’s commentary on blackness is thinner than a piece of paper, and its understanding of racism in America is incredibly cartoonish. That said, Mahershala Ali takes this surface-level material about racial and sexual identity and attempts to translate it with some nuance. Viggo Mortensen is also quite funny. Other than that, the dialogue is laughable and I really dislike the score. Visually, it’s fine. I liked the piano playing. It’s occasionally wholesome, but its charming nature is more or less stamped by its excessive sentimentality. As a whole, whatever.

But let’s get down to the real reason why this movie does not work at all, it’s fucking Driving Miss Daisy all over again, just reverse the races, make Jessica Lange Mahershala Ali and make Morgan Freeman Viggo Mortensen and bang, it’s pretty much the same movie, there is nothing clever or unique about this movie. It’s just an Oscar bait film, the same typical Oscar bait film that we’ve been trying to get rid of for years now, and the worst part about all of this is that there was a far superior Oscar bait film that got completely snubbed this year and that was A Star Is Born, that was an example of an Oscar bait movie done 100% right avoiding a lot of the tropes and clichés and creating new twists and turns with it to create not only a great movie but one of the best movies of last year….and it got completely snubbed at the Oscars only winning 1 of its’ 8 nominations while Green Book got 3. While Green Book doesn’t level my complete anger at winning Best Picture for a lackluster movie like The King’s Speech did in 2010, the fact that Green Book won the Best Picture proves that no matter how much the Oscars thinks it’s changing its’ course and getting its’ shit together, they’re still stuck in the past by letting generic shit like this winning the top prize and trying to make people think that this was the definitive movie of the year. Green Book is just an bore of a film, I really tried to give it a fair shot but I’m sorry, this is one of the dullest and blandest Best Picture winners ever, other than Mortensen and Ali, the rest of the movie is just a forgettable lump, it’s just a bore, a bore of a film that doesn’t work at all.

texto: okay donc Ron & Hermione c'est vraiment un SLOOOOW burn mdr edit : j'avais oublié de l'écrire, mais j'étais trauma de l'illusion où Harry & Hermione se galochent à moitié à poil devant Ron 💀 niveau plot, c'était bien mais j'en attendais un peu plus, je voulais plus d'action, plus d'avancées dans leur enquête, etc. je suppose qu'il marche bien en préparation pour le film final, mais en tant que standalone movie, c'est comme pour The Order Of The Phoenix, j'étais pas vraiment à fond, et un peu déçue. texto: This one is definitely better than the last, but still holds my issue of it being dark, grey and miserable the entire time. (Legit couldn’t see anything half the time cause it’s so damn dark) I know it’s the dark ages or whatever but there’s literally 2 ‘happy’ scenes. Bill’s wedding (the beginning bit) and the dance scene which was perfect I’m standing more with Ron and Hermione in this one they really do seem cute together and it doesn’t seem forced especially if it’s been going on since the fifth movie. For a long ass movie, I saw the time click to an hour and I thought ‘where has that time gone’ Like literally nothing happens for an hour they’re just trying to keep them all long as fuck for continuity I don’t get how everyone’s protesting for dobbys grave (a fictional cgi elf) to not get interrupted by wire or whatever. Like he’s not real. He’s barely in the movies anyway. Also annoying as fuck and so ‘look at dobby, dobby is so innocent and cute’ shut up let the poor labour workers put that damn wire in. That little animated visual for the story was so gorgeous, Tim burton Corpse Bride inspired. Really wish there was more of that. The brown was really needed after all the grey. Literally every British actor is in Harry Potter I swear. What do you mean fucking Kurt Conners and Vecna is in this?

The film has a post-apocalyptic atmosphere whilst focusing on the interactions between the characters, bringing their frustrations and conflicts to the fore. texto: Deux heures à démêler l'histoire. Ils ont coupé un livre en deux, et cette première partie récupère tout ce qui n'est pas spectaculaire : la fuite, l'errance, les campements, les disputes. texto: C’est non. Je l’ai vu juste après avoir lu le livre. Je suis super déçue, ils ne ressemblent en AUCUN CAS au livre ! Ils ont enlevé l’essentiel ! Il y a TOUTE UNE SCÈNE au ministère qui est juste PRIMORDIALE et qui nous fait comprendre que tout part en couille, que cést littéralement la 2nd Guerre Mondiale, qui n’a pas été mise; ou encore que des gens détestent Kreattur alors qu’il est (pour moi) l’un des meilleurs perso les plus touchant et le plus gentil !! ILS L’ONT SALI !!!!! Mais surtout la scène de Remus et Harry qui se dispute n’a pas été mise alors que c’est a ce moment là que l’on se rend compte qu’il a un PTN DE FILS !!!!!! Sérieux, vous arrivez à comprendre l’histoire les gens qui n’ont jamais lu le livre, franchement je vous dois le respect ! Me dites pas que vous avez compris tout ce que faisait Voldemort ?? Les films Harry Potter, c’est vraiment de pire en pire… Sachez que ça me brise le cœur de dire ça… vraiment… c’est MON cinéma à moi🥲 C’est surtout que ça change du premier qui est juste majestueux, et qui est une copie conforme du livre ! Mais quoi qu’il se passe je serais toujours attaché à ces films et ces livres pour des raisons évidentes ! Par contre la scène avec Hermione et Harry qui danse a été la meilleure chose rajouter dans ce film, ptn j’ai chialé alors que j’ai passé tout le film à me plaindre parce que ça ne ressemblait pas au livre ! (Petite pensée pour Mag d’ailleurs, elle m’a subit tout le long du film) J’en avais gros sur la patate, my bad pour cette dissert 😌

texto: Echoooo echooo echoo echoo... Oh look, it's empty, there's nothing in this movie. 2 hours of wandering around the woods carrying the rin- horcrux, that makes its wearer go mad. I didn't remember much about this movie and now I know why: there is nothing to be remembered about it. Endless static shot reverse-shot dialogue scenes. Characters walking from point A to point B in silence and with no music. If there was a plot I already forgot it again. I don't think I've used the phrase "waste of time" in any of my reviews, but this was a waste of time. I kept waiting for anything interesting to happen and it never came. There is no way that the two parter ending is justified, based on this movie. Further evidence that Hogwarts is what makes Harry Potter good. This isn't more "mature", it's just boring.

tema: Roteiro fraco e falta de plot
exemplo: Este grupo aponta que a história parece se perder em detalhes secundários, com uma trama pouco envolvente e momentos em que a narrativa se interrompe ou muda de direção de forma abrupta.
texto: This was probably a hard book to adapt, but their approach doesn't do it any favors. Some scenes are very literally translated to screen, with tons of exposition and explanation between them removed. I feel like we get the worst of both worlds here. Lots of wandering around aimlessly in the woods and bickering, without the benefit of a compelling mystery (which even the book didn't convincingly sell). Perhaps the worst part is the acting. Almost everyone looks bored at this point, and they're given only the most banal dialogue to keep the plot moving. You'd hardly believe these kids are supposed to be best friends of six years. The depiction of magic here is also quite uninspiring; wands are basically just guns.

texto: I just hate what they’ve done with Ron throughout the series he’s gone from my favorite character in the first movie to the absolute most annoying, headache inducing person whenever he’s on screen. Whining, complaining, being jealous, every second he’s on screen is excruciating and exhausting to watch. And what’s with Ron disappearing for a whole ass month? And he just comes back 20 minutes later like nothing happened. The dance with Harry and Hermione was just so incredibly awkward, the whole movie just feels like a slog. This movie was 2 and a half hours but it felt like 4. I also get that the movie is supposed to have a somber mood and depressing mood but god man everything is so gray and uninteresting to look at. The whole movie just feels like an exposition dump and I wanted to turn the movie off the whole time.

texto: I remember this being the “boring one” (and likewise the portion of the book it covers). That assessment was perhaps a little misguided. On rewatch I actually enjoyed the slower pace. The studio’s decision to split the last book into two movies may have been a financial one, but it works out for the best, artistically speaking. texto: People who say they don't like this one because its boring or there isn't any action is CRAZY. This one is literal nonstop action for 2.5hrs?? I've never understood that critique. And I LOVE LOVE LOVE the Tale of Three Brother’s animation (another thing people complain about). Also Scabior is so hot in this!!! What's not to love?? "THESE ARE DARK TIMES THERE IS NO DENYING." I love Bill Nighy's voice lol Another great opening. It is TRAGIC showing Hermione obliviate her parents, and that song is one of the best in the whole series too. Following that with Snape's entrance: Alan Rickman in these final movies is just INCREDIBLE. His fabulous entrance, and his FACE. It breaks me. I love the seven Harrys scene. The polyjuice moment is hilarious, the Hedwig death is shocking and devastating, and then the moment with Voldemort (literally “flying death”) is brilliant! I love his anger bursting out of him when Malfoy's wand doesn't work like expected. The naked snogging vision from the horcrux is wildddd. Still jarring to this day. Not giving us the Peter Pettigrew death was criminal. The whole mirror situation must be so confusing to anyone who didnt read the books. That little shard of glass that is never explained with a random old man staring back and then sending Dobby? This needed to be done wayyy better or should've been scrapped entirely. The Bellatrix knife throw in slow-mo is orgasmic to me. Sad the knife ended up in Dobby, of course. That final scene with Voldemort though!! What a FANTASTIC way to end part 1. (Obviously a money grab, but they did it all so damn well.)

texto: i have no qualms with the premise that humans have been mistreating a species for centuries because they assumed its hostility. in fact, i like it, and i find it particularly creative for a kids movie. where this film goes wrong for me is the characterization. Hiccup’s father is the classic, obstinate parent who shows no affection for his son until Hiccup saves the vikings’ lives. This characterization irks me because at that point his father is just hopping on the bandwagon. It’s like cheering for the Yankees- ok, cool, you support something obviously supportable. the character arc only works if his father shows him affection prior to him proving himself, which doesn’t occur. Astrid doesn’t work for me either, because she is giving no backstory. I have no idea why she has an all consuming thirst to kill dragons, she just comes off as rude to Hiccup for no reason but blind competitiveness. however, as my dad pointed out, this movie is going to make for a great ride at universal

texto: i have no qualms with the premise that humans have been mistreating a species for centuries because they assumed its hostility. in fact, i like it, and i find it particularly creative for a kids movie. where this film goes wrong for me is the characterization. Hiccup’s father is the classic, obstinate parent who shows no affection for his son until Hiccup saves the vikings’ lives. This characterization irks me because at that point his father is just hopping on the bandwagon. It’s like cheering for the Yankees- ok, cool, you support something obviously supportable. the character arc only works if his father shows him affection prior to him proving himself, which doesn’t occur. Astrid doesn’t work for me either, because she is giving no backstory. I have no idea why she has an all consuming thirst to kill dragons, she just comes off as rude to Hiccup for no reason but blind competitiveness. however, as my dad pointed out, this movie is going to make for a great ride at universal

texto: I LOVED this book in primary school, but the movie coming out when I was hitting puberty was exactly the wrong time for me to give a shit about it. Better late than never. Watching it now, I don't remember the book being such a generic hero's journey template. Just the basic synopsis and knowing it's Dreamworks is enough to predict the whole thing beat by beat with zero surprises. Not a fair criticism for a kids movie perhaps, but knowing how fresh and original the source material was I'm very underwhelmed. For an original IP I'd have been more lenient. Disliked the voice acting a lot, Hiccup's actor especially... so nasal and obviously a grown ass adult putting on a kid's voice. Very strange mix of Scottish and American accents to portray the Vikings. Why not get, I dunno, the Skarsgard family to do some hammy Scandinavian accents instead? Not a fan of the dragon designs either, way too cartoony. Straight out of Rayman. Even for a kids movie they could have been scarier and more realistic to raise the stakes a bit. The music was banging though, I'll give it that. The test drive scene choked me up so some magic is certainly there, but it's too by-the-numbers for me overall.

texto: En fin de compte, je crois que c'est un film qu'on a beaucoup trop mis sur un piédestal alors qu'il faut être honnête et se l'avouer...c'est pas si ouf. Alors oui, c'est divertissant. Les 1h30 passe à une vitesse folle, tout est fait pour que tu passes un bon moment devant. L'esthétique est efficace, le montage s'arrête jamais de bout en bout. Et puis, vu que c'est des dragons....................je pense qu'on y est tous très sensibles, c'est sûrement la créature fantastique la plus fantasmé et ce pour une raison : les dragons, c'est cool. L'oeuvre réussit à nous investir émotionnellement, clairement. On est prit par les personnages, on se prend d'affection pour certains, on se met à en détester d'autres,...donc je dirais que ça marche bien. Enfin, les designs dans leur ensemble sont bien foutus, que ce soit au niveau des dragons comme des personnages, tout fonctionne. Donc, ça parait être vraiment bien ce que je raconte, alors pourquoi je l'adore pas ? Parce que c'est un film basique. Et je suis désolé hein, mais tout fonctionne, sans que rien ne soit nouveau. Dans tout les points forts que j'ai émis, tout est ok, tout marche, sans vraiment réussir non plus. Et c'est là que pour moi le film a été un échec, c'est qu'il n'a jamais réussit à me surprendre, à m'étonner. Il est simple, straightforward et ne cherche jamais à nous donner plus que ce qu'on à déjà reçu. Ça répond simplement à nos attentes, sans aller plus loin. Que ce soit visuellement ou narrativement, ça reste très plat. Les couleurs sont sympas sans sortir de l'ordinaire, le travail sur les lumières, pareil et l'histoire va droit au but, avec un dynamisme presqu'un peu trop prononcé. Alors oui, c'est un bon script, oui l'animation est très bien, mais moi ça ne me suffit pas pour y voir un grand film d'animation américain. Selon moi, ça reste une oeuvre qui fait pale figure à côté d'un Chat Potté 2 par exemple. Ça c'est un grand film d'animation américain qui pousse son concept, qui impressionne en mêlant 3D et 2D, utilisant des petits moments de musique hyper intense mais qui sait aussi utiliser son drame avec un message beau et puissant. Y'a des moments plus lent, stressant, bref c'est un vrai roller coaster qui ne se laisse pas emporter par son scénario mais qui comprend les enjeux de l'oeuvre. Ça, c'est fort, ça c'est beau. Bref, c'était mignon, sympa, j'ai passé un bon moment, mais j'y vois pas un grand film.

texto: I will forever love this movie; it's just so good and easily one of the best animated movies I've seen. The animation, the story, the characters, everything about this movie is beautiful. It’s such an enjoyable film, and getting to watch dragons will always be fascinating to me. I adore Hiccup and Toothless's bond; it is so pure and one of the most beautiful, unique friendships in cinema. It serves as a perfect example of the movie's most important theme: tearing down prejudice. I found it so brilliant how the story uses humans and dragons to teach us that we shouldn't let prejudice or fear dictate our perspective of others who seem different from us. Getting to watch Hiccup and Toothless's friendship slowly grow and get stronger is absolutely fantastic. We see Hiccup genuinely getting curious about Toothless, beginning to study him and get to know him from a more empathetic and understanding perspective, instead of just seeing him as something to kill like the other Vikings do. I love that it's a very universal message that we can all learn from, kids and adults alike. The soundtrack is a must-mention when talking about this movie because it is just so good. It's one of my favorites, and the track "Test Drive" always gives me chills when I listen to it. Of course, the sequence itself is also amazing to watch, but the soundtrack definitely elevates it to being truly epic and iconic. Toothless is just so cute and awesome, really mades wish to ride a dragon This movie made me love dragons, and it will forever hold a special place in my heart. “I wouldn’t kill him, because he looked as frightened as I was. I looked at him… and I saw myself” “Stop trying so hard to be something you’re not!” “Thank you for nothing You useless reptile.” 😭 🐉🔥￼

texto: How to Train Your Dragon is such a nostalgic movie! Watching it as an adult took me back to my childhood summers spent lazing around, watching one movie after the other. I love this movie because it reminds you that taking the unconventional path might be slightly harder, but it is far more rewarding in the end. It also reminds you that you never have to be alone and that there will always be people to support you. No matter how crazy your idea is, you have to find the right people. The unique relationship between Hiccup and Toothless pulls you in, making you wish that you had your own pet dragon. Overall, the movie is sweet and a must-watch for anyone looking to spend a cosy Sunday afternoon reminiscing your childhood.

texto: I’m gonna start a “series” of rewatching movies from are/ my childhood after watching the KF trilogy And now the next rewatch “How to train your dragon” I’ll be honest I only remember the 2nd movie with the mum and the dad reuniting with the scene “your as beautiful as the day I lost you” So rewatching this will be quite refreshing. _ Actual review: (Writing whislt watching) Holy hell Stoick hand some hands on him punching up the dragon was pretty cool. Gobber is funny af proper unc vibe too him and gives great fatherly advice too stoick. Hiccup not being able too kill the night fury is a lovely classical display of empathy from are main character and you already know I’m a sucker for that sort of thing. Hiccup and Stoic reminds me of the relationship I have with my dad and idk if I’ll leave this but think of it as a lil crumble of Insight into my personal life. Goobers voice sounds so familiar and I can’t put a name on it? Also fishlegs is ADORBALE, I will die protecting him. I like the fact they establish very early on hiccups keen observation and innovation skills rather than it just coming up when convenient. Ruffnut and Tuffnut are sucha iconic duo Will say quite surprising Hiccup hasn’t read the dragon manual yet? Maybe he has and I didn’t pick up on it in a earlier scene. Hiccup being THIS incompetent is starting too any me too I won’t lie, I say that but I’d probably be snotlout in the training exercises, blaming the sun and all. It not cat why cat shaped? Also TOOTHLESS that’s his name, god it was bugging me I couldn’t remember, toothless and hiccups first meeting is adorable. Also Toothless would be a great Cat name, I already have a army of strays I’ve adopted so I guess I’ll just anoint one the name. HICCUP PETTING TOOTHLESS WAS ADORABLE Hiccup making the back wing and then flying was 10/10, very good display of both there personalities. I love hiccup applying his experience with the smoked eel too training session along with his other experiences with Toothless. Stoic and Hiccup slowly getting closer is heartwarming but also heartbreaking considering there on 2 sides of a different coin I can’t wait for the reveal of hiccups secret too pay off. Also is the elder hiccups grandma? Or just the eldest person on the island? Astrid being the first too find out is great considering how much she hated or held distain for hiccup. Also I wonder when or how hiccup will loose his leg? Considering how much of a bond hiccup and toothless share. I love how willing and firm hiccup is on protecting toothless, standing his ground and how accepting Asstrid is of that. Also??? Why does he have a WOODEN shield when facing a dragon on fire??? No wonder why the Viking’s have been loosing for so long??? Toothless coming in for the save was sick, toothless is a real G. DONT THEY DARE HURT MY SCALEY BOY??? DONT HOLD HIM DOWN LIKE THAT YOU BASTARDS. Stoics and hiccups dialogue was heartbreaking, damn that hit hard, very happy with the way it played out but damn that was sad… Also why take the risk of putting a nightfury on a boat when you could just put the tiny green ones?? Ik the Vickings are brutes but are there forearms as thick as there skulls?? But I’ll give em the benefit of the doubt for being smart enough too use a dragon as a compass but also ya really wanna enter a place known as a “dragons nest” “First too ride one though” - fucking bars Stoic must have the biggest balls in that village cuz I would of been swimming the fuck away after seeing 3 of those fuckers. Also is it just me or does the animation pick up in the 3rd act? The animation looks stunning TRAINING GANG IS HERE! What a sick entry and also hiccup displaying his tactical mind was also sick Side note I’m realising I use the words “sick” and “also” a fair amount Stoic saving toothless was a great character development moment and him apologising was emotional. I wasn’t feeling the OST in earlier scenes but now it’s really hittin hard. THE VILLAGE LOVES DRAGONS, HICCUP IS A HERO AND BELOVED WHAT GREAT GOD DAMN ENDING, GOD THAT WAS WHOLESOME.

texto: The difference in energy between Vol.1 and Vol.2 is pretty huge. This is really a movie that should be watched back-to-back, Vol.1 followed immediately by Vol.2. The two films are designed to create an overall rise and fall in energy, so watching them separately makes that difference in tone work against your expectations. In that sense, I almost wish they had released the whole thing as one sprawling, deeply idiosyncratic epic rather than splitting it into two volumes. Vol.2 is almost an epilogue, with a lot more explanation and exposition, and it has very little of the roller-coaster, jukebox-like exhilaration of Vol.1. Still, the parts that parody the techniques and conventions of kung fu movies made me grin. I loved the feeling of, “Yes! That’s exactly the bit you should be picking up on.”

texto: What I like about Tarantino films is how quirky and fun they are. Kill Bill: Volume One is a perfect example of that. The slower pace and emotional style of Volume Two would, in principle, be ideal in brining a closure to his story. But why don't we really get to understand what Beatrice has been through? You'd expect to really emphasise with her, especially on in a more slow-burner style sequel. It was still a blast, but not as full of energy as the first and wasn't thought evoking enough for it to need to be as long winded as it was. I actually enjoy slower films but there wasn't enough to contemplate in my opinion.

texto: Vol.2 felt like a downgrade from the first movie. The first half of the movie was quite boring and disappointing. It was hard to believe that the bride who dodged O-ren Ishii and Gogo, was the same person to just go head on with that alcoholic. The final encounter initially was emotionally touching but ended up being unsatisfactory, as there wasn't much action with the final dude before the secret technique. Also I wanted the bride to kill that alcoholic herself so bad, his demise felt lacking as the whole point was for the bride to get her revenge.  Building on that, why was there not a single scene of her cutting off names from the list (tsk tsk tsk). Moreover, the character background for Beatrix felt incomplete, too many unanswered questions about her past, hence a Vol.3 of Beatrix facing Nikki and  us getting a better understanding of her throughout would have been so badass.

texto: Вторая часть (хотя это скорее продолжение) Убить Билла меня немного разочаровала. В начале я бы, правда, хотел отметить несколько моментов, которые мне понравились. Прежде всего это эпизод обучения у мастера Пэй Мэя. Фактически это собирательный образ всех кунг-фу-фильмов, особенно той их части, где главный герой проходит обучение у мастера и постепенно познаёт мастерство определённого боевого искусства. Отдельно хочется отметить работу со звуком: звуки ударов, диалоги и даже шумы окружающей среды очень точно передают атмосферу старых гонконгских боевиков. Здесь же хорошо заметно главное отличие двух частей. Если в первой преобладает эстетика японского кино — самурайских фильмов и классических фильмов о мечах, — то во второй Тарантино гораздо сильнее обращается к традициям гонконгского кунг-фу. Понравился и финальный разговор Беатрикс с Биллом, в котором наконец проясняются некоторые моменты, оставшиеся непонятными раньше. При этом Тарантино снова использует свой любимый приём — рассказывает историю нелинейно, перемещаясь между разными моментами времени и постепенно складывая события в единую картину. Однако разочаровавших меня моментов оказалось больше. Во-первых, остальные участники банды Билла кажутся какими-то невзрачными и недостаточно проработанными. Единственной действительно запоминающейся для меня остаётся О-Рен Исии: мы понимаем, откуда она пришла, что сформировало её характер и почему она стала такой, какой мы её видим. Да даже про её телохранительницу Гого нам рассказывают больше, чем про Верниту Грин — первую жертву Беатрикс, которая погибает практически сразу после появления в фильме. Во-вторых, мне показалась странной логика поведения самих убийц. Все они позиционируются как профессиональные и крайне опасные бойцы, но при этом совершают поступки, которые выглядят совершенно нелогично. Зачем Бадд скрывает, что меч остался у него? Зачем Элли Драйвер вообще нужен меч Хаттори Хандзо? И зачем Бадд даёт Беатрикс фонарик в гробу, фактически помогая ей выбраться? В какой-то момент возникает ощущение, что персонажи действуют не как профессиональные убийцы, а так, как нужно сюжету для следующей сцены. И, наконец, я так и не понял, зачем вообще было разделять эту историю на два фильма. Для меня это не две самостоятельные части и даже не две логические главы одной истории это один фильм, искусственно разделённый пополам. Если бы в первой части мы увидели начало и конец истории, а вторая раскрывала бы события между ними, объясняя то, что осталось за кадром, такое решение имело бы для меня гораздо больше смысла. Здесь же я не почувствовал, что у каждой части есть собственная драматургическая функция. В итоге Убить Билла 2 это фильм, который, безусловно, стоит посмотреть, особенно если понравилась первая часть. Но лично для меня он работает скорее как необходимое продолжение, позволяющее закончить начатую историю, чем как фильм, который хочется пересматривать сам по себе.

texto: The difference in energy between Vol.1 and Vol.2 is pretty huge. This is really a movie that should be watched back-to-back, Vol.1 followed immediately by Vol.2. The two films are designed to create an overall rise and fall in energy, so watching them separately makes that difference in tone work against your expectations. In that sense, I almost wish they had released the whole thing as one sprawling, deeply idiosyncratic epic rather than splitting it into two volumes. Vol.2 is almost an epilogue, with a lot more explanation and exposition, and it has very little of the roller-coaster, jukebox-like exhilaration of Vol.1. Still, the parts that parody the techniques and conventions of kung fu movies made me grin. I loved the feeling of, “Yes! That’s exactly the bit you should be picking up on.”

texto: The difference in energy between Vol.1 and Vol.2 is pretty huge. This is really a movie that should be watched back-to-back, Vol.1 followed immediately by Vol.2. The two films are designed to create an overall rise and fall in energy, so watching them separately makes that difference in tone work against your expectations. In that sense, I almost wish they had released the whole thing as one sprawling, deeply idiosyncratic epic rather than splitting it into two volumes. Vol.2 is almost an epilogue, with a lot more explanation and exposition, and it has very little of the roller-coaster, jukebox-like exhilaration of Vol.1. Still, the parts that parody the techniques and conventions of kung fu movies made me grin. I loved the feeling of, “Yes! That’s exactly the bit you should be picking up on.”

texto: Gostei pra caralho desse aqui. Acho interessante como o Volume 2 é um pouco diferente do Volume 1, mas ainda consegue manter a mesma essência. Enquanto o primeiro é mais focado nas lutas e na violência, esse aqui já dá mais espaço para o desenvolvimento dos personagens, principalmente da Noiva e do Bill. Gostei de como exploraram melhor o passado dos personagens, explicando um pouco mais de como era a relação da Noiva com o Bill e também mostrando um pouco do treinamento que a Noiva teve com o Pai Mei. A parte final do filme me surpreendeu bastante. Acho que é porque eu tava com uma expectativa muito alta de que ia ser uma luta bem longa entre os dois, mas, por mais surpresa que eu tenha ficado, achei interessante eles terem focado em algo mais pessoal. Com os dois conversando e relembrando o passado antes de ela aplicar a técnica dos cinco pontos pra matar ele. Mesmo sendo uma cena simples e rápida, foi marcante. E o final dela com a filhinha dela é bonitinho. Enfim, eu amei os dois filmes. O primeiro me ganhou pelas cenas de luta e pela estética, e o segundo, pela história e pelo desenvolvimento dos personagens.

texto: Without completely discarding the relentless frenzy of violence from Vol. 1 , Kill Bill: Vol. 2 presents a radically different approach to the narrative. And personally—I'll just say this up front—I enjoyed this second part even more than the first. The continuation of arguably the most famous revenge plot in cinema history dials it down a notch to embrace a darker, slower, and dialogue-heavy tone. Tarantino shifts away from a nod to martial arts cinema toward a full homage to the Spaghetti Western, something he achieves through high-tension close-ups, wide shots of desert landscapes, and a soundtrack featuring the legendary Ennio Morricone and Riz Ortolani. This is probably the reason I liked Vol. 2 more; Western tropes are a weakness of mine, and Tarantino executes them flawlessly. The final scenes between Bill and The Bride are simply masterful. David Carradine makes the Superman monologue truly hypnotic, and the anti-climatic resolution of Bill’s death—an oasis of peace lasting just five steps—is the perfect closure for a story that has barely let you breathe.

texto: Gostei pra caralho desse aqui. Acho interessante como o Volume 2 é um pouco diferente do Volume 1, mas ainda consegue manter a mesma essência. Enquanto o primeiro é mais focado nas lutas e na violência, esse aqui já dá mais espaço para o desenvolvimento dos personagens, principalmente da Noiva e do Bill. Gostei de como exploraram melhor o passado dos personagens, explicando um pouco mais de como era a relação da Noiva com o Bill e também mostrando um pouco do treinamento que a Noiva teve com o Pai Mei. A parte final do filme me surpreendeu bastante. Acho que é porque eu tava com uma expectativa muito alta de que ia ser uma luta bem longa entre os dois, mas, por mais surpresa que eu tenha ficado, achei interessante eles terem focado em algo mais pessoal. Com os dois conversando e relembrando o passado antes de ela aplicar a técnica dos cinco pontos pra matar ele. Mesmo sendo uma cena simples e rápida, foi marcante. E o final dela com a filhinha dela é bonitinho. Enfim, eu amei os dois filmes. O primeiro me ganhou pelas cenas de luta e pela estética, e o segundo, pela história e pelo desenvolvimento dos personagens.

texto: Very good Film! I think it's best to view Kill Bill as one film but I thought best to watch both volumes individually. Both Reviews will be quite similar, parts will be copy and pasted. Uma Thurman kills (pun intended) it as the lead who goes by many names. Led by vengeance, this machine of human destruction shows little to no mercy against those who wronged her and those who stand in her way. This volume is more character based I'd argue?  Learning more of her and others' backstories as well as diving into the relationship between Bill and The Bride. Cast does very good! Especially Uma as mentioned but David Carradine's Bill may steal the show for some which is completely understandable, his presence alone demands a blend of fear and respect, he comes across as a silver tongued silver fox, almost masking his dangerous personality, almost. Plot paid off very well for me. Emotional at times and almost every character is justifiable in their own twisted ways. Fight scenes are a showcase of brutal creativity in the best ways. Can be a bit gory but in a fun way. I can easily understand if anyone has this as their favourite Tarantino. Some uncomfortable shots lingering on feet but not his worst case of forcing them into scenes. Would definitely watch again! Perhaps The Whole Bloody Affair for an end to end experience.
