texto: Project X si rivela una discreta commedia adolescenziale costruita con l'efficace espediente del falso documentario. Al di là della componente comica, il film propone una critica agli eccessi della gioventù e al bisogno quasi ossessivo di ottenere accettazione e popolarità. La gigantesca festa, dominata da alcol, droga e sesso, diventa così il simbolo di una ribellione adolescenziale destinata a sfuggire completamente di mano. La scelta di alternare riprese con telecamera a mano, cellulari e dashcam rende il racconto dinamico e immersivo, trasmettendo allo spettatore il progressivo deterioramento della situazione e la perdita di controllo dei protagonisti. È proprio attraverso questo caos crescente che il film racconta le conseguenze della ricerca esasperata di approvazione sociale. Il finale, volutamente sopra le righe, risulta forse fin troppo esagerato e poco credibile, ma si inserisce perfettamente nel tono folle e irriverente dell'opera. Nel complesso, Project X è una commedia divertente e coinvolgente che, dietro la sua leggerezza, riesce anche a offrire qualche spunto di riflessione sugli eccessi e sulle fragilità dell'adolescenza.

texto: Much like the party that Costa throws for Tommy, Project X seems determined to be the big, explosive, definitive conclusion to the “one crazy party” sub-genre of comedy. It has everything that could possibly excite a heterosexual teenage boy in the early 2010s – alcohol, drugs, boobs, stunts, implied sex, and everything in between. And for the most part, its mission is successful; later movies that delve into this sandbox, like Office Christmas Party , don’t quite have their hearts in the same place, and it comes off feeling more tired than energetic. My feelings on Project X are actually pretty similar to Office Christmas Party – the debauchery is hardly engaging, and since that’s what the whole film is supposedly barreling towards, it has to be pretty compelling to break through. At least Project X has the excuse of solely focusing on the party. I am not exaggerating when I say there is nothing more to this film than the insanity and excess that comes from an out-of-control hormonal rager. Most of the characters are irredeemably annoying, but that’s nothing new for a film of this caliber. Their values (which, as far as I can tell, bear little difference from the movie as a whole) feel antiquated, even for 2012. It may have intentionally provided an apex (which, in turn, may have killed the sub-genre), but that doesn’t quite dovetail with the quality of the movie itself, as hard as it tries to make itself stand out. It doesn’t matter how cool you were or weren’t in high school; the shenanigans in Project X are more exhausting than anything else.

texto: Much like the party that Costa throws for Tommy, Project X seems determined to be the big, explosive, definitive conclusion to the “one crazy party” sub-genre of comedy. It has everything that could possibly excite a heterosexual teenage boy in the early 2010s – alcohol, drugs, boobs, stunts, implied sex, and everything in between. And for the most part, its mission is successful; later movies that delve into this sandbox, like Office Christmas Party , don’t quite have their hearts in the same place, and it comes off feeling more tired than energetic. My feelings on Project X are actually pretty similar to Office Christmas Party – the debauchery is hardly engaging, and since that’s what the whole film is supposedly barreling towards, it has to be pretty compelling to break through. At least Project X has the excuse of solely focusing on the party. I am not exaggerating when I say there is nothing more to this film than the insanity and excess that comes from an out-of-control hormonal rager. Most of the characters are irredeemably annoying, but that’s nothing new for a film of this caliber. Their values (which, as far as I can tell, bear little difference from the movie as a whole) feel antiquated, even for 2012. It may have intentionally provided an apex (which, in turn, may have killed the sub-genre), but that doesn’t quite dovetail with the quality of the movie itself, as hard as it tries to make itself stand out. It doesn’t matter how cool you were or weren’t in high school; the shenanigans in Project X are more exhausting than anything else.

texto: I’m probably incapable of being objective about this one, but no film captures the absolute worst of late-2000s high-school culture better than Project X . It takes the kind of house-party disaster that used to become national news and turns up the stupidity, damage and excess until it basically becomes a disaster movie . Everything about it is problematic, and almost none of it feels impossible. That soundtrack still turns up in clubs, and even the original screenings became improvised parties the second “ Pursuit of Happiness ” kicked in. I lived those nights, and I still get to relive them through this film. 🔥

texto: Kişisel olarak Barry ile fazlasıyla empati kurabiliyorum ve bu durum beni oldukça rahatsız ediyor; belki de filmin asıl istediği tam olarak budur. Ailesinin, Barry'nin üzerindeki etkisini hiç fark etmeden onunla sürekli uğraşması, aslında yaşadığı öfke patlamalarını yeterince açıklıyor fakat kimse bunu kabul etmek istemiyor. Barry yapayalnız ve bu yalnızlığı gidermeye çalışıyor; ancak doğru yolları seçemiyor çünkü kendisi de içinde ne taşıdığını tam olarak bilmiyor. Burada kastettiğim ona hak vermek değil, sadece onu anlayabilmek. Yine de kendisini seven, ondan hoşlanan ve ona gerçekten değer veren birini bulduğunda işler toparlanmaya başlıyor; en azından öfkesini doğru yönlendirebiliyor. Film boyunca Barry ne zaman rahatsız hissetse ortam sesleri ve müzikler boğucu bir hâl alıyor, her şey sarpa sarıyor. Biraz olsun rahatladığında ise etraf duruluyor, müzikler sakinleşiyor ve her şey yoluna giriyor. Bu adam yıllarca her şeyi içine atmış, duygularını asla ifade edememiş; şimdi ise eline geçen bu fırsatı nasıl değerlendireceğini bile kestiremiyor. İzlerken fazlasıyla bunaldım ve öfkelendim; zaten filmi bu denli beğenmemin asıl nedeni de tam olarak bu.

texto: I would only give ‘Punch Drunk Love’ a 2.5 star rating, because while the film is able to accurately represent a character struggling with social anxiety and repressed rage, the plot is thin and disjointed, making for a confusing and unpleasant watching experience. Certain plot points, such as the pudding scheme and the extortionist brothers' fates fail to resolve, and feel more random than they were likely intended to. It almost feels as though the movie was cut short before it could tie together the story. I personally struggled to maintain focus and understanding as I watched the film. For this reason, I would give the film the relatively low rating of 2.5 stars

texto: Barry Egan will, without question, be physically and verbally abusive to Lena over the course of their relationship, even if he really does love her. Everything we learn about Barry, from how he treats his sisters to his pathological lying to his general inability to control his emotions, points toward this. He is violent, unstable and untrustworthy—and love, for all its beauty, is a turbulent force, not a calming one. Self-control is exactly what it sounds like: it comes from the self , not from a lover. Barry's "quirky" traits would be entirely forgivably from a character standpoint if he recognized his own flaws and made any attempt to improve or mature in ways that really matter. Telling someone you want to stop crying all the time and telling someone you want to stop lying all the time are two different things, and Barry is only interested in the former. The credits rolled and all I felt was scared for Lena, a character whose sole narrative purpose is to inexplicably love Barry. Really not trying to be annoyingly contrarian here, but this was just a tough first watch in 2026. I can see why it was important to so many oddballs, introverts, quiet creative types and whatnot back in the day. Seeing a version of your own weirdness depicted, victorious, and loved is, I imagine, very affirming. But I am baffled by how many people I know identify with Barry. He simply does not deserve the good things happening to him. I want to believe that if you made this movie today, it would be broadly rejected. Undeniably beautiful filmmaking, though. Shitty L.A. never looked better. But no.

texto: Here me out- the concept of the movie is amazing. I understand, empathize and relate to Barry as a character and would've LOVED to see him open up and be comfortable with being vulnerable and being seen through therapy or getting help from friends and family (boy had 7 sisters). The music helps us understand his perspective and how easily he can get overwhelmed by people around him. Instead of turning it towards a pointless romance, it would have been better if it revolved around Barry and his relationships with the people already present in his life. The romance between both protagonist seemed absolutely ingenuine and you CANNOT convince me otherwise. This is the most horrifying rom com I've ever seen. I couldn't let go of the idea that one day, Barry might end up hurting Lena too, in his fit of rage. As much as I love Love, it simply is not enough to change the whole inner and psychological dynamics of a person who has spent their whole life being one way. That being said, I respect those who liked this movie but it simply wasn't for me

texto: Such an interesting twist on Adam Sandler’s earlier work, I have seen plenty of his movies and started this expecting a rom com, but this movie takes the genre and flips it on its head. Sandler’s slapstick humor is transformed into a raw, realistic take on a person who struggles socially and can’t seem to find acceptance. While I still found plenty of moments in this movie funny and entertaining, most of the time is spent with Barry trying to navigate understanding himself and others, all while dealing with the stacking issues thrown at him.

texto: Que PELICULÓN. El ambiente que generan algunas escenas, el trabajo de sonido y dirección es fantástico. Un protagonista cuestionable pero entrañable. Los ataques de ira son increíbles. El simbolismo del piano es hermoso. Una película que se hizo con dedicación y amor (se nota). Hay muchos detalles y trabajo detrás. Es de esas películas que mucha gente odia y que mucha gente ama. Yo ni la odio ni la amo, me gusta. Me parece una película sumamente HUMANA. El conflicto de la puta me parece una decisión muy inteligente de Paul Thomas Anderson. Genera tensión e incomodidad. A la vez que genera un hilo del cual tirar para el desarrollo de personaje.

texto: Definitivamente está es una de mis películas de romance favoritas. No es perfecta en lo absoluto, pero tiene un alma y un corazón que te contagia durante toda la película. El personaje de Barry es (por el momento) mi protagonista favorito de la filmografía de PTA. La inocencia de Barry se ve contrastada con sus problemas de irá principalmente impulsadas por su pasado más violento. Su búsqueda de amor está obstaculizado por su inhabilidad de aceptar quien es y mentir de su pasado. Esto se ve por el como sus hermanas se comportan con el, burlandose y tratándolo como un idiota solamente por ser diferente. Inclusive si Barry les dice que no quiere hablar de esas situaciones, sus hermanas lo tratan peor por ser diferente. La carencia de comprender a Barry es lo que lo lleva a querer alejarse y volverse su propia persona. Pese a los traumas y el dolor de Barry, cuando el encuentra el amor hace todo lo posible para mantenerlo. Se da cuenta de sus errores al mentir y empieza a reconocer quién es el y que quiere hacer para mantener su amor. Hace todo dentro de su poder para proteger a quien más ama y busca el resolver sus problemas sin involucrar a nadie más. Esto hace el amor en Barry, lo convierte en una persona más genuina y capaz de hacer hasta lo imposible para buscar compañía y amor en otros. Y a través de este viaje uno puede ver las aventuras en las que Barry se encuentra y su convicción inocente para buscar ese amor verdadero. En términos de negativos, yo diría que solo Barry resplandece como personaje. Los demás personajes son muy planos y básicos, con Ledra siendo nada más que el interés romántico de Barry. Casi no se le da caracterización y, considerando que es de romance la película, uno tiene que sentir porque ese romance es importante. Aquí no se siente debido a que uno no conoce casi nada de Ledra y se ve como un personaje plano contrastando lo increíblemente escrito de Barry. A lo mejor pudieron darle más tiempo a ala película a enfocarse en Ledra y el como ella se enamora de Barry, no solo Barry de ella. Y los demás personajes son carismáticos pero no tiene mucha urgencia, y el antagonista es gracioso cuando aparece pero poco más. En general que la historia solo se enfoque en Barry crea una película bella, pero uno no puede evitar pensar que pudieron darle más tiempo para brillar a otros personajes. Para terminar, la música es tan etérea  y hermosa, apoyando al viaje de Barry. Toda la banda sonora es un deleite auditivo y hace que el amor de Barry y Ledra se convierta en real. Esto se complementa con la excelente cinematografía de PTA donde se ve lo confiado que está después de sus anteriores trabajos y como el sabe lo que quiere hacer y demostrar. Esta película me hace creer en el amor.

texto: I wanna start off by saying that this was a pretty enjoyable movie. I thought that the movie was really confusing at first but I realized the directors wanted me to feel overwhelmed and confused. It was also very fast paced, random and even chaotic at times. I also felt that the musical elements, the lighting, and the fast anxious dialog also played a role in disorienting me. Honestly, I really liked how immersive the movie was. There were times where I became fully immersed in Barry's chaotic life. But it was a bit too stressful for me, making it hard to pay attention to the small details of the film. Overall, I really liked it though.

texto: Really beautiful and chaotic in the best way possible. Probably my favourite Adam Sandler performance. Loved everything about this on a technical level, score was brilliant and anxiety inducing at times, and the whole film just looked perfect and full of life. The whole thing was so vibrant in the way that I don’t see so often, and the nighttime scenes especially were gorgeous. The scene in the bed at the hotel reminded me a lot of Phantom Thread for some reason in how the relationship worked between Reynolds and Alma. Top tier film 🙏🙏

texto: Se me hizo una película MUY diferente en todos los buenos y malos sentidos. Es muy diferente a las pelis de PTA pero de alguna forma sigue teniendo su esencia en micro situaciones. Es una película rápida, no pierde tiempo en explicarte las cosas, lo sentí como un short film. Muy rara pero gran actuación, incompleta pero chistosa. Tiene raíces de amor, comedia y acción pero ningún género se termina de desarrollar; ni termine siendo una comedia, ni una película romántica, ni una de acción. Es un short film sin género. Punch: Acción Drunk: Comedia Love: Amor

All I remembered was the awesome hawk, and the awesome snake. Both of those things have significantly less screentime than I'd remembered and I was deeply disappointed to realize that as I rewatched it as an adult. Also, there are a LOT of references to testicles (like, specifically testicles) for a movie presumably intended for a child audience. I do enjoy Rango, and I think it's an oddly beautiful film with excellent character designs and a willingness to push its premise to the most entertaining limit. But it's also, and I do mean this entirely seriously and in the most literal, art-movement sense, very surrealist. The scene where he meets Clint Eastwood was genuinely so bizarre that I basically untethered from any sense of groundedness and understanding which I thought I had accumulated throughout this film.

texto: Animated films are something I’d like to spend more time diving into as I go deeper into cinema. I’ve watched a good portion of the acclaimed and popular animated films over the years, and this is one that I’ve seen a long time ago. Johnny Depp’s performance as Rango is a good one for sure. He does a good job of portraying a character that almost ironically treats his life as a performance in itself. Rattlesnake Jake is one of the best animated villains in any Disney or Pixar style film I’ve ever seen, and even though he’s not in the film until the last half hour or so, it is worth the wait. I enjoy the camaraderie that the various residents of Dirt manage to develop over the troubling events that the story focuses on. Nicely timed comedic relief is a focal point here, as with most films of this genre, and doesn’t take away from the progression or characters. Overall, if you have the right expectations, it’s a fun watch if nothing else. I enjoy the western style influence and setting, and wish more animated films shared this time period.

texto: Un film Western de mon enfance. Y'en a, ils avaient du Clint Eastwood, moi j'avais du Rango (et Woody). Donc, un film sur un Caméléon avide d'aventure qui va se retrouver dans tout un esprit Far-West, bonne idée ? J'aime beaucoup la DA qui représente bien le côté crade des habitants, façon animaux du désert sèche bien Americain. Bien détaillés, tous avec du vécu de par leurs séquelles physiques ou même psychologiques. Le rendu Western est franchement bien retranscrit, bien animé et détaillé, ce côté vide du désert qui donne franchement soif à regarder. Avec tous les codes du Western : des habitants hostiles, des pilleurs, Shérif et autres bandits au sein du village. C'est clairement le gros point que je lui donne. Ensuite, personnage assez sympathique, clairement en proie à une belle aventure, et cela le montre bien avec ce côté rêveur de quand il était encore domestiqué. Son côté maladroit, peut-être égoïste de par certains de ses choix, s'inventant un nom et une histoire pour mieux s'intégrer. Tout un passage où il paraît crédible aux yeux des autres, le rendant moins héroïque qu'il en a l'air. Mais sans compter son évolution qui résume parfaitement son caractère qui met en défaut ce qu'il devrait être : s'assumer et se construire de lui-même au lieu de mentir constamment. D'ailleurs, représentation assez rigolote pour ceux qui l'auront reconnue à ce passage, vous verrez. J'aime beaucoup tout l'enjeu concernant leur ressource de survie qu'est l'eau. Comment cela devient rare, ce qui peut créer des conflits, d'autres leaders peuvent jouer là-dessus pour asseoir leur pouvoir, et cela nous aura valu un antagoniste assez bien trouvé dans la créativité, d'animal reconnaissable et aux allures bien Western avec son arme au bout de la queue. Un bel aura, une vraie présence qui vole limite la vedette à l'autre premier antagoniste qui est plus affaires et leader. Bon, j'ai quand même eu un vrai enjeu pour suivre le film au vu d'une fatigue qui commençait à monter, ce qui fait que j'ai eu quelques passages qui donnent l'impression d'être longs et ennuyants, mais c'était peut-être moi. Cela va évidemment influencer ma note finale concernant mon expérience personnel, mais pas grave, j'assume mes responsabilités en termes de visionnage où je dois me stopper si je sens une once d'assoupissement. Mais bon, au moins le film a de bons gags, le message final est correct, et les enjeux de sécheresse parfaitement expliqués. Film sympa, sans être exceptionnel. Juste dommage que je trouve la BO assez mémorable.

texto: This feels like an Adult Swim short (derogatory). Rango has an instantly compelling premise, but too bad its execution is everything I do not want from a premise as delightfully absurd as a hero's journey from cowardly Lizard to Clint Eastwood. It's so painfully self aware and satirical of everything that it just loses the magic that it could have had. Rango is much more of a comedy than an adventure, a Western or a drama, and it sucks that this is the approach they went for. You are absolutely not supposed to watch Once Upon A Time In The West before this, because most of the elements in this film that make you go "oh shit, that's actually really cool" is just stripped from that one. I don't even like Leone or that movie that much for the matter, but I genuinely checked out once the literal main theme song is just a lackluster spoof of Man With A Harmonica. So many shots are just ripped from Leone without even any interesting remixing of ideas like what Tarantino usually does, just homage for the sake of homage. The movie itself also does not hold up on its own. Rango is supposed to be flawed, but he's so fucking irritatingly incompetent and genuinely idiotic that it makes me completely unable to root for his character. He's not a likeable loser or a charming asshole, he's just that one annoying kid in school that you lowkey understand why they're bullied. And all the characters are just whatever, Beans is the only character that I actually find kinda sweet, too bad she's just the damsel in distress. The movie also feels really really long. Could have ended like 15 minutes before if we got rid of all the shitty Leone homages and trimmed one unnecessary set piece. The animation is pretty gorgeous though, that I can't lie. It's too bad so much of it has to be a homage of Leone that it lacks originality. That (SPOILER) character appearing to Rango before the final act is a little tacky, but it's pretty cute. Puts a smile on my face.

texto: Hmm muistin että tää olis ollu parempi... ei siis täysin huono mutta paljon asioita joista en pitänyt. Sekava, poukkoileva ja mitäänsanomaton tarina, unohdettavat hahmot ja todella, TODELLA pakotettua huumoria etenkin ensimmäisellä puoliskolla. Siis oikeasti, tuntui että yhden yhtä asiaa ei oteta leffan ekalla puolikkaalla tosissaan ja joka ikinen lause tuplataan jollain vitsillä, gagilla tai hassuttelulla. Ihan saatanan raivostuttavaa. Lisäksi tuo Rango hahmona on niin perseestä todella pitkään, että kun loppupuolella vihdoin jotain kauan odotettua hahmokehitystä tapahtuu, ei se ilmene mitenkään uskottavana. Onneksi jälkipuoli leffasta on ylipäätään parempi ja vakavampi sävyltään. Olisi ollut sitä alusta asti ja huumoria siroteltuna sinne tänne, niin tässä olisi ollut potentiaalia. Tuntui nyt siltä, että ne vaan tyhjensi jonkun kuratoimattoman vitsivihkosensa vaan sarjatulella, ja sitten muisti että ainiin tässä pitää joku juonikin tehdä ja ohoh meillähän olis tässä ihan hyviäkin aineksia joita vois käyttää. Sinänsä harmi, koska animaatiotyyli on hyvin ainutlaatuinen ja mieleenpainuva, ja moni visuaalinen ja esteettinen ratkaisu on todella osuvia. Ja OSA huumorista on oikein hauskaakin, tai olisi hauskaa jos sille antaisi tilaa vaikuttaa. Sinänsä idea tämmöisestä "aikuisten" animaatiosta, jossa on paljon kaksimielisiä vitsejä ja sivistyssanoja, ja melkoisen rujo animaatiotyyli, on todela hyvä ja toimisi, jos siihen uskallettaisiin nojata sellaisenaan. Nyt tämä tuntuu pokkuroinnilta lasten hömppäelokuvan ja vakavasti otettavan aikuisten leffan välillä, eikä tee kumpaakaan hääppöisesti.

texto: I remember really wanting to see this when it released (though in my memory it released way earlier than it did in reality). I remember so many people singing its praises. I saved Rango for a long time, as I have with a lot of these more mainstream-but-beloved movies. As is often the case, it really has nothing going for it without nostalgia backing it up. Often looking really good, Rango opens pretty strong with a string of whacky cartoon slapstick setpieces, then it completely runs out of steam when it drops into the most generic American family, action/comedy movie template story and just plods through it with nothing memorable, no real characters, no real personality. The character designs are fun. I ended up having to pause it and return 24 hours later because it was boring me to death. I don't think a family comedy should be capable of being boring, but it's so completely lacking in an identity of it's own that there's nothing to connect to. The acid-western epiphany sequence towards the end shakes some energy into the film, by presenting the act of walking into traffic as the solution to all of your problems in a film primarily for children... And of course the epiphany is that capitalism and greed are wasting resources and destroying the earth, which is never really engaged with at all and then Rango wastes loads of water and causes massive amounts of damage and is basically bailed out by everyone else, as he is for the entire story, leaving there with pretty much nothing of value by the end. I guess the Johnny Depp mania of the era was hard carrying this thing.

texto: If you've never seen "Oshi no Ko", it's a very well animated, very badly written anime that tricks viewers into thinking it's good because it's so pretty. Being pretty does not make up for the bad writing. Being pretty is easy. "Rango" is ultimately a very simple and harmless children's film. Narratively it's nothing impressive. Some parts even are arguably just bad. Depp's improv is much less charming these days than it was 15 years ago, and it's got probably the worst example of the dreaded "liar revealed" trope in recent memory. But it is also one of the most artistically creative and visually impressive pieces of animation ever put to screen. It's more than just "pretty". In fact most of the film is ugly as all hell, but intentionally. Animation just being pretty doesn't excuse flawed writing, but the level of artistic talent and creativity put into this film is different from "pretty"

texto: Rango cuenta la historia no solo de un don nadie, sino de un mentiroso. Rango en un principio miente ya que anhela ser alguien digno de admiración como en sus historias, pero comprende que las palabras no significan nada sin acciones. Su evolución se siente realista, no vemos directamente los cambios pero sabemos que algo dentro de él esta cambiando. Es visualmente preciosa y aunque el estilo no es para todo el mundo no se puede negar que hay ciertos momentos en la película en los que es un deleite para la vista. texto: La vi hace mucho tiempo de niño, al inicio no me parecía la gran cosa, solo veía bichos feos y una lagartija vaquera. Al crecer, por los azares del destino, la quise ver. No recuerdo el cómo ni el porqué. Ahora Rango, una película que para mí se ha ganado un lugar preciado en mi corazón. El personaje es un cobarde con aires de grandeza, quien habla mucho y actúa poco. Ha fingido ser más fuerte o seguro de lo que realmente es; pero aun así, acepta su destino. Un hombre (lagartija, creo) que está dispuesto a entregarse al espectáculo de la vida y ser el personaje principal de su propio destino. Rango empieza actuando en un terrario y termina actuando en el mundo real, hasta que la actuación se vuelve su realidad. Para mí, creo que de eso se trata un poco la vida: fingir lo que queremos ser para reconfortarnos un poco y darnos esos pequeños empujones que necesitamos en el camino. No puede evitar verme reflejado; es cine absoluto.

texto: Rango is a really fun and unique film. It has a great protagonist, a distinct Wild West theme and presentation, and it’s hilarious. Rango is an awesome character with very strong character development. He starts as a chameleon in a tank, gets thrown in the middle of no where, fakes it til he makes it, becomes sheriff and starts proving it through moments such as standing up to Rattlesnake Jake and protecting Dirt. He ends up becoming a symbol of hope and a true hero for Dirt. The Wild West theme and the presentation of this film are amazing. The pretty sunsets and night skies, the desert setting, a great score, the sounds such as the clock hitting high noon on a Wednesday or guns reloading, and the town of Dirt give it a distinct feel. The Mariachi owls as narrators and occasionally breaking the fourth wall also added on to its feel. Rango is a really fun film with a great protagonist who goes from zero to hero. Combine that with comedy and a beautiful yet distinct Wild West presentation makes this a great watch. 8/10

texto: I haven’t been the biggest fan of westerns, but maybe I was looking in the wrong places! I watched this as a kid and wanted to come back to it because I remember loving it so much. It started off a little slow, but it picked up very quickly. I can’t lie. I had to watch this in three parts so my rating might be a little bit biased this time. But something that I really loved about this movie was how gritty the animation was. I feel like sometimes you see animation movies now and they’re always very clean and no violence or death or anything like that but this movie really felt real in that sort of way when it came to the armadillo or even Rango just eating one of the dragonflies that were going by. It was oddly refreshing in that way. Rango was a very fun character to watch, a very basic evolution but that’s not always unsatisfying if done right. A fish out of water story done perfectly in my opinion. Beans wasn’t a very developed character though, wish there was more there. texto: I haven’t been the biggest fan of westerns, but maybe I was looking in the wrong places! I watched this as a kid and wanted to come back to it because I remember loving it so much. It started off a little slow, but it picked up very quickly. I can’t lie. I had to watch this in three parts so my rating might be a little bit biased this time. But something that I really loved about this movie was how gritty the animation was. I feel like sometimes you see animation movies now and they’re always very clean and no violence or death or anything like that but this movie really felt real in that sort of way when it came to the armadillo or even Rango just eating one of the dragonflies that were going by. It was oddly refreshing in that way. Rango was a very fun character to watch, a very basic evolution but that’s not always unsatisfying if done right. A fish out of water story done perfectly in my opinion. Beans wasn’t a very developed character though, wish there was more there. I did love the country bumpkins at times because they brought a lot of color to the whole vibe of the movie. Overall, a super fun watch. Great party movie. Very rewatchable. texto: Look, I love me a good war story. Unfortunately, I have a soft spot for cute soldier guys or something like that I guess. But, this felt too much like propaganda, even for my liking. There was such a clear and egregious link between the Christian god, American ideals, and victory. Furthermore, it pushed a simplified concept of right and wrong/good and evil. Saving Private Ryan is in no way a bad movie. It just doesn’t consider the same things that I do going into a war film or war story. In war, everyone suffers. Soldiers are victims to the systems they trust and are brainwashed by. I want a complex look at this and all the moral dilemmas that go along with being on the battlefield. Other people just want a good American movie depicting our soldiers as brave heroes. And that’s fine, I suppose, just not what I’m looking for.

texto: Okay, the first thought I had as the movie was getting started was, holy shit the sound design and choreography in this movie is absolutely phenomenal. The first action scene is extremely memorable but the highlight is the sound and atmosphere throughout the entire movie. That’s the real star of the movie, sorry Tom Hanks. That’s where my praise ends for this movie. It’s a war movie but what war movies always get wrong is that patriotism/nationalism has no place in a war movie. It cheapens the horrors of war when this movie tries to have its cake and eat it too. It wants to say, “isn’t this horrible how so many people are needlessly dying?” But simultaneously makes it seem like the American troops are the heroes. I get that WWII is sort of a layup in that America was fighting true atrocities, but war movies love to gloss over the innocents from the opposition to instead focus on the militants from the “good side”. We see people kill enemies that have surrendered and disregard for civilians from Tom Hank’s troop. I think the only good war movie can be an anti-war movie which is not this movie. It glorifies war but wants to act like it shows how atrocious war is at the same time which makes it fail overall. But goddamn I love Tom Hanks and would be lying if the movie wasn’t solidly made and acted which earns it a three star rating despite my major flaws and concerns with the movie. It’s genuinely well made and had me invested the whole time, I just can’t get behind war.

texto: I just watched this movie for the first time in 30 years. And while the film is nothing short of an astounding technical achievement, it is as morally and philosophically bankrupt as a film like this could possibly be. ﻿ ﻿Setting aside the events that led up to D-Day and the US entry into a two-front war, this film makes two arguments that I find absolutely appalling: ﻿ ﻿1) That a pacifist subjected to the horrors of war can be thus justified in the committing of a cold-blooded murder. ﻿2) That all who come after owe it to those who gave their lives to be better people because of their sacrifice. ﻿ ﻿When the Captain says "Earn this" to Ryan, I thought that was a really lousy thing to do to another human being. The plot had already established that not only had Ryan had no say in the mission, he vehemently disagreed with it, and wanted nothing to do with it. So for the captain to say that is to put a burden on Ryan that he in no way deserved. ﻿ ﻿But that isn't even the point of that line. Spielberg is trying to tell all of us that we owe it to those who died to earn their sacrifice. And while one can certainly commend them for ending the tyranny of the Nazis, that doesn't mean we all owe it to them to live the lives that they did not get to. Their sacrifice was in the name of freedom. To me, this film seems to make the argument that the sacrifice was in the name of war. ﻿ ﻿Captain Miller could have died anywhere in Europe. He and his team could have died on Omaha Beach. But because they died on that bridge, that doesn't make Private Ryan indebted to them for a sacrifice he did not ask for. And to see a broken old man on that beach 50 years later asking his wife for validation is just piling on. ﻿ ﻿And Upham's murder of the German soldier he previously campaigned to release is somehow meant to show that the horrors of war can change even the least warlike of men. But the manner in which this happens is in purely cold blood, as justification for Upham watching him shoot the captain. Upham has a perfect position to fire his weapon in combat, and the movie could have done that. Instead, Upham takes the prisoners, and shoots the one in cold blood. ﻿ ﻿Nothing justifies this murder. We are meant to see Upham reshaped by war, but to what end? That murder is justified in some context? Upham's lack of remorse in his action contributes to the idea that Spielberg is saying the murder is justified, but I don't agree. ﻿ ﻿I left the movie feeling very unsettled. There's a lot of emotional manipulation here, and a lot of scenes that ring very hollow thirty years later. And while this may be a strong technical achievement, as a film - as a work of art - I find it lacking.

texto: This will be my longest review because it’s 1am and I’m pissed off that I can’t connect with Spielberg movies (Sorry Jon). I just don’t get it. It makes me irrationally frustrated that I can’t pinpoint why I don’t like Spielberg movies all that much. I’ve only ever loved two of his movies, Catch Me If You Can and Jaws. Literally all his other “masterpieces” including this one, I find to be just decent. He makes decent movies. The last 40 minutes or so of this movie, when the final battle begins, are good. I’m invested. The problem is, that’s 1/5 of this ridiculously long movie. Maybe the emotional beats would have hit for me if it wasn’t all relying on Tom Hanks, an actor I just don’t like. The technical movie making ability is obviously there, but they are all boring, even though the stories being told shouldn’t be boring. I mean, Indiana Jones , Jurassic Park , Saving Private Ryan . Three of his most beloved movies that I just didn’t care for all that much. Maybe they are just outdated and not made for modern audiences, but I don’t think that’s it. A thought just popped into my head. I dislike high sentimentality movies. Spielberg always makes these overly sentimental, borderline emotionally manipulative films to the point that it just pisses me off and takes me out of the movie. The score of this movie just feels so cheesy. It may be unfair to Spielberg as well, because I didn’t see any of these movies at the time they came out, and I’m sure they have influenced so many of these little tropes that I find annoying to watch now, but at the time they were inventive and new. Alright, enough ranting. This movie should have and easily could have been an hour shorter.

texto: Now here's a film I hadn't seen in over two decades. I never cared much for this one, in part because I'm not the biggest fan of war cinema, and in part because I think Spielberg is a director who should stay away from anything too serious. And sure enough, there's too much misplaced sentiment here to make it a good film. The casting isn't great either, the music is icky, and the film is way too long, with too many lulls dragging the whole thing down. But I did find a bit more to enjoy here compared to the first time I watched it, mostly in the action scenes. But then you have films like 1917, and there's no more need for Spielberg's tomfoolery. A massively overrated war flick.

texto: “Tell me I’ve lived a good life. Tell me I’m a good man” Someone else said Saving Private Ryan works for a metaphor as US involvement in wars in general, in the sense that there’s always a private Ryan to save, a cause to fight for, and the sacrifice made will always be greater than the life saved. In trying to convince the audience that this great sacrifice is the point of war or why it’s necessary, the film misses the fact that this is precisely why war is irredeemably pointless. The film wants to portray all our lead heroes as victims of brutality who want it to end, but also encourages them to be perpetrators of brutality. Upham is the best example of this. He starts the film as a staunch pacifist, someone who wants to bring an end to the brutality on both sides through strict adherence to the Geneva conventions. By the end of the film however, motivated by revenge, he gives into his rage and kills a surrendered German soldier, starting the cycle of violence and brutality once again. The film frames this loss of empathy as heroic. None of my issues with the film are in the directing/filmmaking of it. Spielberg is great and he’s really firing off all cylinders here. But none of that matters (in fact it might make it worse) if the script that directing is supporting creates a world where war is always justified as long as you have a private to save.

texto: Saving Private Ryan é um daqueles filmes que conseguem fazer a guerra parecer algo físico. Não é só assistir aos personagens lutando; existe uma sensação constante de caos, medo e desorientação. A sequência inicial do desembarque na Normandia é provavelmente uma das representações mais impactantes de combate que já vi. Spielberg não tenta transformar aquilo em uma batalha "bonita". A câmera fica próxima dos soldados, o som é agressivo e tudo acontece de maneira extremamente caótica. Também gosto bastante de como o filme equilibra as grandes cenas de batalha com momentos mais silenciosos entre os personagens. A missão de encontrar Ryan funciona como uma estrutura para discutir o custo humano da guerra e o significado de sacrificar algumas vidas para salvar uma pessoa. Tom Hanks funciona muito bem como Miller porque ele não é apresentado como um super-herói. É um homem tentando cumprir uma missão enquanto carrega o peso de tudo que está acontecendo ao redor. É um filme longo, mas a direção mantém a tensão muito bem construída. Um clássico do gênero e, pra mim, facilmente 5 estrelas.

texto: Spielberg works his magic once again. The first 30 minutes or so of this film are masterfully shot, written, acted, and edited. It’s a genuinely unflinching, brutal, and deeply heartbreaking depiction of World War II that I have not seen anything like. The pain, the horror of it all, is ridiculously intense and it really puts things into perspective. The cinematography throughout is absolutely breathtaking, using natural landscapes, framing, and camera motion to perfectly capture the various emotions of the film. Tom Hanks delivers the standout performance here. I grow continually more impressed with his acting range and how he is able to portray such complex characters so well. Matt Damon is also great, as usual, and the supporting cast in general is very good as well. The storyline is extremely compelling (bring Matt Damon home 🤯) and results in an emotional, epic journey for a small squad of soldiers searching for one man. It truly feels like an epic journey in so many ways. I wouldn’t have minded if it was maybe just a half-hour shorter, as I found some of the really powerful moments not to be the loud, chaotic combat scenes, but the smaller-scale, intense interactions between soldiers just trying to keep surviving and getting through these traumatic experiences. There is a great amount of both, but my only real complaint with this movie is that it feels a bit long in parts. However, that’s a small nitpick in what is otherwise a ridiculously entertaining, important film that is masterfully made. There’s a reason that Spielberg is considered one of the best to ever do it. His range as a director is simply remarkable. He can create lighthearted, family friendly crowd pleasers like ET and then turn around and deliver a haunting, gorgeously shot war epic that captures the horrors of World War II.

texto: That opening battle might be one of the most insane things I’ve ever watched. Spielberg doesn’t make D-Day look exciting or heroic in the normal movie sense. People are drowning before they even reach the beach, bullets are ripping through soldiers, explosions make Miller temporarily lose his hearing, and medics are trying to save people who are already basically dead. The shaky camera, washed-out look, sound, and complete confusion make it feel like Spielberg is dropping you into the middle of Omaha Beach instead of letting you comfortably watch it. What surprised me is that the rest of the movie is much quieter. The mission to save Ryan sounds heroic until the soldiers start questioning why eight men should risk their lives for one person they don’t even know. Tom Hanks is perfect as Miller because he never feels like some unstoppable war hero. He’s exhausted, scared, his hand won’t stop shaking, and he’s just trying to keep his men together long enough to finish the mission. Wade’s death and Mellish getting slowly stabbed were especially hard to watch. I do think the movie loses a little momentum between the opening and final battle, but when that last battle starts Spielberg somehow manages to make everything feel chaotic while still letting me understand where everyone is and what they’re trying to do. “Earn this” is such a brutal thing for Ryan to have to carry for the rest of his life. After *Schindler’s List* and now this, Spielberg might be even better when he takes away all the spectacle and forces you to look directly at people.

texto: Today, after 32 years on this earth I am officially a man. That's how I should feel because when I was growing up this movie was mandatory to being a man. At least that's what it felt like. Everyone in highschool and college was obsessed with this movie, which I can understand if I was a teenager when it came out. Not a teenager 25-30 years later.  I remember going to friends houses and you would see the iconic movie poster on the wall, or a frame of him at the end of the movie. Quoting it constantly. Maybe it was the first "adult" movie they got to watch because their parents grew up with it, maybe it was their first exposure to hot women with their boobs out, the gangster life style, or the word "fuck" that wasn't said by their father to them.  It is interesting to me that so many men make this movie their whole entire personality, and if you are one of those people, you need help! I obviously never watched this movie as a child, or a teen. Chances are my parent's wouldn't have allowed me to. Then when I was old enough to seek it out, I just didn't care to. My only other exposure to the Scarface franchise besides what was said above was actually the video game for the Nintendo Wii. Why did I own this game at 12, I don't know but I did. I used to have to use the stupid joy con to drive around the little shitty cars in it. I never beat it, it was an open world GTA clone which is funny because Vice City is obviously a clone or heavily inspired by this film. I likely beat the first couple of missions and then drove around killing people. Anyways onto the actual film. A rags to riches to self destruction movie. Obviously a hugely influential movie, for all kinds of future work. I liked it for what it was but I felt that it did drag from time to time. I think from the 3rd act on the movie is extremely good. It really kicks into gear from the wedding on. Obviously the movie is most remembered from the epic conclusion which does live up to the hype. Al/Tony really carries this movie, I did find the movie kind of hokey and Al's over the top acting in majority of the stuff he does really fits the vibes of the movie. I am glad I watched it to finally say that I have but I don't see myself ever choosing to watch it again, and if I have kids someday this wouldn't be the top of the list of movies to show them. "I always tell the truth. Even when I lie." The best thing to come from this movie is the Bad Guy Razor Ramon

I remember going to friends houses and you would see the iconic movie poster on the wall, or a frame of him at the end of the movie. Quoting it constantly. Maybe it was the first "adult" movie they got to watch because their parents grew up with it, maybe it was their first exposure to hot women with their boobs out, the gangster life style, or the word "fuck" that wasn't said by their father to them.  It is interesting to me that so many men make this movie their whole entire personality, and if you are one of those people, you need help! I obviously never watched this movie as a child, or a teen. Chances are my parent's wouldn't have allowed me to. Then when I was old enough to seek it out, I just didn't care to. My only other exposure to the Scarface franchise besides what was said above was actually the video game for the Nintendo Wii. Why did I own this game at 12, I don't know but I did. I used to have to use the stupid joy con to drive around the little shitty cars in it. I never beat it, it was an open world GTA clone which is funny because Vice City is obviously a clone or heavily inspired by this film. I likely beat the first couple of missions and then drove around killing people. Anyways onto the actual film. A rags to riches to self destruction movie. Obviously a hugely influential movie, for all kinds of future work. I liked it for what it was but I felt that it did drag from time to time. I think from the 3rd act on the movie is extremely good. It really kicks into gear from the wedding on. Obviously the movie is most remembered from the epic conclusion which does live up to the hype. Al/Tony really carries this movie, I did find the movie kind of hokey and Al's over the top acting in majority of the stuff he does really fits the vibes of the movie. I am glad I watched it to finally say that I have but I don't see myself ever choosing to watch it again, and if I have kids someday this wouldn't be the top of the list of movies to show them. "I always tell the truth. Even when I lie." The best thing to come from this movie is the Bad Guy Razor Ramon

texto: Aviso que si quieren una buena review vayan a ver la que hice de la odisea, voy a defenestrar esta pelicula No sufría TANTO con el acento de una película desde Emilia Pérez. Al pacino todo bien pero que poronga fue eso, casi no usaron actores latinos y la verdad que fue espantoso bancarme esos asentos por casi 3 horas. Que pelicula de mierda, y es que no encuentro más palabras para decirlo. Yo entiendo que siempre hay trabajo detrás de las películas y que siempre hay alguien que se desveló esciribiendo el guion, editándola, asegurándose de que la fotografía esté bien , pero en mi opinión es una mierda. ¿Enserio hay gente que idolatra a Tony Montana? La pelicula quiere hacer una historia de un personaje complejo y duro cuando lo único que hace es decir fuck todo el tiempo. Me pareció un discurso vacío y sin sentido con personajes que carecen de profundidad, siento que se podría haber explorado más y no reducir todo a hacer plata y matar gente. No hay un arco de personaje que logre involucrarte en la historia y solamente grita todo el tiempo para hacernos creer que es un gran personaje y que haya GENTE QUE LO IDOLATRE . WTF. Me parece mal que este se considere un clásico del cine. Si quieren ver a un personaje profundo que se meta en el mundo del narcotrafico miren a walter white en Breaking bad, es el ejemplo Perfecto de cómo adentrarse en ese mundo y la realización de darte cuenta de que el tipo enrealidad siempre quiso esa vida, y su enfermedad ya era una excusa. No soy fan de Breaking bad pero incluso ahí podes darte cuenta cuando un personaje es bueno y esta bien construido, aunque a mi no me guste tanto. Después no tengo mucho más para decir.

exemplo: Comentários elogiam a narrativa de subida e declínio do protagonista, considerando-a um dos elementos mais marcantes e que carrega um forte impacto emocional.
texto: Até onde uma ambição que pega fogo pode te levar, com um orgulho tão ignorante? Tony Montana veio de baixo, igual a gente… Quis enriquecer e ser o dono do mundo, igual a gente… Quis mudar o jogo e dar a volta por cima, também igual a gente… Até porque todos queremos riquezas, mansão, um belo carro, ter nossa família ao lado e aproveitar a vida. Tony com certeza trouxe esse mesmo fogo de ambição, ousadia e coragem! Coragem! Tudo o que ele tinha era sua palavra e sua coragem. Todo problema que enfrentou enquanto era um Zé foi inspirador. Ter atitude nas suas escolhas e não fugir, desejar incansavelmente a mulher que, para ele, era um troféu, ter a vida que sente merecer. Estávamos observando a volta por cima enquanto Tony cuidava de tirar os tubarões do mar, até restar somente ele. E ele conseguiu… Mas a arrogância precede a queda. Depois que conquistou tudo, o que restou? Uma visão de sua esposa drogada? Que passou de um troféu a um peso morto. Seu melhor amigo? Que morreu pelas próprias mãos por causa de seu ciúme doentio com sua irmã. Tudo o que sobrou foi tédio e a incapacidade de se manter sóbrio. (Brinde: kg de cocaína.) Tony foi corajoso, ambicioso e ousado. Não há melhor definição para ele do que a garra de alcançar o topo. Mas do que adianta toda aquela ambição se no fim, você acaba cego pelo orgulho e pelo egoísmo? No fim, ele realmente não precisava de ninguém. Mas também morreu sozinho pelos mesmos motivos. A queda da coroa, um leão enfraquecido pelo vazio após conquista. Sempre mire alto, confie em si e seja ambicioso. O mundo é dos ousados. The World Is Yours 🌎🏆

texto: Cuando critico una película siempre me abstengo de usar las palabras "aburrida" o "divertida", en su uso coloquial al menos, donde apelan a lo mas primitivo, básico y plano de una opinión no aportando nada, por eso cuando digo que algo es divertido me refiero a algo diferente, a algo como Scarface. Una película que te plantea cierto mundo con personalidades y poderes que se desarrollan entrando en conflicto entre ellos jugando con los limites impuestos. Es divertida porque usa la cámara, la música, el vestuario y el escenario para ambientarte en un mundo donde el protagonista es el auto cocainómano que arrolla todo lo que tiene en frente exprimiendo una crítica a la masculinidad hasta la ultima gota de su sangre en una impresionante actuación de Al Pacino. Tony Montana tiene una fuerza para elevarse tan impresionante como desmedida cuando quiere apoderarse de lo que no es suyo, de lo que le falta adentro y es mas fuerte que él y su plata. Si es divertida es porque es una gran película. pd: No sabia que la radio de GTA 3 de flashbacks sacaba todas sus canciones de acá. Duro.

texto: Nose quién es el guionista. Pero dejarlo trabajar. En los momentos en los que le dejan expresarse y hace que Tony Montana hable es genial. A veces con un simple diálogo metafórico puedes explicar toda una historia, desde los inicios en cuba, hasta lo más alto de la pirámide capitalista. Con UN SIMPLE DIÁLOGO. Si consigues demostrar que puedes explicar todo el personaje de Tony solo con eso, deberian tener más peso las palabras y no tanto los pium pium. Si esto se hubiera dado podría considerarlo un 5. Actuación loquísima, TODOS (Michelle Pfeiffer no te conocía pero creo que es la mejor actuación femenina que he visto). Que bien ver gente actuar así de bien. Las escenas tampoco eran preciosas pero utiliza muchos recursos que me gustaron mucho. La música me ha flipado, me recuerda a Tarantino en algunas cosas. La comedia (bien metida siempre) me encanta. El ritmo de la peli es lo que me ha parecido lo mejor. Son 3 horas de peli, pero es que lo requiere. Gracias por no querer agotar las reservas de dopamina todo el rato. No hace falta poner escenas de acción y tiro y música todo el rato, de esta manera cuando escuches música sabes que el director te quiere transmitir algo, SI SEÑOR. APRENDE NOLAN. En fin, los gangsters y el camino del héroe no son mis cosas favoritas sinceramente, pero es que todo lo que he comentado es mi mierda. Peli recomendable y realmente considero que si no te gusta o es menos de un 3,5 no entiendes nada. La escena del restaurante es de lo MEJOR que he visto en el cine. Me emociona y todo. Mezcla crítica política + explicación de personaje + suspense + actuación LOCA, y sin música... Pelos de punta.

texto: Tony Supreme. Probably the most 80s movie of all time. It’s got the music, the aesthetic, the rise-and-fall narrative, the bombastic characters and performances… Scarface shows how lonely the top can be, it’s a cautionary tale. Tony is one of the most loud and violent men in film, but he also loves his family, he refuses to kill an innocent woman and her children. It would’ve been easy to make him a 100% evil, heartless killer, but giving him just the tiniest bit of restraint makes him so much more interesting.

texto: Mano, que filme ENORME! A história de um imigrante ilegal que vai pra Miami e acaba subindo muito rápido no mundo do crime, o que acaba fazendo o poder subir pra cabeça depois que ele alcança um patamar de superioridade dentro daquela área. É um clássico filme de ação e, embora ele seja foda pra caralho, eu não acho que tenha nada TÃO relevante assim pra destacar. O filme tem uma vibe muito foda que lembra pra cacete o GTA Vice City — que inclusive foi bastante baseado no filme — e as músicas são muito boas também. O protagonista, Tony Montana, é muito foda e um cuzão em algumas partes, e é mais isso que eu tenho a dizer que não conte spoilers da história. Vale a pena a experiência por ser um clássico do cinema e eu só não dou 5 estrelas por não ter nada que me impactasse tanto a esse nível. A e o final é CINEMA pqp, eu já tinha visto alguns cortes antes mais cacete, é uma obra de arte, é simplesmente LINDO.

texto: ***Revisit to see if my feelings on Scarface have changed as my movie tastes have matured and aged. I was very impressed with how well Carlito's Way was shot and how well each scene seemed to flow into the next. I've seen Scarface maybe three times, and while it's a perfectly fine movie, I had always thought it was overrated. This watch is too see if my more nuanced appreciation for cinematography and certain filmmaking styles will make me appreciate this film more. Relationship between Tony and Elvira seems off to me. Scarface is a fun ride, and I enjoy the ride, but I like I find more flaws in the journey. The editing is poor. The performances and connectivity between a lot of the actors feels off. Scarface is a good movie, with many memorable sequences, but it's less a sum of all parts movie and more individual stand-outs, like the cinematography. I love the feel of this Miami ride, and while shots aren't necessarily sewn together as I prefer, the shots themselves are vibrant, colorful, and full of style. I see why so many rappers and rogues love this movie so much. Scarface is a gangster who doesn't take shit from anyone, gets what he wants, and takes what he wants. This movie is more 'trash gangster' than 'Prestige gangster', which I feel I under appreciated as a genre. The movie hits a different tone 2/3 of the way through the movie when Tony reaches his apex. The film becomes more fun and announces itself with the 'Push It' montage. I don't love the script. I'm not the biggest Oliver Stone fan, and I don't know how much of the script De Palma changed, but certain plot lines just don't quite work for me. While he has his moments, of the elite Al Pacino performances, this is lower on my list. I prefer the cocaine mania of Ray Liotta in Goodfellas to the psychopath Al Pacino cocaine acting. He was absolutely awesome when snorting the comically large mounds of coke. The Gina plot isn't hammy enough to be enjoyed for pure trash, but it isn't well written enough to get any points from a prestige drama. Scarface is definitely elite trash crime, but I prefer Carlito's Way. I do have a much greater appreciation for Scarface for what it is as opposed to what it isn't. 84/100

texto: Hubris, cocaine, and lust are a deadly combination. Fucking absolutely fantastic movie. Amazing score, killer performances, brilliant set dressing and editing. Scarface is a very long movie but it respects your time and makes every minute of Tonys unstoppable rise and inevitable downfall worth sitting through. Al Pacino and Michelle Pfeiffer absolutely killed their roles. Pacino delivers some of the most iconic lines in all of cinema history with a swagger only he could bring to them and Pfeiffer manages to capture our fascination portraying a level of anhedonia while also quite possibly being the most level headed person in the entire movie except maybe Frank. Tonys downfall was there since the beginning, reckless abandon and burning hatred. The same thing that got him to the top could only ever have led to tearing him and everyone he loved limb from limb. The world is yours but if you burnt it to ashes what is it worth?

texto: I’m in the minority when I say I’m not a huge fan of mob movies, and I don’t care. They just typically aren’t my cup of tea. But Scarface is a damn good movie. It’s honestly one of the most enjoyable mob movies out there, if you ask me, because it’s faster paced and more energetic. It’s not necessarily the best of its genre, but it’s a great movie. Scarface takes a wild and entertaining look at how greed can consume someone, leading them to the destruction of themselves and everything around them. All of the performances are fantastic, but obviously Al Pacino is a standout in anything he’s in because he’s a legendary actor. texto: Probably the shortest a 3 hour long movie has ever felt for me. I’ve seen and heard so much about this movie but it was my first time seeing it. Al Pacino puts on such a powerful and entertaining performance from the start (but like that was honestly everyone) so it was easy to stay invested the whole time. The story is simple, yet complex which I liked. It includes many little details that I’m sure I missed some. It’s such a nice feeling when you expect a movie, especially a classic, to be good and it actually follows through. Can’t wait to watch this again.

texto: The British are not cool, whether they’re black or white. Never thought much of Russians or Jews either. The best parts of this movie are when Mickey’s around. Wished it was a little more focused on him, and was just a singular narrative instead of being British Pulp Fiction. And man, the editing. Quite a product of its time! They go hard on digital zooms for some reason and it looks like crap. “Woahhh cool things happening, play some fast music and just digital zoom in and out!” Moronic. A lot of other editing choices are quite good. I like the montage of the American leaving/coming to London. I really like when Mickey goes underwater during that last boxing match. Some editing decisions just made the events confusing. Why does Tony and the American just let Boris walk away? Do they assume he’s dead? I mean, I sure did. Why don’t the black guys kill him? Do they ALSO assume he’s dead? Man the black guys are honestly just totally stupid. Not locking doors, pulling a gun on Tony and then just walking away…not sure why theyre just dumped on again and again. And when that British guy walks in on then with the dead body, they just stand around and let him monologue? And then they just follow him around? What are you guys DOING . Are you stupid? I think it’s just bad writing honestly. “Crime doesnt pay”, so in order to continually punish the characters the script just makes them stupid. Also the poster is really quite colorful for such a drab movie. Pick a lane…

The narrative benefits from an excellent Brad Pitt, who is both iconic and hilarious in the role of the itinerant boxer Mickey O’Neil. A cult classic underpinned by brilliant dialogue and an ensemble cast in sparkling form.

texto: Je ne suis généralement plus trop fan des films de super-héros (merci marvel), mais il faut dire que cette nouvelle saga a su attirer mon attention au vu des critiques qu'elle a suscité y compris au niveau de ceux qui ne sont pas fan de super-héros. J'ai d'abord trouvé le film très drôle, les gags sont vraiment bien amenés et pas trop lourd, que ce soit le père qui demande à son fils de lui dire "je t'aime", ou simplement les situations inconfortables dans lesquelles Miles se trouve. Le rythme assez rapide du film permet de ne pas s'ennuyer, et cela est d'autant plus appuyé vers la fin avec les différents styles d'animation proposé en fonction d'où proviennent les différents personnages. Au niveau de l'intrigue par contre c'est moins bien de manière générale, bien que je trouve le début avec la mort de Peter Parker assez réussie, la suite va vraiment être un peu trop basique à mon gout. Il y a d'abord l'antagoniste qui a mon sens n'a qu'un proto-développement un peu bâclé, des facilités un peu grossières comme la meuf spiderman qui est dans le labo et qui arrive à la rescousse, c'est assez curieux. J'ai aussi trouvé qu'il y a eu un certain manque de progressivité dans le power up de Miles, genre il passe vraiment du tout au tout sans transition, sans vraiment se découvrir. Bref, l'histoire bien que trop basique se regarde bien grâce aux touches d'humour et l'animation originale. Un bon moment.

texto: You already know the story, so I ain’t gonna resume it So, I am not the biggest Spider-Man fan, not even what you would call a “fan”, but the movie was, alright, like, yes, I didn’t dislike it, but it’s not all “ WOW! ABSOLUTE CINEMA! ” For me, like yes! I'll watch Across The Spider-Verse, but I don’t really expect it to be a 5 star film for me, since your rating for any Spider-Man film depends a bit on how much of a “fan” you are in my opinion, the story's nice, some predictable things, the animation is great but not only because the animation is great means I will love a film, it always depends on how I see the story, plot, acting, etc, and my own enjoyment, though overrated, my rant is because I am pretty sure like 90% of 5 star reviews are just Spider-Man fans, which, it isn’t wrong to be a fan, but not because it’s a piece of media from a franchise means it’s necessarily 5 stars, everyone talking about the animation when, yes it’s nice and has good animators and shit BUT DOES THAT MAKE THE WHOLE FILM GOOD?!….for me? No. What matters is the story and plot for me, unless your animation is choppy and just shitty and that’s when it matters, if you’re a huge animation studio good animation is expected, I just don’t really connect with Spider-Man, sorry but, as much as I try to enjoy the films maximum I have ever given to a Spider-Man film (so far) is 4/5 stars, like I get why people are fans but, I just…it isn’t my thing! I can watch the films but it wouldn’t be my first choice! No, since I am autistic that doesn’t mean I have to love Spider-Man, each person will have their own opinion and thoughts, that’s basically all for my review/rant.

texto: Look, we can animate! Don't pay attention to the consecutively disappointing, recycled tropes and plot holes though ^^ Looks pretty, right? Now the best thing is that you are going to eat it up because it is Spiderman!! And because it is Spiderman you don't even have to think for yourself because the plot is being spoon-fed to you, isn't that great? Look at our other movies that have the exact same character arc again and again all over!!! And we even have super hip music that you guys at your age enjoy! You're going to love it!! Rant : It seems that in general, people justify this audiovisual product by saying: "Oh, but it looks pretty!" I have a few problems with this. First of all, this kind of animation is also from the perspective of 2018 nowhere near revolutionary. It is not daring of them "to try a new style" since typical marvel fans are just eating everything up anyway. And it's marvel, they can afford it. This movie just wanted to be edgy but in the end produced the same recycled and overused marvel tropes as always. "It was my fault" before the random ass villain uncle dies, the shy new kid at school, main character suddenly gaining confidence and being able to do crazy things even though they couldn't do anything before.. Aunt May being in on the secret just for convenience's sake to keep the plot going? Also, how ironic that trying to force your movie to be self-aware about it's overused tropes just sheds more light on HOW OVERUSED YOUR TROPES ARE. It's like shooting yourself in the knee and laughing awkwardly while doing it. Half of the things that happened had no significance because, guess what? There was a magic USB-Stick that happened to have the perfect code to stop the big evil machine from blowing everything up, wow how convenient for the main character, he didn't even have to do anything... Oh, and the music felt insulting to my ears.

texto: Looks pretty but a narrative mess. You can clearly see the seams where different narratives get welded together, too bad all lead to nowhere. Too many villains, and only Kingpin gets a motive that is PeterB's counterpart, neither of which get explored, we only see the resolution. Instead we get a coming-of-age story with Miles Morales, a teen that has it all, but having contempt for it; it just don't sit right with him. His new private school is too elitist, but we only see him having trouble socially as well as being overwhelmed with schoolwork, good thing  he's an A+ student. Why does he want to become Spiderman? No idea, sure he saw his masked weirdo get killed in front of him, but others came, other that were far more capable that were not keen on having dead weight to lug around. The idea of not doing schoolwork was part of his plan, but bailing on being Spiderman wasn't. Is that his motivation, looking cool? Why was he so eager to get the Spider-people's approval? Miles' story is that of an uncomplicated character: he gets everything, does the right thing and the only blemish is his character is the fact that he idolised a crook. Funny thing is it gets resolved immediately. Don't you worry, your favourite Miles Sue is super dooper simple to understand: he is perfect, yuppie!

texto: Only part of this I actively enjoyed was a singular joke that happens while Miles is carrying around a passed-out Peter B. Parker and they say "𝘓𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘴 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘢 𝘤𝘩𝘪𝘭𝘥 𝘥𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘭𝘪𝘬𝘦 𝘚𝘱𝘪𝘥𝘦𝘳-𝘔𝘢𝘯 𝘥𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘨𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢 𝘩𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘭𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘱𝘴𝘦 𝘣𝘦𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘥 𝘢 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘪𝘯." I felt that this didn't expand upon 𝘢𝘯𝘺 of the characters well enough, which is SO sad considering the sheer number of them, I mean we hardly even get to know Miles and that SUCKS!!!! From the bottom of my heart, I hope we get another movie that actually wholly delves into Miles Morales story. I want Spider-Man movies to go much further into 𝘸𝘩𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘺 𝘢𝘳𝘦 as people, their motivations, hopes, etc. This felt lacklustre, which perhaps is due to the short run-time? They tried to cram too much shit into an hour and 56 minute movie- and it suffered for it. Not even to mention the villains were incredibly shallowly characterized, especially Olivia Octavius, of whom we know next to nothing about; she has zero personality, no interesting traits...and her design is awful! Those dreadful plastic-y tentacles of hers are reminiscent of children's toys. Ugh! Then there's how idiotic everything is about Kingpin, I couldn't stand anytime he was on screen due to his dreadful design- sorry, why does he look like a fucking wall in sheer mass, as well as resembling an egg? Is he supposed to be Kingpin or Humpty Dumpty.......... The soundtrack is excruciating...I had to mute multiple times just to finish this, why the hell would you subject me to Post Malone! That's plain torture. And I get that's dramatic to say but it's /really/ fucking bad, and I'm used to hating the song choices in film, like ?? try harder. Another thing is that, while I understand they were going for a "comic book aesthetic" sort of thing with the designs and art choices in general as...y'know, Spider-Man is a comic character, they just failed to do it effectively. For something so praised I expected much better art direction and designs.

texto: So this is the movie everyone fucking loves? Was The Big Lebowski funny? Yes. Was it the funniest movie I've ever seen? Yeah... NO. I went into this with pretty high expectations because I've heard so many people call this one of the funniest movies ever made. I also really like the Coen brothers, so I was expecting to laugh my ass off. I didn't. Not once. And that's probably the biggest problem I had with it. I understood the jokes, I thought the characters were funny, and I could see why people love it, but I just never found myself actually laughing out loud. It was more like sitting there thinking, “Okay, that's pretty funny.” The story itself worked really well though. It's such a stupid fucking situation that somehow keeps getting more complicated. The Dude gets mistaken for someone else, gets dragged into this whole kidnapping situation and suddenly he's involved in all kinds of bullshit he clearly doesn't want to be involved in. And then there's Walter. Walter is probably my favorite part of the movie. This man is fucking insane. Every single situation somehow turns into a war because Walter refuses to just chill for five seconds. And the gag with Donny constantly trying to talk while Walter tells him to shut up every time was pretty funny. Poor Donny just wanted to participate. I also have to talk about Peter Stormare because I fucking love that dude. He barely has anything to do in this movie compared to some of the other characters, but he was still great. Every time he showed up I was like, “YOOOO IT'S PETER STORMARE.” His character is basically just this weird, silent, intimidating Swedish guy who looks like he's about to commit a crime at any second. I don't even know what it is about him, but I just love watching this man in movies. The characters were definitely the strongest part of the movie. The Dude is obviously iconic. He's basically a man who has completely given up on life and somehow still gets dragged into every possible problem. He doesn't even seem surprised anymore when something ridiculous happens. Walter is the complete opposite. He treats every tiny problem like it's a military operation. And Donny is just... there. I also really liked how bowling was basically connected to everything. I didn't expect the movie to lean this hard into bowling, but somehow it worked. You have this ridiculous crime story happening, but everyone is still somehow finding time to go bowling. That was probably the most unique thing about the movie for me. Because honestly, I didn't find much else that stood out. The cinematography was fine, but nothing really blew me away. It looked like a normal movie to me. There weren't many shots where I thought, “Holy shit, that looks amazing.” And that's usually something I really appreciate in movies. I also think I expected the whole thing to feel more unique. Everyone talks about The Big Lebowski like it's this completely insane experience that you've never seen anything like before. And while the characters definitely have their own personalities, the actual movie didn't feel THAT special to me. Maybe that's why I didn't connect with it as much as I wanted to. I know this is one of those movies that has a massive fanbase and I can absolutely understand why. It's well written, the characters are memorable, the dialogue works, and the whole story is pretty damn entertaining. I just wasn't laughing. And when your entire reputation is being one of the funniest movies ever, that's kind of a problem for me. I still had a good time watching it though. It was never boring and I definitely don't regret watching it. I just expected something way more memorable, especially after hearing people hype this movie up for years. Maybe I'll appreciate it more on a rewatch. Maybe I was just in the wrong mood. Maybe I need to become a professional bowler first. For now though, it's just a good movie to me. 6/10 bowling balls TIM OUT Good watch, but bro... where was the fucking laughter?

texto: Diría que la comedia debe de ser el género más complicado dentro de la subjetividad cinematográfica. Una película cómica necesita provocar risas, al igual que una dramática necesita despertar la empatía oculta. ¿Qué pasa cuando una comedia no genera gracia al espectador? Bien, este ha sido mi caso con *El gran Lebowski*. La historia nos pone en los zapatos de Jeff Lebowski/Dude, un idiota perroflauta que se mete en una misión de millonarios. El contraste entre la solemnidad del Gran Lebowski y la de Dude es gracioso. El viejo es alguien elegante y bien hablado; en cambio, Dude es un porrero que va en bata o con ropa de estar por casa todo el día. La tarea que le dan a Jeff es sencilla: dar un millón de dólares a los secuestradores de Bunny. La esposa de Lebowski es una jovencita que está buena y que está con el anciano por dinero. Es decir, estamos ante una sugar baby que está con un carcamal. Que Lebowski esté con una niñata así demuestra su vanidad y su necesidad de mostrarle a la gente su poder económico mediante la compra de una joven actriz porno. Seguramente lo necesite porque no tiene nada realmente a su nombre y anhela ser poderoso. Todos esos discursos que le da a Jeff sobre el trabajo son pura mierda viniendo de él. «Con los ricos y poderosos siempre un poco de paciencia». Jeff hará su misión con Walter... Oh, Walter, ¡qué pesado me has parecido! Walter debe de ser uno de los personajes más insoportables que he visto en una película, en general. Pierde los nervios y, en vez de hablar, grita todo el rato gilipolleces. Hasta Jeff lo sabe, pero no dice nada por cariño. Entre que relaciona todo con Vietnam, se cree el Rambo de los bolos, apunta con armas al hispano pedófilo... Yo creo que Walter es un personaje que no despierta indiferencia: o te hace mucha gracia, o se te hace pesado. El otro gran compañero de bolos es Donny, quien no tiene un rol en la película. Solo se dedica a «interrumpir» debido a que no se entera de lo que hablan y quiere ser incluido. En general, su función es que Walter grite, nada más. Su muerte tiene un chiste que debería hacer gracia sobre dónde le han disparado, pero, como no le han disparado, simplemente sufre un infarto. Hablando de la protagonista femenina, Maude Lebowski, no me ha parecido súper graciosa. Juliane Moore me pareció muy graciosa en *Boogie Nights* o en *Kingsman*, por decir algo más moderno, pero en esta película me ha sabido a poco. Es la hija cínica del Gran Lebowski y su «relación» con Jeff es follar para quedarse embarazada. Ella odia a su padre por ser un inútil, como Jeff, pero que se las da de importante por haber heredado lo que su esposa tenía. No está mal para despertar risas, pero a mí no me ha llegado ese personaje. Si tú me das cinismo, tienes que hacerlo con un argumento que lo justifique. La misión se desarrolla con momentos cómicos y algunos momentos insoportables de Walter, como la escena de la cafetería. Luego descubrimos que no había millón de dólares y todo era una farsa para librarse de esa actriz porno de poca monta. Los «villanos» alemanes son bastante idiotas. Me hace gracia que su característica sea el nihilismo y estén desmotivados durante todas sus acciones. No está mal, pero cuando veo ese duelo final con la bola de bolos y a Walter arrancando una oreja... apagué el cerebro. Cuando al final sale el narrador, pensé que esto era una broma. Es un cowboy cualquiera que es la voz narrativa y dice: «Al final, Dude está tranquilo por todos nosotros». Gracias, Dios de los vaqueros, no pensé que el porreta iba a estar tranquilo después de esto. Hablando de la fotografía y la cinematografía, he de decir que me han gustado. Aunque sea de película de serie B, he de decir que me gusta que sea intencional. La historia es cómica y no necesitas una fotografía IMAX 70 mm. La banda sonora es una delicia. Los Coen tienen un gusto muy bueno para las canciones. Ya sea cuando Dude escucha su mixtape o cuando está alucinando, sabes que hay un temazo de fondo. Las escenas alucinativas están bien, pero tampoco me han pillado con las ganas de encontrármelas. Son escenas que vemos mientras Jeff está inconsciente y sirven para ver cómo su mente interpreta los acontecimientos que vive. La actuación de Jeff Bridges es la mejor, la verdad. Me sorprende que la película haya reunido a Bridges, Philip Seymour Hoffman y Juliane Moore. Las actuaciones, muy bien. A modo de conclusión, quiero decir que la película tiene la base y todo lo necesario para ser graciosa y que a una vasta mayoría le encante, pero a mí precisamente no me ha pillado gracioso. Creo haber destacado todos los demás aspectos de forma positiva (actuaciones, fotografía, banda sonora y, en cierto modo, la historia), pero su comedia no me ha encandilado. Entonces volvemos a la premisa: ¿una película cómica puede ser buena si no puede hacerte reír? Mi respuesta es sí, pero si el resto de cosas consiguen compensar esa carencia. Si la película depende íntegramente de la comedia y a alguien, por alguna razón, no le ha hecho gracia, no pasa nada; tal vez le haga gracia otro día o nunca se la genere.
