Ella odia a su padre por ser un inútil, como Jeff, pero que se las da de importante por haber heredado lo que su esposa tenía. No está mal para despertar risas, pero a mí no me ha llegado ese personaje. Si tú me das cinismo, tienes que hacerlo con un argumento que lo justifique. La misión se desarrolla con momentos cómicos y algunos momentos insoportables de Walter, como la escena de la cafetería. Luego descubrimos que no había millón de dólares y todo era una farsa para librarse de esa actriz porno de poca monta. Los «villanos» alemanes son bastante idiotas. Me hace gracia que su característica sea el nihilismo y estén desmotivados durante todas sus acciones. No está mal, pero cuando veo ese duelo final con la bola de bolos y a Walter arrancando una oreja... apagué el cerebro. Cuando al final sale el narrador, pensé que esto era una broma. Es un cowboy cualquiera que es la voz narrativa y dice: «Al final, Dude está tranquilo por todos nosotros». Gracias, Dios de los vaqueros, no pensé que el porreta iba a estar tranquilo después de esto. Hablando de la fotografía y la cinematografía, he de decir que me han gustado. Aunque sea de película de serie B, he de decir que me gusta que sea intencional. La historia es cómica y no necesitas una fotografía IMAX 70 mm. La banda sonora es una delicia. Los Coen tienen un gusto muy bueno para las canciones. Ya sea cuando Dude escucha su mixtape o cuando está alucinando, sabes que hay un temazo de fondo. Las escenas alucinativas están bien, pero tampoco me han pillado con las ganas de encontrármelas. Son escenas que vemos mientras Jeff está inconsciente y sirven para ver cómo su mente interpreta los acontecimientos que vive. La actuación de Jeff Bridges es la mejor, la verdad. Me sorprende que la película haya reunido a Bridges, Philip Seymour Hoffman y Juliane Moore. Las actuaciones, muy bien. A modo de conclusión, quiero decir que la película tiene la base y todo lo necesario para ser graciosa y que a una vasta mayoría le encante, pero a mí precisamente no me ha pillado gracioso. Creo haber destacado todos los demás aspectos de forma positiva (actuaciones, fotografía, banda sonora y, en cierto modo, la historia), pero su comedia no me ha encandilado. Entonces volvemos a la premisa: ¿una película cómica puede ser buena si no puede hacerte reír? Mi respuesta es sí, pero si el resto de cosas consiguen compensar esa carencia. Si la película depende íntegramente de la comedia y a alguien, por alguna razón, no le ha hecho gracia, no pasa nada; tal vez le haga gracia otro día o nunca se la genere.

texto: Diría que la comedia debe de ser el género más complicado dentro de la subjetividad cinematográfica. Una película cómica necesita provocar risas, al igual que una dramática necesita despertar la empatía oculta. ¿Qué pasa cuando una comedia no genera gracia al espectador? Bien, este ha sido mi caso con *El gran Lebowski*. La historia nos pone en los zapatos de Jeff Lebowski/Dude, un idiota perroflauta que se mete en una misión de millonarios. El contraste entre la solemnidad del Gran Lebowski y la de Dude es gracioso. El viejo es alguien elegante y bien hablado; en cambio, Dude es un porrero que va en bata o con ropa de estar por casa todo el día. La tarea que le dan a Jeff es sencilla: dar un millón de dólares a los secuestradores de Bunny. La esposa de Lebowski es una jovencita que está buena y que está con el anciano por dinero. Es decir, estamos ante una sugar baby que está con un carcamal. Que Lebowski esté con una niñata así demuestra su vanidad y su necesidad de mostrarle a la gente su poder económico mediante la compra de una joven actriz porno. Seguramente lo necesite porque no tiene nada realmente a su nombre y anhela ser poderoso. Todos esos discursos que le da a Jeff sobre el trabajo son pura mierda viniendo de él. «Con los ricos y poderosos siempre un poco de paciencia». Jeff hará su misión con Walter... Oh, Walter, ¡qué pesado me has parecido! Walter debe de ser uno de los personajes más insoportables que he visto en una película, en general. Pierde los nervios y, en vez de hablar, grita todo el rato gilipolleces. Hasta Jeff lo sabe, pero no dice nada por cariño. Entre que relaciona todo con Vietnam, se cree el Rambo de los bolos, apunta con armas al hispano pedófilo... Yo creo que Walter es un personaje que no despierta indiferencia: o te hace mucha gracia, o se te hace pesado. El otro gran compañero de bolos es Donny, quien no tiene un rol en la película. Solo se dedica a «interrumpir» debido a que no se entera de lo que hablan y quiere ser incluido. En general, su función es que Walter grite, nada más. Su muerte tiene un chiste que debería hacer gracia sobre dónde le han disparado, pero, como no le han disparado, simplemente sufre un infarto. Hablando de la protagonista femenina, Maude Lebowski, no me ha parecido súper graciosa. Juliane Moore me pareció muy graciosa en *Boogie Nights* o en *Kingsman*, por decir algo más moderno, pero en esta película me ha sabido a poco. Es la hija cínica del Gran Lebowski y su «relación» con Jeff es follar para quedarse embarazada. Ella odia a su padre por ser un inútil, como Jeff, pero que se las da de importante por haber heredado lo que su esposa tenía. La misión se desarrolla con momentos cómicos y algunos momentos insoportables de Walter, como la escena de la cafetería. Luego descubrimos que no había millón de dólares y todo era una farsa para librarse de esa actriz porno de poca monta. Los «villanos» alemanes son bastante idiotas. Me hace gracia que su característica sea el nihilismo y estén desmotivados durante todas sus acciones. No está mal, pero cuando veo ese duelo final con la bola de bolos y a Walter arrancando una oreja... apagué el cerebro. Cuando al final sale el narrador, pensé que esto era una broma. Es un cowboy cualquiera que es la voz narrativa y dice: «Al final, Dude está tranquilo por todos nosotros». Gracias, Dios de los vaqueros, no pensé que el porreta iba a estar tranquilo después de esto. Hablando de la fotografía y la cinematografía, he de decir que me han gustado. Aunque sea de película de serie B, he de decir que me gusta que sea intencional. La historia es cómica y no necesitas una fotografía IMAX 70 mm. La banda sonora es una delicia. Los Coen tienen un gusto muy bueno para las canciones. Ya sea cuando Dude escucha su mixtape o cuando está alucinando, sabes que hay un temazo de fondo. Las escenas alucinativas están bien, pero tampoco me han pillado con las ganas de encontrármelas. Son escenas que vemos mientras Jeff está inconsciente y sirven para ver cómo su mente interpreta los acontecimientos que vive. La actuación de Jeff Bridges es la mejor, la verdad. Me sorprende que la película haya reunido a Bridges, Philip Seymour Hoffman y Juliane Moore. Las actuaciones, muy bien. A modo de conclusión, quiero decir que la película tiene la base y todo lo necesario para ser graciosa y que a una vasta mayoría le encante, pero a mí precisamente no me ha pillado gracioso. Creo haber destacado todos los demás aspectos de forma positiva (actuaciones, fotografía, banda sonora y, en cierto modo, la historia), pero su comedia no me ha encandilado. It’s very different in how its narrative unfolds, some could receive this as “that’s it?” or “nothing really happens” but I think its structure itself is conducive to what it’s trying to communicate. texto: The Dude abides. He doesn’t align with an ideology, he doesn’t classify himself as anything but The Dude. He isn’t deeply opinionated or bound by his roots and his past. He simply does what makes him happy and content. He goes bowling, he smokes weed and most importantly he has his rug which really ties the room together. Throughout the film he is constantly dragged away from his simple life by people of all types of ideologies. The nihilists, the fascists, war veterans, corrupt pornographers and of course the big Lebowski. What connects all these different factions is LA; early 90s LA. The specific time and location where all of these people of strong beliefs congest and complicate life for the dude. He’s simply a tumbleweed in the wind, dragged literally and figuratively into the web of crime and corruption often by Walter. Walter who is constantly exploding into violence yet claims he once dabbled in pacifism. The Coens create such an amusing critique of ideologies using the contrast to the dude. Every other character is driven by money, sex or violence despite what they say. Even Maude and Donny aren’t as pure as the dude as they both seek out sex/money by the end, despite generally being very good characters. The Coens show how nobody truly follows their beliefs and every character contradicts themselves. The Nihilists don’t care about anything yet constantly pursue the ransom money. The big lebowski acts like a successful man yet it’s all a facade to get money in the first place. Then the film takes a turn towards the end as it carries through the character development and commentary from the first half and starts to become an outlook on the human condition. “I guess that's the way the whole durned human comedy keeps perpetuatin' itself down through the generations. Westward the wagons, across the sands of time” . That’s what this film is at its core, a human comedy. Balancing nihilism and cynicism whilst being the funniest and most quotable film of all time.

texto: Something I love about the Coens is their ability to portray just how strange regular people are. They show this both in how someone really is, the random hills they will die on, their grand goal to in which happiness will be achieved, the creature comforts they enjoy. In addition, how on top of that, the characters society makes us play to each other when interacting and not only how that is odd, but even more odd when people stitch those roles into the fabric of their identity. Obviously in a Coen movie these things are more exaggerated or on the surface, but believe me, really listen to people you know or be more vulnerable with divulging your real thoughts and you’ll see we are all little freaks and that’s awesome. Everyday life is colored with such surrealism. On a side note Walter will go down as one of the performances so good at being a type of person I cannot stand that I had to be like “it’s just a movie it’s just John Goodman”

texto: The last scene of this movie leaves me with such comfort. "The Dude Abides." and just Bridges overall energy that he leaves us with even after the whole tirade with the nihilists, a fake millionaire, and a slew of pointless mishaps that all occur due to his name. "Can't worry about that shit. Life goes on, man." Such a simple line, but yet runs do deep. I wanna be on this level of laxed. I kinda just wanna be The Dude. Not necessarily living in this movie per say, but just the Zen and comfortability with his own vessel and just riding out this hellhole called "life". I think it might be the funniest movie of all time on top of all this. Its got great characters, some astonishing framework, an excellent soundtrack, all combined into a plot that has NOTHING to do with the main character. The Dudes life is just rudely interrupted by mistake and his simple life of bowling, driving around, and smoking weed gets put on hiatus all because some ignorant ass people want money. But, like he said. "Can't worry about that shit. Life goes on, man."

texto: "What the hell does that have to do with Vietnam?!" The movie is good at proving a point on everyone not trying to care despite giving effort into making things complicated. I just had a hard time believing Obadiah from Iron Man is just here. As a polar opposite of his role. And that they made Sullivan an unhinged war veteran. I guess that monster energy business didn't work out for him. The "Dude" is the definition of a washed up junkie just doing what he wants to do. He is a bit more self aware of his surroundings and is rational, even if his entire shtick is to be nonchalant.  He clocked the entire conflict on the kidnapping being just a ploy for the hostage, only difference was that the more he engaged with the hijinx of the Lebowski family and their money, the more he fell into a rabbit hole of problems. Walter is also a good example of being too engaged with something to a point where it shouldn't be. He tries to commit to things like being Jewish even if he isn't, sticks to bowling rules like it's the law, and picks fights he has little odds with. He is the reason Dude got stick in the ransom situation and is why it got escalated. The moment the conflict is something that doesn't relate to him or bother him, he disengages and dissacosiates with bowling. The death of their friend and the constant imagery of bowling from Dude's acid trip were also good contrasts to how Dude handles his pressure and his focus on reality. He chooses to associate around the end to what was important now after the money situation died down. And that, despite how much Walter ruined Dude's life, he keeps him as a friend because he no longer wanted to continue caring. In a world where he already tried proving himself, the situation gave him one more reason not to pivot to chaos anymore and stick with his laid back lifestyle. Anyhow this movie also taught me to love my toe more. No sliced toes.

texto: Has been the 3rd rewatch in about 6 years…tonight reminded me it’s just fucking awesome. The writing is original and clean and smart, and I can’t find any other words for it except just being pleasantly surprised and heavily entertained, every time I chuck it on. And it’s been so well written that you pick up different things from the movie every time. Between being funny without trying, some amazing choreographed shots, mixing in characters that could just be figments of imagination (iykyk), cool dialogue and a classy soundtrack, I genuinely think this is one of my favourite movies of all time. And the character of The Dude I feel like I could watch him or listen to him monologue all day. It’s something that’s kooky and uncanny and cool and awesome that you know every time you watch, you are going to enjoy.

tema: Atuação de Heath Ledger como Joker
exemplo: A atuação de Heath Ledger como Joker é citada como o ponto forte do filme, com espectadores considerando que ele eleva a produção e que seu desempenho é um dos melhores da trilogia. No entanto, espectadores apontam que ele carrega o filme demais e que o personagem carece de profundidade.
texto: Para mí, The Dark Knight es la mejor película de la trilogía. Lo que más me gustó fue la forma en que se desarrolla el personaje de The Joker y cómo se opone ante Batman para intentar destruir Gotham. La historia es más compleja y madura que la de la primera película, y se nota que Nolan elevó el nivel en todos los aspectos. La actuación de Heath Ledger como Joker me pareció excelente. Consigue transmitir perfectamente la locura y el caos del personaje, convirtiéndolo en uno de los villanos más memorables del cine. Aunque hay momentos en los que la película puede sentirse un poco lenta o pesada, especialmente por su duración, sigue siendo una experiencia que vale la pena. Al terminarla me dejó una muy buena sensación y entendí por qué tanta gente la considera una de las mejores películas de superhéroes de todos los tiempos. Algo que hace especial a esta película es la forma en que Christopher Nolan utilizó cámaras IMAX para muchas de las escenas más importantes. Esto permitió mostrar Gotham, las persecuciones y las secuencias de acción con una escala impresionante que todavía hoy se siente espectacular. Además, Nolan intentó evitar el uso excesivo de CGI, prefiriendo efectos prácticos siempre que fuera posible. Gracias a esto, muchas escenas conservan una sensación de realismo que las hace envejecer mejor que otras películas de superhéroes de la misma época. Esa combinación entre IMAX, efectos prácticos y una dirección muy cuidada es una de las razones por las que la trilogía sigue siendo tan recordada.

texto: I completely understand why people call this one of the greatest superhero films ever made. I just don’t love it as much as everyone else seems to. Heath Ledger is obviously incredible. Every scene with the Joker has this horrible sense that anything could happen, and he completely owns the film. The interrogation scene alone deserves all the praise it gets. The problem for me is that outside of the Joker, I find parts of it a bit cold. Christian Bale’s Batman works, but Bruce Wayne never connects with me as much as other versions of the character, and Harvey Dent’s arc feels slightly rushed considering how important he becomes by the end. It’s brilliantly made, looks great and has some genuinely iconic moments, but I admire it more than I actually enjoy watching it.

texto: Looking back on this almost 20 years later and my biggest takeaway is how insecure this movie is. Dark Knight is CONSTANTLY SCREAMING its themes at you in the most dramatic, self indulgent way possible. You’ll have the Joker literally look at the screen and state “I’m an agent of chaos” while Gordon and Batman wax poetically on whether people are naturally good or evil. Worst of all, the movie will go out of its way to tell the viewer that some people are simply irredeemable and need to be put down. Contrast that to how the Spider-Man movies will try to tackle the heavy subject of villain redemption. Sure the execution is childish but at least it tries!   I came away with the theory that Nolan thought that superhero movies were not good enough to stand on their own so he had to water this down into the most grounded, serious, “adult” version of the Batman possible. The problem isn’t that The Dark Knight has nothing to say. It’s that it has so much confidence in how profound those things are that it rarely bothers to dramatize them. The movie is a long, slow, plodding mess that does not get the buy in necessary to take it self so seriously. Two hours and thirty minutes and no one gets developed. Gordon is always right and never pushed to grow, Harvey’s turn felt superficial and rudimentary, Rachel was literally in the movie to die. Worst of all, the Joker. We get so much time to develop and build on them relationship between him and Batman; how they’re mirrors of each other, how their philosophies are contradictory, how they mess with each other’s head. Instead we get Joker stating funny quips and theorize on le society. And I’m sorry but this movie and this performance is no where near good enough to justify the worship the Joker and this movie at large gets.

tema: Falta de desenvolvimento de personagens femininas
exemplo: A representação feminina é criticada por ser superficial e não contribuir significativamente para a trama. Espectadores apontam que as mulheres são reduzidas a personagens secundárias e que a trama não dá espaço para que elas sejam desenvolvidas.
texto: Получше первого фильма, но всё так же много несуразностей, благоглупостей. Сюжет как сюжет, комиксовый, но смотреть скучно. Почему? Игра актёров средненькая, запомнились разве Аарон Экхарт (прокурор Дент, «двуликий») хорошей игрой и Мэгги Джиленхолл нулевой игрой (а в фильме они - пара, то есть сыграли «на контрасте»). Единственный актёр-монстр фильма - Хит Леджер, и теперь Джокер может быть только таким, а мир не может быть прежним. Без Леджера фильм остался бы лишь раскрашенным картонным комиксом, где много взрывается, мчится и летает, но это неинтересно. Рассудочный гений Нолана делает красивую картинку, но на этом и всё. Как ни странно, пришла мысль, что Нолан не знает, что такое хорошая актёрская игра, и потому не требует её от актёров. Сериал «Готам» перекрывает «Рыцаря» по всем статьям.

texto: Achei esse filme um pouco confuso… não sei se foi porque hoje eu estava com a cabeça meio aérea ou se “ O Cavaleiro das Trevas ” só é complexo mesmo. Odeio sair de um filme me sentindo burra, sabe? Mas a simbologia é poderosa e bonita. É legal ver como por trás de toda a ação existe uma discussão enorme sobre moralidade, justiça, caos, heroísmo e até sobre o que faz alguém se tornar um vilão. É claro que a atuação do Heath Ledger de Coringa realmente faz jus à fama que tem. É 100% absurda. Mas uma coisa que me incomodou foi a m0rte da Rachel. Para alguém que tem uma importância tão grande na história, a m0rte dela foi tão abrupta… superamos rápido demais algo tão importante. Sei que a m0rte dela é essencial para a construção do Duas-Caras, mas faltou explorarem mais a forma como tudo aquilo afeta o Bruce Wayne e a história. Como sempre, acho que o Nolan tentou fazer com que um simples filme de herói ficasse cult demais. “ Ou você m0rre como um herói ou vive o bastante pra se transformar em um vilão. ”

texto: Para mí, The Dark Knight es la mejor película de la trilogía. Lo que más me gustó fue la forma en que se desarrolla el personaje de The Joker y cómo se opone ante Batman para intentar destruir Gotham. La historia es más compleja y madura que la de la primera película, y se nota que Nolan elevó el nivel en todos los aspectos. La actuación de Heath Ledger como Joker me pareció excelente. Consigue transmitir perfectamente la locura y el caos del personaje, convirtiéndolo en uno de los villanos más memorables del cine. Aunque hay momentos en los que la película puede sentirse un poco lenta o pesada, especialmente por su duración, sigue siendo una experiencia que vale la pena. Al terminarla me dejó una muy buena sensación y entendí por qué tanta gente la considera una de las mejores películas de superhéroes de todos los tiempos. Algo que hace especial a esta película es la forma en que Christopher Nolan utilizó cámaras IMAX para muchas de las escenas más importantes. Esto permitió mostrar Gotham, las persecuciones y las secuencias de acción con una escala impresionante que todavía hoy se siente espectacular. Además, Nolan intentó evitar el uso excesivo de CGI, prefiriendo efectos prácticos siempre que fuera posible. Gracias a esto, muchas escenas conservan una sensación de realismo que las hace envejecer mejor que otras películas de superhéroes de la misma época. Esa combinación entre IMAX, efectos prácticos y una dirección muy cuidada es una de las razones por las que la trilogía sigue siendo tan recordada.

texto: Eric Roberts’ filmography is fascinating. From this awful film to the cinematic masterpiece that is A Talking Cat!?! by gay soft-core porn legend David DeCoteau. Christopher Nolan wishes he was that talented The Dark Knight is one of those films which has such a huge following that any negative opinions of it feel automatically contrarian. I hate that, because I should feel safe saying how dull, unimaginative, and outright pathetic this movie feels. I truly do not understand why anybody likes this as a Batman film, let alone considering it as one of the greatest movies ever made. I will never say that something is “objectively” bad but I will confidentially say that Christopher Nolan objectively doesn’t understand Batman There’s no nuance, the fight choreography and editing throughout is total ass, no one is giving a good performance and dear god the pacing flows like a traffic jam. “Oh but Heath Ledger’s performance as the Joker is incredible” it really isn’t. Even if it was a good performance the characterisation is so butchered it fundamentally isn’t the Joker, and the performance is like one tier above Jared Leto’s (this isn’t a compliment to either of them). He’s so Reddit moderator “SOCIETY BAD” I cannot fucking stand it. The performance is certainly not good enough to justify the wave of bullshit method actors who took inspiration from him and this might be incredibly unfair to say, but if the bugger didn’t die then no one would talk about him in this way There’s maybe 5% sauce throughout the entire film but having Gotham just be Chicago is wildly dull - my fiancée and I made the joke that if you could swap out Batman with Optimus Prime and nothing changes in terms of the the city’s aesthetic then you’ve really fucked up. This Batman is far too militaristic and passé about everything that I truly cannot excuse this film’s faults. The copaganda is insane - obviously there’s gonna be cops in a Batman movie but this film makes the point that Batman cannot function without them which is insane. I do not like The Dark Knight and I truly do not understand how people like it as a crime film, as a Batman film, and as one of the supposed best films of all time.

texto: A bit of a slog. Coming off of Batman the animated series. Nolan's imagining of a grounded batman universe is hellishly drab and heterosexual. As potentially interesting as the Joker performance is, the absense of camp does the character a big disservice, and the rivalry (or lack there of) lacks a lot of the charisma present in other renditions, in favor of something that feels much more generic (though maybe thats just me feeling inundated with the performance's shadow over the past decade of nerd and incel culture). The movie feels bloated, long, and with lots of fat to cut.

texto: We commonly criticize Hollywood action fare for being dumb but the far far more infuriating thing to me about this (and about a lot of Nolan movies tbh) is how hard it tries to have the superficial appearance of being a smart movie that is about something. Early on in the film a copycat Batman asks the real one “what makes you different from me?” and the Joker is introduced as an ideological foil to Batman, as another character willing to use extrajudicial means to advance a personal agenda. The copycat Batman asks a good question! And the rest of the movie circles around it, seemingly exploring themes of vigilantism, legitimacy, force, or community- I say seemingly because it sets up that these might be interesting avenues to use the character of Batman to explore…. and then doesn’t. By the end, the only real justification of Batman offered by THE DARK KNIGHT is that he’s a rich guy with military hardware and that nobody can stop him. The movie spends so much effort asking the question and being self reflexive that I can’t help but be bothered by this “lesson.” The movie itself is expanding on the core idea of BEGINS- “what if Batman existed in the real world?” by asking a new question: “Isn’t the idea of Batman kind of stupid?”

texto: Any moment the Joker isn't on screen, it's boring. I'm only giving it these 2 stars for the hospital explosion and Heath Ledger's performance, which is too good to be in this 154-minute-long disgrace to cinema. After watching the first two films of this trilogy, there's a thing that recurred, and tbh in any Nolan film I ever watched -aside from fascist propaganda- which is that there's not a single shot of any subtextual meaning anywhere in here; something that requires the audience to "read between the lines" rather than relying on characters directly stating their feelings, avoiding on the nose dialogue creates psychological depth and i long to see the day i see this thing in a Nolan movie. another thing that bothered me is that this movie relays on dialogue designed to establish themes, believing it can exploit their value to make the rest of the movie seem to dive into those ideas but it doesn't, the movie features famous lines about heavy topics but uses these dramatic speeches as a shortcut. It wants the audience to think the whole story is a deep exploration of those ideas, even when the plot itself is just a standard action movie. Batman, Harvey and the Joker (in this adaptation) exist only to prove a philosophical point rather than act like real people. and btw Nolan, not even Heath Ledger or Christian Bale can save your cheesy lines lol Gordon, or should I address Nolan-the writer- why would you trouble yourself with building a whole world for your film, then have a father tell his 8-year-old son what Batman is so poetically for the sole purpose of a good ending line?

texto: The Joker is one of my all time least favourite comic book characters and most of that is because of the impact this movie had on the cultural consciousness. The “agent of chaos” characterisation is just. so. tedious. How does the Joker achieve anything in this film? He magically has everything he needs in exactly the right place like some Joker ex machina. And he’s so annoying. Sure, this is a good performance by Heath Ledger, but he’s performing an exhausting and irritating nuisance so I can’t say I enjoyed watching him. As annoying as it is, at least the Joker actually HAS a character. Everyone else in this is just a wooden puppet being pulled around on strings into big, boring set pieces. Oh, and the only female character of note gets fridged to develop the men. Classic Nolan! Also, I don’t really buy into the whole “superheroes are right-wing propaganda” thing some people have about the genre, but this is definitely right-wing propaganda.

texto: AMAZING MOVIE. Heath Ledger, Aaron Eckhart, Christian Bale and more put up an amazing performance in this movie. Heath Ledger as the Joker is undoubtedly one of the best portrayals of a villain. Heath is thee JOKER himself. His dialogue, his shift in tone, facial expressions, his mannerisms and more are exactly who you would imagine the Joker to be. 10/10 performance by Heath and he made this movie what it is. Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent was phenomenal and you can really feel how much of a tremendous symbol of hope he was for everyone in Gotham. Christian Bale’s Batman this movie was a HUGEEE step up from the first one. We see him alot more in the suit, and we see the sacrifice plays he has to make in order to be the dark knight of Gotham. The moral debates, the action sequences, the cinematography, the dialogue, the plot, the character developments and more are what make this movie arguably one of if not thee best superhero movie of all time. It should serve as a blueprint. Con, at times I do feel like it did jump around a little bit. Another con is how underdeveloped Rachel feels. In both the movies it’s a little hard to connect with Rachel, and understand the way Bruce or Harvey feel. This isn’t really a con but the performances put up by Aaron and Heath at times overshadow Christian Bale’s performance. However that’s just how good the villains were in this movie. Once again, Heath Ledger as joker is just unbelievable. This performance he put up is inspiring and you really FEEL the tension he brings. For superhero movie standards this is a 4.5/5

tema: Roteiro e direção de Christopher Nolan
exemplo: O roteiro e a direção de Christopher Nolan são elogiados por sua complexidade, profundidade e habilidade em equilibrar ação, drama e reflexão filosófica. Reviews mencionam que a trama é bem construída e que a direção demonstra uma maturidade técnica impressionante, com uma narrativa que se desenvolve de forma envolvente.
texto: This is everyone’s favorite adaptation of Batman? Are we watching the same movie? In celebration of the Lego Batman’s dlc release tomorrow I decided that this movie needed a rewatch. First, Heath Ledger is phenomenal. Outside of J.K. Simmons in Whiplash , Heath Ledger is probably my favorite performance ever. Bale has never completely convinced me as either Bruce Wayne or Batman. And the voice sucks!!!! Pattinson’s Bruce feels like someone consumed by being Batman while Bale’s Bruce often feels like he is simply operating within Nolan’s crime story. I heavily prefer Reeves’ dark and gothic Gotham to Nolan’s much brighter Chicago setting city. There are times when TDK feels less like a Batman movie and more like an extremely well-made crime thriller that happens to have Batman in it. How can I even call this a Batman movie when Joker commands most of the screen time? Batman feels strangely disconnected from being the “world’s greatest detective”. The fingerprint reconstruction scene is supposed to demonstrate his detective abilities, but it mostly amounts to technology doing the detective work for him rather than Batman being this great detective with supreme intelligence. The same goes for his equipment. Reeves makes Bruce’s obsessive commitment to building and modifying his own gear part of his characterization whereas Nolan’s Batman has Lucius Fox seemingly hand him whatever the plot requires. And what exactly is this sorry ass excuse for this brightly lit Batcave? Some of the movie’s logic also loses me. The entire Hong Kong sequence feels excessive and out of place. Batman supposedly doesn’t kill despite blowing things up everywhere he goes. Rachel falls off a skyscraper and walks away seemingly unharmed. More importantly, the Joker’s plans work with almost supernatural precision. Every person seems to react exactly as he anticipates, every piece falls into place, and almost nothing meaningfully disrupts his schemes. Ledger is so magnetic that he makes you want to overlook it but it’s hard. I also understand the thematic purpose of the Joker having no conventional motive. He represents chaos and wants to prove that civilized people can be pushed into abandoning their morals. But committing chaos for the sake of it has never been as interesting to me as it apparently is to everyone else. The character motivation feels deliberately vague in a way that doesn’t completely work for me. Still, I don’t want my complaints to make it sound like I think this is a bad movie. Far from it. Nolan knows how to construct a great movie, and there are some incredible sequences here. The truck flip and the hospital blowing up remain ridiculously cool. I also wonder how much of the Batman debate is generational. A lot of millennials grew up with Bale as the Batman, while Gen Z got Pattinson at a formative age. Maybe I’m simply more drawn to what Reeves thinks Batman should be: this lonely gothic loser detective boy that’s inseparable from Gotham itself. I just think Reeves’ The Batman runs laps around this iteration of Batman. The Dark Knight is a good movie but I’m just not convinced it’s my version of a great Batman movie. B+ish

texto: Watched this at a packed out screening in 35mm… this movie has never hit so hard. Unfathomably good character work—some of the best ever written. What makes this a masterpiece, among many other things, is its commitment to pitting these opposing ideologies against each other with such force. Every scene is working to elevate the central conflict: hope vs. cynicism, chaos vs, order, cruelty vs. hope. It’s brutally honest about tragedy, but more than anything, a resounding appeal to have faith in people. Felt like I was watching this for the first time again. You thought we could be decent men in an indecent time. You may lose your faith in me, but don’t lose your faith in people.

texto: I honestly don’t know how to review this movie. I hated the first hour of the movie as it took forever to get going. But when the main plot finally developed, it was good. Slow start, but by the end of hour three I was sold. One of the weirdest movies I’ve ever watched. Another thing about the first hour was that I was like “this is a western that takes itself so seriously and I this classic doesn’t hold up today at all” but I realized I was the serious one… The beats this movie was going for wasn’t to be cool and wasn’t cheesy, it was being done ironically as this western is actually an offbeat comedy in many ways and you can even go as far as saying a “buddy comedy” (even though they earnestly try to kill each other more than once lol)! When I finally realized that, I was able to enjoy the movie so much more. In this three hour movie there is probably only about 30-40 minutes of dialogue…again, super weird. But the musical score is absolutely incredible and more than makes up for the lack of dialogue. There are several very recognizable pieces and the score lends to several undeniably classic music montages and scenes that are just so cool to have finally seen. I’d sum the movie up like this: The Ugly beginning, The Good second act, And the BAD-ASS ending

texto: عملت ري واتش للفلم ودا ريفيو محدش مهتم يقرأه عن **The Good, the Bad and the Ugly** فيلم ويسترن ممتع جدًا، وأكتر حاجة شدتني فيه هي الشخصيات نفسها، خصوصًا **The Ugly**. الشخصية دي حرفيًا بتسرق أي مشهد تظهر فيه. طماع، كذاب، أناني وانتهازي، ومع ذلك عنده كاريزما تخليك مستمتع بيه رغم إنك عارف إنه شخص مش كويس. والفيلم عمومًا مش قائم على فكرة إن فيه «خير وشر» بشكل بسيط، كل شخصية عندها دوافعها وطريقتها في النجاة، وده اللي مخلي الصراع بينهم ممتع. كمان العلاقة بين الثلاثة من أحسن الحاجات في الفيلم، لأن كل واحد فيهم عايز يوصل لنفس الهدف، لكن مستحيل يثق في التاني. الفيلم طويل شوية، لكن بصراحة مقدرتش أزهق منه، خصوصًا مع الموسيقى والإخراج والجو العام. **The Ugly من أكتر الشخصيات اللي علقت معايا، والفيلم نفسه واحد من أفضل أفلام الويسترن اللي شوفتها.**

texto: Хороший, плохой, злой и неважно, кто какой, потому что все уроды Очередное дельце, которое теперь проходит на фоне Гражданской войны в США. Фильм, очевидно, смотрится намного масштабнее предыдущих из "Долларовой трилогии". Локаций больше, яркие главные герои, интересная завязка, повышенные ставки в стиле классического вестерна — круто. И тем не менее, у меня больше неприятных впечатлений, чем приятных. Во время просмотра меня не покидало ощущение, что на экране я вижу незнакомых героев. Что главный герой трилогии, что полковник Дуглас нравились мне из-за своей человечности. Да, это дикий запад с дикими законами и разумеется, понятие морали тут очень растяжимо. Но это не мешает в главному герою в "За пригоршню долларов" по-доброму общаться с барменом и помогать семье, попавшей в беду. Это не мешает ему признать мастерство полковника Дугласа в "На несколько долларов больше", более того, подружиться с ним и вести дело вместе. В этом же фильме, герой Клинта Иствуда стал ухмыляющиймся отморозком, что меня очень расстроило. Да, сцена с исполнением мечты Капитана армии севера вроде как показывает его эмпатию, но вряд ли он бы стал взрывать тот мост, если бы сам в этом не нуждался. Так что им просто было по пути и он между делом угодил желаниям Капитана. В остальном главный герой хладнокровная пафосная и молчаливая картонка, и мне жаль это говорить. У него была своя, в каком-то смысле добрая харизма мальчишки-проныры, это подкупало. Ну да ладно, теперь о Дугласе. Во втором фильме он предстаёт перед зрителем как прагматичный, расчётливый профессионал с моральным кодексом или как минимум чувством чести. Опять же, он признал способности героя Иствуда и пошёл с ним на дело. Делился с ним переживаниями и опытом. Про его основную мотивацию я вообще молчу, желание отомстить за сестру это достаточно благородно (оставляем за скобками моральную сторону вопроса, опять же, это вестерн в котором важно зрелище). Здесь же, Дуглас тоже стал отморозком и это грустно. Получив власть в лагере армии севера он пользовался своим положением ради наживы, избивал людей и т.д. Но если оставить эмоции и попытаться трезво взглянуть на картину, то она выглядит вполне логично. В условиях отсутствия закона и морали люди меняются не в лучшую сторону, особенно ,когда на кону большие деньги. Особенно, когда на фоне идёт война. И вполне логично, что человечность героев стирается и остаются только атрибуты, по которым можно отличить друг от друга ожесточивчихся, расчеловеченых героев. Просто, это не совсем та атмосфера, которую я ожидала от фильма. А если это и была главная мысль, то она здесь не раскрыта. Что до Туко, за ним мне было наблюдать интереснее всего. Его не было в предыдущих фильмах, поэтому я изначально воспринимала его, как такого, жалкого жадного прохвоста. Отличный и яркий персонаж. Дополнительное наблюдение: не скажу, что фильм скучный, просто в некоторых моментах затянут. Вполне возможно, что он так состарился. Этот фильм вызвал во мне противоречивые эмоции, и это, на самом деле, здорово. Потому что я не написала ни слова о первых двух, хотя они мне понравились. Рада, что ознакомилась, просто немного озадачена послевкусием.

texto: No need for me to go into deep detail to illustrate this film. Any cool things you saw in later Western films and games came from Sergio Leone's "Dollars" trilogy. Quentin Tarantino shamelessly ripped scenes off to make his own classics. I can't blame him; a great artist should know how to steal.  Leone invented a perfect formula for colorful, yet gritty period films. The Good, the Bad and the Ugly has it all: iconic characters, grand-scale journey, clever twists, cool gunslinging action, and off-the-charts badassery. Even "The Good, the Bad and the Ugly" became a popular tagline. Ennio Morricone's legendary score remains the golden standard for the entire Western genre. Obvious audio dubbing is a "bad" part of the film, but it is also part of the old movie charm. In the early days of cinema, filmmakers worked around limitations to realize their vision. Sergio Leone and his crew built an epic cinematic monument that dwarfs most modern blockbusters.

texto: Laden with thematic depth and reflections on violence, relationships, money, and obviously the intersections of those three, The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly may be a little too long but it’s also far more emotionally engaging than the other films in the Dollars trilogy. Eli Wallach’s scenes around the halfway mark, convincing himself and Blondie both that he truly cares for him are an incredible showcase of talent and bring the film’s ideas into focus. When Clint Eastwood shows up in the town to help Tuco shoot his way through Angel Eyes’s crew of bandits, asking him “Were you gonna die alone?” the bizarro brotherhood between these characters is crystal clear. They love each other, they have each other’s backs, but Tuco in particular can’t stop himself from stabbing Blondie in the back. Blondie knows this, and just accepts that that’s the way it is - he treats Tuco accordingly. From there we move to the bridge sequence, as pointed a war satire as there ever was, and finally, what is probably, for my money, the greatest sequence in movie history, the cemetery. With a bit more research and a couple of ancillary texts, I could probably write a few thousand words on the overwhelming scale of the setting and the goal of the characters in being there. My final (and initial) thoughts on this movie are that this is not Sergio Leone, Clint Eastwood, Lee Van Cleef, or even Eli Wallach’s movie (although he has quite a claim to it). It’s Ennio Morricone’s. Every single scene is not just elevated by the music, it’s made by it. This score is so perfect, so tonally dialed-in, that it carries the movie even more than John Williams’s work on The Empire Strikes Back does. Of course, in the case of Star Wars , the music doesn’t need to support every scene in the same way. In a movie like this one, with sparse dialogue and beautiful yet largely unexciting visuals, the music is able to be the main character. It fits each scene like off-the-rack pants fit a 5’10”, 160lb white man - that is to say, nothing has ever fit better. It’s considered one of the best of all time for a reason, but it really does stand out as exceptional in an already incredible movie.

texto: Tengo que reconocer que el western no es un género que me atraiga especialmente y que, en ocasiones, puede llegar a hacérseme algo repetitivo, pero tenía una deuda con esta película y muchas ganas de verla, y he de decir que me ha dejado una sensación completamente distinta. A pesar de sus casi tres horas, no he sentido que se me hiciera realmente pesada, y eso me parece uno de sus mayores méritos, si bien es cierto que hay algún momento en el que el ritmo se resiente y algunas partes se podrían haber acortado. Leone se toma su tiempo, pero sabe perfectamente cómo utilizarlo. Cada plano, cada silencio, cada mirada y cada duelo están construidos con una clara intencionalidad. La película tiene una personalidad enorme, unos paisajes espectaculares (joder, qué bonita es España), una fotografía increíble y una puesta en escena que hace que hasta los momentos más pausados tengan algo que decir. Los tres protagonistas funcionan y se complementan ciertamente bien, y me ha dejado especialmente buen sabor de boca que ninguno sea el típico héroe o villano perfectamente definido, sino que todos se muevan por sus propios intereses y tengan su propia moral. Además, la banda sonora es absolutamente brutal y consigue elevar muchas escenas que ya de por sí funcionan, especialmente en el tramo final, donde se respira pura tensión hasta el último segundo. Una película que entiendo perfectamente que sea considerada un clásico.

texto: Bon ce dernier opus reste en dessous du précédent … Sergio Leone se surpasse en termes de réalisation. Ce film surclasse les deux autres en termes d’imagerie, de scénographie, d’effets spéciaux. La musique est encore une sublime et culte. J’aime beaucoup la relation qui s’établit entre le bon et le truand qui se trahissent mutuellement jusqu’au dernier moment, ça change du précédent. Toutefois, l’ambiance guerre de sécession m’a moins accroché que le western pur et dur. J’ai trouvé également que le rythme du film est très irrégulier, ce qui est dommage pour un film de cette trempe. Heureusement que la scène finale vient sublimé tout ça, car on aurait presque oublié la brute tout du long du film

texto: This film is pretty much flawless. It's kind of baffling that Leone even bothered plagiarising Kurosawa when he had this kind of cinematography up his sleeve - the way its shot is incredibly tasteful and innovative. Obviously the soundtrack is great, and while the script is simple that makes it charming in its own right. The actors get the most they can out of it, and any lack of intrinsic emotion in the wordplay is made up for by the intensity of their expressions - there's a kind of glint in their eyes that gives an unmistakably fiery passion to every scene.

texto: Good lord almighty the set design, the costumes, the SCORE? Why did anyone else even try making another western after this? Unexpected for me going into this was the extent to which it was a civil war movie. There's a lot of consideration for and time spent with soldiers on both sides of the fighting and while I can't fully extrapolate a further meaning from it right now (my head hurts so bad) I can appreciate the extent to which it helps give this film a unique identity. What I can extrapolate is that this movie is beautiful. Sergio Leone shows you something stunning every few shots. And while I think the height of this trilogy is still the finale of For a Few Dollars More, I admire that this movie succeeded in the task of making a three hour movie that really only revolves around two people thoroughly engaging throughout and its finale is still cinematic perfection. My only complaint about this movie is that the BAD sort of gets shafted in favor of the good and the ugly. Lee Van Cleef is just a very good actor and I wish we saw more of him as Angel Eyes. Okay what am I still doing talking about this what do you want me to tell you about this movie? its the most famous western of all time just go watch it

texto: The film begins by introducing its three main characters. And it does it so brilliantly that it might just have one of the greatest character introductions in cinema history. Clint Eastwood plays the Good — Blondie, as he is called in the film. Lee Van Cleef plays the Bad — Angel Eyes. And Eli Wallach plays the Ugly — Tuco. Although all three performances are excellent, Eli Wallach's performance as Tuco is easily my favorite. He gets more screen time than the other two, but more importantly, somehow manages to become incredibly likable despite being, well… Tuco. Coming from extreme poverty, Tuco has embraced banditry and has absolutely no idea what morality even means. He's selfish, greedy, opportunistic, and constantly looking for the easiest way to make money. Blondie, on the other hand, is a lone wolf who lives by his own rules. And then there's Angel Eyes — compared to the other two, he's more refined and knows exactly how to position himself alongside whoever holds the power. During the Civil War, for example, he rises to the rank of colonel and uses the army to further his own interests. In that sense, the three characters can almost be seen as three different social types: The Bad is disciplined, military, and part of the system. The Good is a scruffy outsider who refuses to belong to any system. The Ugly is essentially a poor man from the countryside who has chosen banditry and is desperately looking for a shortcut to wealth. And that's what makes the three characters so interesting: these aren't just Western archetypes. They're three types of people we can still recognize around us today.

texto: Laden with thematic depth and reflections on violence, relationships, money, and obviously the intersections of those three, The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly may be a little too long but it’s also far more emotionally engaging than the other films in the Dollars trilogy. Eli Wallach’s scenes around the halfway mark, convincing himself and Blondie both that he truly cares for him are an incredible showcase of talent and bring the film’s ideas into focus. When Clint Eastwood shows up in the town to help Tuco shoot his way through Angel Eyes’s crew of bandits, asking him “Were you gonna die alone?” the bizarro brotherhood between these characters is crystal clear. They love each other, they have each other’s backs, but Tuco in particular can’t stop himself from stabbing Blondie in the back. Blondie knows this, and just accepts that that’s the way it is - he treats Tuco accordingly. From there we move to the bridge sequence, as pointed a war satire as there ever was, and finally, what is probably, for my money, the greatest sequence in movie history, the cemetery. With a bit more research and a couple of ancillary texts, I could probably write a few thousand words on the overwhelming scale of the setting and the goal of the characters in being there. My final (and initial) thoughts on this movie are that this is not Sergio Leone, Clint Eastwood, Lee Van Cleef, or even Eli Wallach’s movie (although he has quite a claim to it). It’s Ennio Morricone’s. Every single scene is not just elevated by the music, it’s made by it. This score is so perfect, so tonally dialed-in, that it carries the movie even more than John Williams’s work on The Empire Strikes Back does. Of course, in the case of Star Wars , the music doesn’t need to support every scene in the same way. In a movie like this one, with sparse dialogue and beautiful yet largely unexciting visuals, the music is able to be the main character. It fits each scene like off-the-rack pants fit a 5’10”, 160lb white man - that is to say, nothing has ever fit better. It’s considered one of the best of all time for a reason, but it really does stand out as exceptional in an already incredible movie.

tema: Crítica ao individualismo e ao capitalismo
exemplo: Reviews medianas apontam que o filme glorifica um sistema capitalista e uma visão individualista da felicidade, promovendo a ideia de que a perseverança e o trabalho duro são suficientes para superar qualquer adversidade, o que é considerado uma mensagem simplista e problemática.
texto: A melancholic watch, focusing on a beautiful father-son relationship, The Pursuit of Happyness goes onto show just how much money controls the quality of our lives. While Christopher’s character can be admired for his perseverance, grit, determination and for being a lovely father, the film glorifies the idea of “pulling yourself up from your bootstraps..” The film understands and in turn, portrays the phenomenology of poverty, struggle and sorrow without holding back. But what it fails to do is critique a system that is radically capitalistic, feeds upon ‘productivity culture’ and normalises kissing the ass of rich men just so you can ‘climb up the ladder.’ Success stories, like Christopher’s, will always be loved; they are inspiring. But one person’s success does not serve to acquit a system that constantly and deliberately keeps people on the brink of collapse and poverty.

texto: Shockingly, this film came out before the late-00s financial crisis. It would have felt even more relevant a year or two later, when a LOT of people were feeling a money crunch. But its concerns are sadly evergreen. Times are really tough right now, and I feel that as a parent of three kids. When the film focuses on that, it’s very effective. I want to see a struggling father succeed for the sake of his son, of course. I am quite privileged, but I think about what I would do to provide for my family if the worst happened. The film loses me in the details, though. It feels like Chris is in this mess because of many boneheaded decisions made before and during the film that strain my sympathies. His wife leaves and he insists that she’s incapable of caring for their son. Why? I’ve seen no indication that she’s a poor mother. Am I supposed to read that as Chris’ pride or his understanding that his wife is a poor provider? And his big win is becoming a stockbroker, the kind of person who creates financial crises that will put more people in these conditions. A lot of these thoughts are front-loaded in the film for me. The ending pulls at the heartstrings just right and makes me feel the joy. But I found it a slog to get there. All that aside, the big takeaway here is Will Smith. It’s a great acting performance, it’s a better box office performance. Smith was the biggest movie star of the 00s. Whether it was action, sci-fi, a rom-com, an original superhero film, his films were successful. He could take this schmaltzy, manipulative pap and make it one of the top ten films of the year. His star power was off the charts, and that’s rewlly interesting to me. Watched as part of a 20th anniversary 2006 retrospective.

texto: I have a lot of mixed feelings on this one. It has some moments that were sweet. The acting was great. I've actually seen this before and remembered liking it quite a bit. But this time, I struggled a bit. Largely because I never actually really liked Chris Gardner. Everything he was doing felt really selfish. He demanded his kid stay with him even though he knows he has no way to support his kid. And as a result him and his kid have to really struggle. And it's kind of all his fault. He has another option by allowing the kid to go with his mom to New York. So the movie just made me feel frustrated and kind of pissed off at Chris that he couldn't put his own ego aside to just do what's best for his kid. Now it didn't really make sense to me that the mom didn't fight harder. I just felt like I was missing part of the story. Turns out I was and quite a bit. In the true story, Chris cheated on his wife and got his mistress pregnant. She tried to take their son but he kind of assaulted her and was arrested for that. She does end to taking their kid to New York deciding not to press charges and then eventually ends to taking the kid back after a few months to live with his dad. Then after he becomes a broker he arranged for the kid to stay with her due to his long work hours. This feels like important info to leave out. Finding this out, it just feels like the movie wasn't honest with me. And I find that to be kind of gross to be honest. If I were to treat this as a fictional story, I might feel a bit different. Still didn't like Chris Gardner, but I at least would respect that he was at least able to eventually future things out. And that itself can be a inspirational story. So the story isn't a bad one. But I am mixed on the message. In the ending, while Will Smith is narrating, he says this moment of my life is called happiness. And I don't know how I feel about that. Because having a successful career is not equivalent to happiness. Happiness can be found without success in your career. I do get that if you have no money or resources at all, and your basic human needs aren't being met, it is going to be hard to actually be happy. But having a lot of money isn't really what makes one happy. And it just feels like this movie unintentionally sends the message that to be happy you need to find success in your career, and I don't really think that's true. Anyway, the movie isn't bad exactly. It has it's good elements. But I certainly do have many issues with the movie. Enough where I don't think I would call the movie good. 5/10

texto: A Classic American Dream Movie, But A Tone Deaf Film First I want to say I actually don’t dislike this film. I thought it was a good fun watch that was obviously made with lots of care and good intentions. The low lows we experience with Chris are trully devastating making it feel like your really there struggling alongside him. The amount of time and care the producers put into Chris’s personality and life make you really feel for him and see that he doesn’t deserve to be in this terrible situation. It has everything you would want in an American Dream™️ Movie. The zero to hero story, idealizing capitalism, and the ultimate message of work hard and you can achieve anything. But that’s not true. And this brings me to my main problem with this film. The Ideal (Fake) America Chris, the rest of his family and all the other characters, live in an ideal America free of racial or class bias that does not exist and has Never existed. This film focuses on the struggle of the working class black man in 1980s America but forgets about the fact he is working class and more importantly black. You really expect the audience to believe that in 1981 a rich millionaire CEO is inviting a black middle class intern with him to a football game in his private box because he just knocked on his door. Chris faces no sort of pressure or discrimination in this regard. Changing his race would have zero impact on the story. It seems Chris himself doesn’t even know he’s black. He is constantly quoting Thomas Jefferson a known racist and proud slave owner, and watching Ronald Reagan on the tv (No idea what that scene added). The film also glamorizes Chris bringing his son with him into homeless because he’s “In the pursuit of happiness” and it’s all gonna work out. While simultaneously shaming his wife for wanting to take her son away to a better place Final Notes It’s still a good movie overall aside from all these complaints. Will smith did a great job as Chris and Jayden was phenomenal. To think he was only around 7 years old when this was filmed is insane.

texto: Film del 2006, diretto da Gabriele Muccino. Chris Gardner viene lasciato dalla moglie e si ritrova ad affrontare enormi problemi economici, dovendo al tempo stesso prendersi cura del figlio piccolo Christopher. Questo film drammatico mi colpisce sempre molto personalmente. Nonostante presenti qualche limite dal punto di vista tecnico, la sceneggiatura, ispirata a eventi realmente accaduti, riesce sempre a coinvolgermi emotivamente. Narra la storia di un uomo che ha scommesso sull’investimento sbagliato e che si ritrova a dover far fronte a una serie di disavventure che si intrecciano con gravi problemi economici. Dallo sfratto all’abbandono da parte della moglie, passando per lo scarso profitto dei macchinari che cerca invano di vendere, Chris arriva a decidere di cambiare vita, trovando il coraggio e l’ambizione di intraprendere una nuova strada: uno stage non retribuito come broker. È commovente la dedizione, la passione e la resilienza di Chris, il quale, nonostante i numerosi problemi, continua imperterrito sulla propria strada, cercando di barcamenarsi tra il lavoro come venditore, la gestione del figlio e l’impegno dello stage, che prevede ore di studio ma anche l’acquisizione di nuovi clienti. Questo film ci ricorda quanto, anche nei momenti più bui, spesso ci si possa aggrappare a qualcosa, cercando di cambiare l’ordine degli addendi e, di conseguenza, il risultato della propria vita. Il coraggio di Chris, la sua abnegazione conciliata all’ambizione, hanno come propulsore principale la sofferenza, la povertà e l’incapacità di dare al proprio figlio ciò che desidera. E forse questo film, ripeto, nonostante presenti qualche pecca tecnica, mi colpisce sempre nel profondo, probabilmente proprio per le tematiche affrontate, che coincidono con un particolare periodo della mia vita. Questo lungometraggio, per quanto mi riguarda, è terapeutico: un film che, a ogni visione mi migliora l’umore e mi fa credere un po’ di più in me stesso. Per quanto concerne il comparto tecnico, la regia di Muccino prevede un utilizzo della macchina a mano che reputo disordinato e poco pulito. L’angolazione con cui viene posta la macchina da presa in alcune scene non mi convince, così come non mi convince appieno il blocking degli attori, in particolar modo nelle scene domestiche o in quelle racchiuse entro quattro mura. Risultano invece più azzeccate le scene all’aperto, ambientate in una New York movimentata, con Chris che inizialmente sembra andare quasi sempre nel verso opposto rispetto alla folla. Il film, invece, si conclude con un Chris perfettamente integrato in quella stessa folla, mentre cammina sui marciapiedi di New York. Gradisco questa rappresentazione di una New York frenetica e caotica. La macchina da presa si concentra spesso sulle lunghe file nei dormitori della Caritas, fotografando una parte della popolazione in difficoltà. Apprezzo l’intenzione di Muccino di mostrare anche questo volto della città, lontano dall’immagine patinata e idealizzata di New York. Will Smith è ottimo e riesce a essere estremamente coinvolgente dal punto di vista emotivo. Ottima anche la performance del giovane Jaden Smith. Voto: 8

tema: Falta de desenvolvimento emocional e críticas ao sistema
exemplo: Há críticas medianas apontando que o filme não desenvolve profundamente os personagens, especialmente em relação às consequências emocionais da pobreza e à crítica ao sistema capitalista, que é considerado superficial e apoiador de uma visão de mundo individualista.
texto: A melancholic watch, focusing on a beautiful father-son relationship, The Pursuit of Happyness goes onto show just how much money controls the quality of our lives. While Christopher’s character can be admired for his perseverance, grit, determination and for being a lovely father, the film glorifies the idea of “pulling yourself up from your bootstraps..” The film understands and in turn, portrays the phenomenology of poverty, struggle and sorrow without holding back. But what it fails to do is critique a system that is radically capitalistic, feeds upon ‘productivity culture’ and normalises kissing the ass of rich men just so you can ‘climb up the ladder.’ Success stories, like Christopher’s, will always be loved; they are inspiring. But one person’s success does not serve to acquit a system that constantly and deliberately keeps people on the brink of collapse and poverty.

texto: Pull Yourself Up by Your Bootstraps: The Movie I get why people like, or even love this movie. It’s well made for the most part, and it boasts career best performances from both Will and Jaden Smith (not that that’s saying much in Jaden’s case, but I digress). But man, this is just straight up capitalist propaganda wrapped up in a feel good package. The movie unironically depicts Thomas Jefferson and Ronald fucking Reagan as inspirational figures! The message of this movie is essentially that you can work yourself out of poverty by working hard enough and being treated poorly by rich white guys. I understand that this is based on a true story, and that Chris Gardner actually did manage to work hard enough to get out of the dumps, but this movie isn’t interested in engaging with the class system that it relies on to get dramatic moments out of. On the contrary, it has the opposite of class consciousness in a way that hasn’t aged well in the slightest post-2008 financial crisis. I don’t hate this movie, but I hate its message and thematic content. It’s almost offensive to me, and it certainly insults my intelligence.

texto: I have a lot of mixed feelings on this one. It has some moments that were sweet. The acting was great. I've actually seen this before and remembered liking it quite a bit. But this time, I struggled a bit. Largely because I never actually really liked Chris Gardner. Everything he was doing felt really selfish. He demanded his kid stay with him even though he knows he has no way to support his kid. And as a result him and his kid have to really struggle. And it's kind of all his fault. He has another option by allowing the kid to go with his mom to New York. So the movie just made me feel frustrated and kind of pissed off at Chris that he couldn't put his own ego aside to just do what's best for his kid. Now it didn't really make sense to me that the mom didn't fight harder. I just felt like I was missing part of the story. Turns out I was and quite a bit. In the true story, Chris cheated on his wife and got his mistress pregnant. She tried to take their son but he kind of assaulted her and was arrested for that. She does end to taking their kid to New York deciding not to press charges and then eventually ends to taking the kid back after a few months to live with his dad. Then after he becomes a broker he arranged for the kid to stay with her due to his long work hours. This feels like important info to leave out. Finding this out, it just feels like the movie wasn't honest with me. And I find that to be kind of gross to be honest. If I were to treat this as a fictional story, I might feel a bit different. Still didn't like Chris Gardner, but I at least would respect that he was at least able to eventually future things out. And that itself can be a inspirational story. So the story isn't a bad one. But I am mixed on the message. In the ending, while Will Smith is narrating, he says this moment of my life is called happiness. And I don't know how I feel about that. Because having a successful career is not equivalent to happiness. Happiness can be found without success in your career. I do get that if you have no money or resources at all, and your basic human needs aren't being met, it is going to be hard to actually be happy. But having a lot of money isn't really what makes one happy. And it just feels like this movie unintentionally sends the message that to be happy you need to find success in your career, and I don't really think that's true. Anyway, the movie isn't bad exactly. It has it's good elements. But I certainly do have many issues with the movie. Enough where I don't think I would call the movie good. 5/10

texto: The Pursuit of Happyness ist der American Dream Film schlechthin. Man muss nur alles geben, hart arbeiten und daran glauben, dann wird der Erfolg schon kommen. Nun, natürlich ist da etwas dran, egal, wie man ansonsten zu diesem Denken steht. Das Problem dieses Films liegt für mich nicht in der Geschichte, die er erzählt, denn die ist nett gemeint und zusätzlich mit toller Musik unterlegt. Doch es wird vorausgesetzt, dass wir diesen Erfolg selbst miterleben. Dass wir am Ende mindestens so aufgeregt sind wie Chris, ob er den Job nun bekommt oder nicht. Es muss das Publikum emotional mitreißen. Und hier komme ich zu meinem Hauptproblem des Films: Das schafft er einfach nicht. Jedenfalls nicht bei mir. Aber man möge mir die Möglichkeit geben, mich zu erklären. Uns werden mehrere Situationen geschildert, die Chris immer wieder den Boden unter den Füßen wegziehen. Die Ehefrau verlässt ihren Mann und ihr Kind. Die Gläubiger stehen förmlich vor der Tür. Man verliert die Wohnung. Alles Situationen, in die man nicht gelangen möchte, da sie potenziell die eigene Existenz, beziehungsweise die der Familie bedrohen. Und während uns all das geschildert und gezeigt wird, geht The Pursuit of Happyness auf die wichtigsten Fragen, die sich aus dieser Konsequenz ergeben, nicht ein. Denn, was macht all das mit den Menschen? Was macht es mit einem, ständig unsicher zu sein, was als Nächstes passiert? Und wie reagiert man darauf? Diese Fragen ergeben sich gezwungenermaßen aus der Handlung. Doch darüber erfährt man kaum etwas. Dafür sind die Dialoge/ das Drehbuch insgesamt zu oberflächlich. Es werden hier und da schöne Worte gefunden, um die Botschaft des Films zu formulieren(was in den Szenen auch sinnvoll ist, nicht nur Exposition, was der Film aussagen möchte). Aber das Innere der Charaktere wird so gut wie gar nicht beleuchtet. Dadurch verliert der Film enorm viel an Gewicht, weil die emotionalen Szenen dann natürlich nicht so stark wirken können, wie sie sollten. Hinzu kommt, dass The Pursuit of Happyness quasi durchgängig optimistisch ist. Was ich auch per se nicht schlecht finde, allerdings war es dem Film in diesem Fall meiner Ansicht nach nicht zuträglich. Das passiert hauptsächlich durch die Musik und Kamera, die beide wirklich gut sind, aber ich hätte mir gewünscht, manchmal auch etwas kälter in der Inszenierung zu sein, da man dadurch eher Mitgefühl erzeugt hätte. Somit ist tolle Kameraarbeit, tolle Musik, gutes Schauspiel und eine eigentlich motivierende Botschaft in einem zu oberflächlichen Film gefangen und kann seine Wirkung nicht so wirklich entfalten.

texto: What in the "pull yourself up by your bootstraps", American capitalism bullshit is this? Early on - the film pans across a clip of Reagan talking on the TV, and it took me until about the end of the movie to realise it was not doing so ironically. I was expecting some third act twist Chris realises that being a stock broker isn't the realisation of the American Dream, nor worth risking your family's wellbeing for. But as it turns out - it is! I normally wouldn't come down so hard on a film for its political messaging but I was honestly left gobsmacked. Feels very "pre-GFC". Somehow its made all the worse but the film itself being really great in many ways. Smith is obviously charismatic as fuck, and its a rare joy to be able to watch a genuine father and son on screen. Their most desparate moments are truly heartbreaking.

texto: The Pursuit of Happyness ~ Gabriele Muccino (SPOILERS) This film is bursting with Neo-liberalism - it’s a less insidious version of Forest Gump on steroids. The Pursuit of Happyness is a pile of overly-sentimental nonsense. Muccino presents nearly two hours of vile “American Dream” propaganda - where any problem can be overcome if you simply work hard enough and get wealthy. Muccino uses this singular outlier case to support Neo-liberal ideology. However, Muccino completely disregards the systemic issues that make this impossible. A system that necessitates poverty, unemployment, poor education, lack of social programs - capitalism. These issues are essentially entirely disregarded. Fuck this conservative Neo-liberal dogshit film Revolting.

texto: A feel-good story about extraordinary effort finally paying off, but it never feels too sentimental or sugarcoated. The protagonist has some natural talent to begin with, and he also makes some fairly self-centered choices in his pursuit of success, which gives the story a welcome sense of realism. As you’d expect from a story based on real events. At the same time, the film also reflects the reality of a society that has no adequate system in place to help people who are homeless. In that sense, I felt a kind of paradoxical criticism of a society where the pursuit of happiness is so difficult without an exceptionally strong will to survive.

exemplo: Reviews deste grupo apontam que o filme não atinge o nível de humor e inteligência das primeiras temporadas da série, e que soa mais como um episódio estendido que um filme.
texto: Just like The Simpsons, this review series has been running too long. I LOVE The Simpsons. The show has really shaped humor and culture for hundreds and hundreds of people. The show’s peak was from seasons 2-8, from 1991 to 1997. So, dear reader, you might be asking along with me: why the hell did they wait until 2007, far past when people had been saying the show had been running too long, to make The Simpsons Movie? Who the hell knows, but it really is a detriment. While the think the film definitely has its very funny moments, it lacks a lot of the intelligence, both in the humor and emotion, that the show had. The film feels like a long version of a Simpsons episode, which really doesn’t work. I think that even if you’ve never written anything in your life, the structure of a 22 minute episode is far different from the structure of a 90 minute movie. I think a lot of movies based off shows have that issue, such as The South Park Movie, but that film worked much better for a few reasons. 1. The humor in The South Park Movie was consistently gutbustingly hilarious, whereas in The Simpsons Movies, while there aren’t any stinker jokes, the majority of them are just ok. There aren’t a lot of jokes I’ll be quoting over and over all watching it. 2. The South Park movie actually plays out like a film, the story is coherent, emotional beats pay off, running jokes resolve, and you feel like you actually watched something of cinematic scale. The Simpsons movie feels a lot looser, like a TV episode, but that means that plot lines don’t make sense, or don’t resolve, the emotional bits don’t really work out, and it overall feels less cinematic. 3. The South Park Movie did something above and beyond the show. The film had a massive scale, a lot of the animation was upped, and there were a bunch of over the top Broadway style musical numbers, stuff you wouldn’t see on a typical South Park episode. The Simpsons Movie feels like an episode of The Simpsons, even down to the animation. There is very little to distinguish the film from an episode. Homer’s opening joke of “why do we pay to watch something we get on TV for free” really feels indicative of the film’s quality. Overall, not really a bad film, but not really a must watch. Definitely only recommend it for hardcore fans.

texto: Just like The Simpsons, this review series has been running too long. I LOVE The Simpsons. The show has really shaped humor and culture for hundreds and hundreds of people. The show’s peak was from seasons 2-8, from 1991 to 1997. So, dear reader, you might be asking along with me: why the hell did they wait until 2007, far past when people had been saying the show had been running too long, to make The Simpsons Movie? Who the hell knows, but it really is a detriment. While the think the film definitely has its very funny moments, it lacks a lot of the intelligence, both in the humor and emotion, that the show had. The film feels like a long version of a Simpsons episode, which really doesn’t work. I think that even if you’ve never written anything in your life, the structure of a 22 minute episode is far different from the structure of a 90 minute movie. I think a lot of movies based off shows have that issue, such as The South Park Movie, but that film worked much better for a few reasons. 1. The humor in The South Park Movie was consistently gutbustingly hilarious, whereas in The Simpsons Movies, while there aren’t any stinker jokes, the majority of them are just ok. There aren’t a lot of jokes I’ll be quoting over and over all watching it. 2. The South Park movie actually plays out like a film, the story is coherent, emotional beats pay off, running jokes resolve, and you feel like you actually watched something of cinematic scale. The Simpsons movie feels a lot looser, like a TV episode, but that means that plot lines don’t make sense, or don’t resolve, the emotional bits don’t really work out, and it overall feels less cinematic. 3. The South Park Movie did something above and beyond the show. The film had a massive scale, a lot of the animation was upped, and there were a bunch of over the top Broadway style musical numbers, stuff you wouldn’t see on a typical South Park episode. The Simpsons Movie feels like an episode of The Simpsons, even down to the animation. There is very little to distinguish the film from an episode. Homer’s opening joke of “why do we pay to watch something we get on TV for free” really feels indicative of the film’s quality. Overall, not really a bad film, but not really a must watch. Definitely only recommend it for hardcore fans.

texto: Uma experiência cinematográfica muito inteligente e autoconsciente. Os Simpsons definitivamente já tiveram dias melhores, e isso não é nenhuma novidade, mas é impossível não sorrir ao ver esses personagens de volta às telonas. O roteiro começa muito bem, com uma premissa inteligente e várias ideias genuinamente engraçadas. O problema é que, em algum ponto perto da metade, parece que eles se esqueceram completamente da própria premissa e o filme começa a se perder. Mesmo assim, é difícil não se divertir. E talvez a falta de ambição seja justamente uma das coisas mais admiráveis sobre a série. Os Simpsons não precisam reinventar a roda. Continua sendo grosseira, ácida, estúpida e estranhamente cativante na medida certa. Realmente não precisamos de muito mais. Uma das melhores piadas acontece quando os religiosos percebem que o fim do mundo chegou e que não foram salvos. Em completo desespero, eles correm para o bar em busca de uma bebida, enquanto as pessoas que já estavam no bar correm para a igreja em busca de salvação. É uma inversão tão simples, absurda e brilhantemente cínica, o tipo de piada que eles fazem parecer fácil. Eu ri muito disso. Desde o primeiro fotograma, este é Os Simpsons em sua essência. Não há nenhuma tentativa de tornar a série maior, mais profunda ou mais importante do que realmente é. É simplesmente uma boa e velha visita a Springfield, agora em uma tela muito maior. Talvez não seja um retorno à era de ouro, nem de longe, mas depois de todos esses anos, passar algumas horas com esses velhos amigos ainda é melhor do que assistir a mais uma reprise.
